Overall, our results show that augmenting low-rank factorization with learnable non-linear projections effectively mitigates the limitations of linear bottlenecks, yielding more faithful compressed embeddings under fixed dimensionality and suggesting a promising direction for embedding layer compression beyond purely linear methods.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds via Vector-Valued $L_p$ Correlation $V_α$
papers.abstract: Understanding generalization of randomized learning algorithms remains a central challenge. Mutual-information and total-variation bounds provide complementary ways to quantify data--hypothesis dependence, but they can behave quite differently in high-dimensional regimes. We study a one-parameter family of dependence measures, the vector-valued $L_p$-norm correlation $V_α$, and derive generalization bounds whose dependence terms interpolate between total variation (TV) at $α=1$ and variance and $χ^2$ related behavior at $α=2$. For $α>2$, the Hölder-conjugate loss moment is below two, yielding heavy-tailed specializations that can remain finite even when the loss variance is infinite. A particularly interpretable specialization occurs at $α=2$, where the bound can be expressed in terms of the variability of the algorithm's output density across datasets, $\int \sqrt{\mathrm{Var}_S[p(w\mid S)]}~ dw$. We show that the entire $V_α$ family is invariant under smooth bijective reparameterizations of the hypothesis space. We also introduce an adaptive density stability (ADS) condition that implies explicit control of $V_2$, and we verify it for Gibbs-type posteriors under bounded losses (yielding rates that depend on the inverse temperature and sample size). To address scaling, we extend the framework to a conditional formulation using supersamples, analogous in spirit to conditional mutual information (CMI), and discuss evaluations in the output space as a practical surrogate for estimating dependence. Simulations on Bayesian linear regression illustrate how tuning $α$ can change the tightness of the resulting bounds across regimes. Additional supersample experiments on noisy MNIST and on a pretrained ResNet-50 for CIFAR-10 show similar behavior of the projected loss-space bounds beyond the original clean-MNIST setting.

papers.title: BIRD-RL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning over Stateful Data-Centric Environments
papers.abstract: While agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training small language models (SLMs), existing frameworks are predominantly tool-centric and struggle with data-centric environments. Specifically, applying tool-centric frameworks to stateful tasks like SQL debugging introduces severe spatial inefficiencies since proper environment isolation typically requires a separate database container per rollout. Naively reusing databases without tracking evolving states across multi-turn interactions causes trajectory contamination and cross-trajectory interference, which severely destabilizes policy updates. To overcome these bottlenecks, we introduce BIRD-RL, a novel four-stage agentic RL curriculum that alternately enhances foundational agent reasoning and trajectory-adaptive on-policy exploration to circumvent the instability inherently associated with direct end-to-end learning. Crucially, to support this curriculum, BIRD-RL is driven by a Trajectory-scoped Persistent Execution Infrastructure, which enables safe database replica reuse while preserving trajectory isolation. This design improves spatial RL efficiency by 12.8x, successfully enabling scalable agentic RL for complex data-centric tasks without needs of Kubernettes. Empirical evaluations on the BIRD-CRITIC-SQLite benchmark demonstrate that our 7B and 14B models achieve Success Rates of 44.40% and 48.00%, respectively, showing competitive performance against strong proprietary model-based agents such as Claude-Opus-4.6 Agent (48.20%). Furthermore, BIRD-RL successfully trains unified SLMs capable of both advanced SQL debugging and generation, highlighting its broader potential for multi-objective optimization across heterogeneous, real-world data-centric tasks.

papers.title: One Act, Many Masks: Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) have substantially improved the performance of LLM agents on complex, long-horizon interactive tasks. However, despite progress in fine-grained credit assignment, policy optimization still applies these learning signals through response-specific probability ratios. Different textual responses can induce the same executable effect, yet credit differences arising from subsequent outcomes remain tied to their individual textual realizations. We identify this mismatch as credit-update misalignment. Our analysis reveals that credit-text pairing directly shapes policy-update directions, even when the policy context and executable effect are held fixed. Motivated by this finding, we propose Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization (EMPO), which aligns policy optimization with execution-level equivalence through an effect-level surrogate that couples updates across alternative textual realizations. EMPO preserves the original credit signals, integrates with both trajectory-level and step-level credit estimators, and requires no additional critics or rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Sokoban show that EMPO outperforms strong baselines in both task performance and learning efficiency.

papers.title: VIRA-Bench: Diagnosing Pedagogical Contingency Understanding in Online Tutoring Videos
papers.abstract: Understanding a one-to-one tutoring video requires more than recognizing its events. A model must connect a visible teacher intervention to the learner response it elicits and to the follow-up adjusted to that response. Existing video and educational-dialogue benchmarks typically emphasize event recognition, temporal reasoning, social-state inference, or transcript-based interaction, but rarely diagnose this action-response-adjustment relation. We introduce VIRA-Bench, a focused diagnostic benchmark for short-horizon pedagogical contingency in one-to-one online tutoring. VIRA-Bench contains 1,005 tutoring clips and 1,322 multiple-choice questions with researcher evidence audit and expert verification, organized into Observable Evidence Grounding (OEG), Interaction Contingency Reasoning (ICR), and Support-Response Modeling (SRM). Across 11 models, the best reaches 61.3%, well below the 91.0% human reference on a stratified subset, and ICR generally has the lowest layer accuracy among leading models. Under controlled input manipulations, removing video most strongly degrades OEG, whereas disrupting temporal order most strongly degrades ICR. Free-response, Stem+Options, and synchronized-shuffle controls show that response format, static question cues, and video-ASR mismatch do not explain these layer-specific patterns. The results identify distinct behavioral evidence dependencies without claiming an internal architectural mechanism. VIRA-Bench provides a focused evaluation resource for multimodal dialogue grounding, pedagogical discourse, and temporal reasoning in online tutoring.

papers.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>19683$, we settle the Cheng--Murray deep-hole problem for full-length Reed--Solomon codes in every dimension $2\le k\le q-2$, with the characteristic-two cases stated explicitly. For odd $q$, the deep holes are precisely the words of degree $k$. For even $q$ and $k\ge3$, the same conclusion holds except for an additional family when $k=q-3$. In even characteristic and dimension two, every deep hole has a unique expression $a h(X)+bX+c$, where $a\ne0$ and $h$ is a normalized $o$-polynomial. The proof combines quadratic quotient algebras, graph-theoretic weighted independent-set inequalities, and planar arc completion. We also obtain normal rational curve rigidity in the corresponding nonexceptional dimensions, the projective Reed--Solomon covering radii, and distinct-coordinate solvability and remainder criteria.

papers.title: MERP: A Latent-Bottleneck Framework for Robust Multi-Modal Multi-Label Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal multi-label emotion recognition is important for affect-aware systems, but models trained with complete text, visual, and acoustic streams often degrade sharply when some streams are unavailable at deployment. We address this train-test gap by learning a compact representation that preserves emotion-specific evidence from any available subset of modalities. We propose the Multi-modal Emotion Recognition Perceiver (MERP), which maps the joint sequence into a fixed-size latent bank, thereby keeping repeated reasoning independent of raw input length; it extracts label-specific evidence before and after latent reasoning and aligns the two levels through reconstruction. MERP further uses positive and negative class prototypes, a noise-gated feature enhancer with frequency-shaped perturbations during training, and confidence-aware class-wise fusion to strengthen separability, reduce sensitivity to missing inputs, and combine complementary predictors. Under 20 percent test-time random modality drop, MERP achieves micro-F1 scores of 0.563 on CMU-MOSEI and 0.780 on M3ED, exceeding the strongest evaluated baselines by 0.004 and 0.005, respectively; in the severe CMU-MOSEI audio-only setting, it retains 0.473 micro-F1 versus 0.022 for LDDU. These results show that fixed latent reasoning provides a practical, testable route to robust multimodal emotion recognition without requiring missing-modality examples during training. Code is available at https://github.com/Creative-zcx/MERP.

papers.title: Look Beyond the Question: Preserve-Focus-Fuse for Whole-Slide Image Question Answering
papers.abstract: A question about a whole-slide image rarely names every morphological finding needed to answer it. Question-guided patch selection can therefore overlook supporting morphology, while slide-level compression can dilute focal evidence. Inspired by how pathologists combine broad slide review, question-directed examination, and integration of their findings, we introduce BEYONDPATH, a Preserve-Focus-Fuse framework for whole-slide image question answering. Preserve learns a question-agnostic Morphology Bank through answer supervision across multiple questions about each training slide. Focus retrieves questionspecific evidence from all foreground patches, including regions outside the Bank. Fuse integrates the preserved morphology at the retrieved evidence positions through Morphology-on-Visual-Evidence Fusion, producing a fixed 96-token visual prefix. On WSI-Bench, BEYONDPATH achieves an Avg-9 of 0.769 and leads all eight reported report-generation metrics using the same checkpoint. It also achieves 0.639 zero-shot overall accuracy on SlideBench-BCNB. Controlled ablations show complementary benefits from morphology preservation and question-directed retrieval, and support cross-question supervision and fusion at the evidence positions. These results support looking beyond the question's explicit cues: preserving broader slide morphology while retaining the ability to seek evidence for each question.

papers.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People
papers.abstract: Visual grounding (VG) in visual question answering (VQA) is a fundamental capability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enabling the detection of the most relevant region in an image to answer the question. This reflects the model's capability of multimodal comprehension, which is crucial when interacting with visually impaired people (VIP). Indeed, visual grounding, when applied to assistive scenarios, is not merely a technical feature, but rather a trust and safety requirement. In this work, we study visual grounding in VLMs for visually impaired people. To this end, we assess open-source VLMs on visual grounding using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and challenge, which contains real-life images taken by VIP. We propose VG-SHAP, which extends an existing explainability framework to provide visual grounding explanations, allowing the evaluation of black-box VLMs. Our results on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding challenge show that despite generating correct answers, VLMs struggle to ground in the proper region in the image. However, these results are constrained by the quality of the segmentation model of our explainability framework and further research is necessary.

papers.title: PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration
papers.abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}

papers.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna based NOMA in specific output power regions.

papers.title: RubatoCodec: Budgeted Adaptive Speech Tokenization with Streaming Decoding
papers.abstract: Neural speech codecs provide discrete tokens for speech generation. Lower frame rates shorten token sequences, but each token must then carry more linguistic and acoustic information. Variable-frame-rate codecs address this trade-off by adapting token allocation to speech content, but threshold-based allocation lets content determine the token count, so the sequence length a speech generator must produce varies across utterances and datasets at a fixed setting. We present RubatoCodec, a variable-frame-rate speech codec built on X-Codec-2 with an exact utterance-level event budget and streaming decoding. Its Adaptive Firing mechanism uses changes in codec features and waveform spectra to divide speech into variable-duration events without a learned boundary predictor. Discrete codes and an explicit duration represent each event, allowing a speech generator to predict and decode one event at a time. Controlled experiments show that adaptive allocation outperforms fixed-rate coding in reconstruction fidelity and intelligibility at low event rates. A model trained on large-scale multilingual speech achieves competitive reconstruction quality across English, Japanese, and Mandarin, with the best intelligibility preservation among the compared codecs on the evaluated English and Japanese benchmarks at comparable bitrates. In a matched text-to-speech comparison, the adaptive representation yields lower WER and higher UTMOS and UTMOSv2 with comparable speaker similarity. The speech generator also learns the codec's utterance-level event budget without an explicit generation-time rate constraint. These results demonstrate that budgeted adaptive speech representations support both high-quality reconstruction and streaming text-to-speech generation. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/third-intelligence/RubatoCodec and https://huggingface.co/third-intelligence/RubatoCodec.

papers.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
papers.abstract: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. Across the 44 Atari-100k model--collection pairs that pass our reliability checks, including three released families, event patches outperform random patches in 39 (sign test p=1.4 x 10^{-7}), with a median gain of +44 percentage points. (2) The remaining error is structured: a complementary patch separates errors at true events from those elsewhere, while an eight-step timing tolerance recovers few events missed by our deterministic models. This structure also guides repair: a rule recorded before four repair outcomes were known predicts when a diffusion model repairs these failures. Event patches improve plan ranking, and the same concentration appears on control tasks with rare reward events.

papers.title: Searches for coincident Gravitational Waves and High-Energy Neutrinos from the KM3NeT and ANTARES telescopes during O3
papers.abstract: Various models predict that gravitational-wave sources produce high-energy neutrinos. Among them are compact binary coalescences with at least one neutron star, but also core-collapse supernovae or accretion disk instabilities. Two different analyses are presented, combining data from the LIGO and Virgo gravitational-wave detectors with those from the ANTARES and ORCA neutrino telescopes observed during the third observing run of LIGO-Virgo. In the first analysis, selected high-energy neutrino candidates were used as triggers to search for gravitational-wave candidates. In the second analysis, a search was conducted for potential spatial and temporal coincidences between subthreshold high-energy neutrino candidate events and subthreshold gravitational-wave candidates emitted by compact binary coalescence systems. In both searches, no significant coincidences were found. Upper limits on the rate of sources emitting both high-energy neutrinos and gravitational waves are presented. In particular, with the joint search, a joint source rate density upper limit of $8.8\times10^2~\mathrm{ Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ was found for a typical binary neutron star coalescence with a GW emitted energy of $10^{-1}~\rm M_\odot c^2$ and an isotropic energy emitted in neutrinos of $10^{51}~$erg.

papers.title: An end-to-end function for the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole
papers.abstract: We show that the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole can be written in closed form. The image plane is embedded as a plane tangent to a sphere centred on the black hole, and the map between a point source and its image point, which we call the photograph function, is treated as the analytic object. Explicit expressions are obtained for sources on the celestial sphere at infinity and for sources in the equatorial plane, without solving for the intermediate null geodesics. The construction is exact, and it makes the multivalued branch structure, the relation to the photon sphere and to the shadow boundary, and the self-similar higher-order images directly readable.

papers.title: A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Recently, multi-node inertial measurement unit (multi-IMU) systems have shown promise for robust odometry in legged robots. Multi-IMU fusion can improve legged robot odometry but requires accurate spatiotemporal calibration among the sensors. Existing multi-IMU calibration methods, designed for aerial or handheld platforms, face challenges on legged robots because routine locomotion may provide insufficient excitation, while foot slips, impacts, and vibrations introduce measurement disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose A2I-Calib++, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model. It estimates temporal offsets, extrinsic rotations and translations, and inertial biases through temporal correlation search followed by analytic spatial and bias estimation, without artificial calibration targets or complex parameter tuning for the target IMU. A2I-Calib++ comprises three core modules: 1) a Noise-Isotropy-Inspired Trajectory supported by a finite-horizon conditioning proposition that generates sufficient excitation to limit noise sensitivity; 2) a constraint-aware Adversarial Motion Priors controller that combines the anti-noise excitation with a rolling-contact reward for contact-aware execution; and 3) a contact-constrained virtual IMU that fuses pre-calibrated calf IMUs and joint kinematics under a rolling-contact model to construct the calibration reference. Furthermore, evaluations on both simulation and real-world quadruped platforms demonstrate notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.

papers.title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?
papers.abstract: Jet tagging is one of the most important applications of machine learning at the Large Hadron Collider. Recent models build in more physics knowledge or rely on large-scale pretraining, but the experiments place strict limits on their inference cost. Knowledge distillation can transfer their performance to small students that are cheap to run. We ask which properties of a teacher help the student, how small a student can get and how close it can come to the state of the art. On a jet tagging benchmark, we distil six teachers that differ in architecture, symmetry and pretraining, including two foundation models, into five small students. Every teacher improves every student, and the gain depends mainly on the strength of the teacher. We then shrink our two strongest distilled students, Transformer and L-GATr-slim, in width and in depth. With 20 thousand parameters, a distilled L-GATr-slim outperforms every published jet tagger trained from scratch at a fraction of the inference cost of every teacher. Even with two thousand parameters, it matches ParT, a model with a thousand times as many parameters. We also study what the students learn from their teachers. Our benchmark of inference cost shows that students of the same size can differ by almost an order of magnitude in speed. We release the code and the weights of all trained models.

papers.title: From hard-core to soft-core bosons in a shell trap
papers.abstract: We study the low-temperature states of a system of spinless bosons trapped in a broad spherical shell. In our virtual (path-integral Monte Carlo) experiments, we specifically examine how the equilibrium structure and overall superfluidity of the system are affected by a change of the interparticle-potential core from hard to increasingly soft. In this manner we bridge the gap between the behaviors of two species of bosons: Helium-like atoms, which self-assemble into ordinary crystalline solids, and Rydberg-dressed atoms, which in simulation form cluster (super)solids. We also vary the particle mass, i.e., the quantumness of the system, so as to modify the relative stability of ``solid'' and fluid states. We thus find a whole spectrum of (finite-size) phases with a curved structure, including multilayer and cluster phases, as well as superfluids and single layer supersolids. In particular, we confirm that supersolids only occur in the presence of clusters. By considering three system sizes (from 60 to 180 particles), but rescaling the trap radius so that the density stays fixed, we verify that supersolid states only exist in the same range of particle masses. Our model serves as a platform to test how emergent properties are modified, in spherical geometry, in the crossover from atoms to dressed atoms.

papers.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. In this work, we observe that sparsifying attention in different layers and at different denoising steps affects final-video fidelity to substantially different degrees. Yet the identities of the most sensitive layer-step pairs remain nearly unchanged across inputs. Building on these findings, we propose Allocating Layer-step Latency by Output Tests (ALLOT), a training-free sparsity allocation method. Treating each layer-step pair as a cell, ALLOT estimates each cell's contribution to final-video error through (i) cell probing and (ii) trajectory calibration, then jointly optimizes cell densities under a measured-latency budget. It preserves existing selection strategies and kernels, replacing only the allocation component. At equal or shorter wall-clock time, ALLOT outperforms every compared allocation strategy with XAttention, with an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo. Extensive experiments across four additional published pipelines on Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and HunyuanVideo show that ALLOT outperforms or ties the default in all nine settings.

papers.title: Beyond Shortcut Learning: Hierarchical Spatial Prototype Regularization for Face Forgery Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in generative models have enabled highly realistic face forgeries, yet generalizing deepfake detectors to unseen manipulation pipelines remains a major challenge. One critical yet underexplored issue is that the learned forensic representation itself may fail to remain stable across different manipulation sources. In this paper, we provide new evidence that naively fine-tuned vision models suffer from severe \textit{forensic representation collapse}: their extracted cues are often entangled with unstable, dataset-specific artifacts, resulting in structurally fragile representations and poor cross-domain generalization. Leveraging this insight, we propose \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{S}patial \textbf{P}rototype (\textbf{HSP}) regularization, which explicitly models the forgery manifold by learning a structured prototype subspace over spatial features. We further introduce prototype orthogonality and second-order assignment balance, which jointly preserve the geometric independence of latent forgery factors and promote high-effective-rank utilization of the forensic representation, thereby reducing reliance on dataset-specific shortcuts. Empirical results demonstrate that our method substantially improves generalizability, yielding average frame-level AUC gains of 5.6\% and 5.3\% in the cross-dataset and cross-manipulation settings, respectively. Moreover, when used as a plug-in module, HSP boosts the average video-level AUC of existing state-of-the-art detectors to 95.3\% (+1.8\%). These results demonstrate the practical value of HSP as an easy-to-adopt regularization module for enhancing deepfake detectors.

papers.title: DynaWeave: Learning to Adapt through Dynamic Scenario Synthesis
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use tools to complete tasks in stateful environments. However, many training environments remain largely static apart from changes caused by the agent's own actions, whereas external events introduced by other users, services, or sudden contingencies in real environments can invalidate ongoing plans. To address this gap, we introduce DynaWeave, an automated synthesis framework that transforms existing static tasks into verifiable dynamic scenarios. The framework generates exogenous events relevant to each task, covering changes in task requirements, environment state, and external information. It uses directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to represent dependencies between events and an execution engine to activate them during agent interaction. A dynamic verifier revises only the evaluation checks affected by events that actually occur and retains all other checks. Using DynaWeave, we collect 2,095 verified interaction trajectories across 36 environments and use them for supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5 models. Experiments on Gaia2, CostBench, and ToolMaze show that DynaWeave achieves consistent improvements in overall performance across all three evaluated model sizes, increasing the task completion rate on CostBench by 67.34 percentage points and even exceeding the performance of Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview on ToolMaze. These results support dynamic scenario synthesis as a practical approach to training agents to adapt to changing environments. Our code is available at https://github.com/Miaow-Lab/DynaWeave.

papers.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
papers.abstract: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

papers.title: Deciding Scale Placement in MXFP4 Dot Products with Integer Arithmetic
papers.abstract: The Open Compute Project's microscaling (MX) family includes MXFP4, which stores 32 four-bit elements with a shared power-of-two scale. When lowering a dot-product reduction, a compiler can apply these scales before the reduction, or defer scaling until afterwards. Although equivalent over real numbers, these formulations can produce different IEEE binary32 results through overflow or underflow, with equivalence also depending on the reduction tree. We study the legality of compiler rewrites in either direction by deriving conditions under which the two formulations are bitwise equivalent. To decide rewrite legality, we construct an integer state machine that exploits the finite element alphabet and shared power-of-two scales, modeling overflow, NaN, and subnormal rounding. We prove its faithfulness under bounded scale codes and integer coefficients, yielding an exact encoding of the equivalence query in quantifier-free linear integer arithmetic (QF_LIA). For MXFP4, we derive a closed-form sufficient upper bound on the sum of scale exponents for any fixed binary reduction tree within the supported coefficient range. This bound depends on the size of the largest proper subtree. For four tree shapes at block lengths $k\in\{2,3,4,8,16,32\}$ and two shapes at $k=64$, SMT finds counterexamples when this upper bound is increased by one exponent step. Against the standard direct encoding in quantifier-free floating-point arithmetic (QF_FP), on matched queries cvc5 proves the integer version in seconds but reaches a configured one-CPU-hour limit on the floating-point proof even at $k=2$. The implementation was cross-checked using an independent floating-point encoding, exhaustive and stratified binary32 execution, and GPU replay of counterexamples. An MLIR lowering prototype demonstrates selection between the two formulations using the certified conditions as static or runtime guards.

papers.title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
papers.abstract: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from inclined orbits around Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on generic inclined orbits provide a critical dynamical probe of strong field gravity, as they uniquely break the severe parameter degeneracies inherent to planar equatorial trajectories. To isolate the exact rotational signatures, we extend the periodic-orbit framework to three-dimensional inclined trajectories in the Kerr spacetime, specifically focusing on the $r$--$θ$ orbital resonances. By mapping the geodesic motion into a co-precessing spatial framework parameterized by Mino time, we compute the emitted quadrupole waveforms and evolve the local dynamics using circularity-preserving radiation reaction. It is demonstrated that frame-dragging induces a transient dynamical tilt at periastron, which directly splits the emitted radiation into an exact five-comb spectral architecture. When this resonant structure is resolved over a single coherence time, the statistical error on the dimensionless spin is reduced to $σ_a \approx 10^{-2}$, improving upon the equatorial baseline by up to two orders of magnitude. Because any bound orbit in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime generates a maximum of three frequency combs, the detection of this five-comb hierarchy establishes a rigorous, model-independent null test to strictly exclude spherical geometries.

papers.title: Room-temperature near-infrared optical readout of triplet spin states integrated in carbon nanotubes towards quantum sensing
papers.abstract: Optically addressable electron spin qubits that function at room temperature and under ambient conditions are essential for advancing quantum sensing. Solid state defect platforms offer robust spin-photon interfaces but lack precise defect positioning and electronic tunability. Molecular spin qubits enable bottom up chemical design yet suffer from limited photostability. Here, we introduce para-halophenyl (-Cl, -Br and -I) quantum defects in (6,5) single wall carbon nanotubes that trap triplet excitons with a spin-photon interface that is operable under ambient, room temperature conditions. These defects were shown to emit in the near infrared within the biological transparency window, and their placement on the nanotube surface provides nanoscale proximity to target environments. The deep optical traps formed by the defects yield exceptional photostability. Here, we demonstrate optical initialization and readout of these triplet states at room temperature, provide proof of principle sensing of paramagnetic molecules, and highlight potential for on chip detection. Together, these results establish SWCNT defects as a promising new platform for future quantum sensing.

papers.title: Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe2
papers.abstract: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

papers.title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
papers.abstract: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and étale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.

papers.title: Quantum Belief Characterization: A Multi-Shot Notion of Equivalence
papers.abstract: A recent formulation of quantum belief showed that quantum retrodiction depends not only on the reduced density operator of the system of interest, but also on correlations with a hidden reference system, which leads to the notion of quantum belief equivalence. In this paper we formulate a multi-shot problem, where the extended posterior obtained after one update is used again as the prior for the next update. We first define a formal notion of $n$-shot equivalence and derive several propositions for arbitrary extended beliefs. We then argue that the agent must also specify why the data obtained in different rounds concern the same underlying object. Through the quantum de Finetti representation, this narrows the one-copy belief to a special class: candidate-state ensemble belief. In that sector, we show that two beliefs are $n$-shot equivalent if and only if their $(n+1)$-th moments are equal. We also give a physical interpretation of this moment condition and illustrate it through the equivalence between Haar priors and projective-design priors at bounded update depth.

papers.title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
papers.abstract: Significant spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal history-dependent attenuation jointly govern wave propagation in composite materials, making full-scale direct numerical simulation (DNS) computationally prohibitive. This study proposed a high-order multi-scale (HOMS) method for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems with highly oscillatory and discontinuous material coefficients. Using a multi-scale asymptotic expansion approach, the macroscopic homogenized equation, and first- and second-order correction terms are derived to construct the high-accuracy HOMS solution. Moreover, a local pointwise error analysis identifies the leading residual eliminated by this HOMS solution and validates its local physical balance preservation. Then, a global energy-norm error estimate establishes the $O(\varepsilon)$-order convergence rate for the HOMS solution. Subsequently, an efficient spatiotemporal multi-scale algorithm integrating the finite element and finite difference methods is designed, which employs a novel fully discrete $L2\text{-}1_σ$-Newmark scheme, and corresponding unconditional shifted-energy stability and explicit convergence rates are also obtained for the macroscopic homogenized displacement and velocity, respectively. Both two- and three-dimensional examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness of the proposed HOMS method. This work provides an effective multi-scale tool for nonlocal-in-time wave simulation in engineering applications.

papers.title: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance
papers.abstract: Robust and reactive collision avoidance remains a central challenge for deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies on real robotic manipulators, particularly when transferring behaviours learned in simulation to the physical world. This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance. The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles. These results highlight the potential of EDF-based representations to mitigate the sim-to-real gap and support reliable and real-time collision-aware behaviour in complex and changing environments.

papers.title: Higher-order Angular Momentum Transport of Alteraxial Phonons in 2D Magnets
papers.abstract: The coupling between lattice vibrations and magnetic order in two-dimensional (2D) magnets gives rise to a variety of physical phenomena, among which magnetic effects of axial phonons carrying phonon angular momentum (PAM) have attracted considerable interest. However, a systematic classification of axial phonons in 2D magnets that covers their multipolar patterns and the resulting transport manifestations remains largely unexplored. Here, based on symmetry analysis, we classify all 2D magnetic point groups by their long-wavelength PAM wave patterns. Beyond the s-wave axial phonon, we identify alteraxial phonons with p-, d-, f-, g-, and i-wave multipolar textures, characterized by 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 zero-PAM nodal lines, respectively. We then develop a theory of nonlinear PAM transport driven by a temperature gradient and derive two selection rules: a parity selection rule that determines whether the response occurs at even or odd orders, and an angular-harmonic selection rule that fixes the lowest allowed order for each wave pattern. The multipolar PAM patterns and selection rules are exemplified by two effective lattice models realizing f-wave and d-wave PAM patterns, respectivley. The angular dependence of the nonlinear PAM current reflects the underlying multipolar PAM texture, offering a signature for experiments. Our results establish a symmetry-guided framework for detecting and utilizing higher-order PAM textures in 2D magnets.

papers.title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training
papers.abstract: Feed-forward visual geometry models, exemplified by VGGT, have demonstrated strong multi-view reconstruction capabilities through dense global attention. However, the resulting all-to-all cross-view computation scales quadratically with the number of input views, making long-sequence inference particularly expensive due to substantial frame-level redundancy among highly overlapping observations. We uncover a topology-first, geometry-later evolution in VGGT camera tokens: shallow-layer tokens reliably capture local view neighborhoods, whereas deeper-layer tokens progressively encode globally organized inter-view geometry. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for structure-aware frame-level key--value sparsification. At each global-attention block, BlazeVGGT constructs a view-level similarity kernel from camera-token relations and employs greedy determinantal point process inference to select a compact set of mutually complementary views. The selected views constitute the key--value context, while all input frames are retained as queries. This asymmetric attention design preserves dense per-frame predictions while eliminating redundant cross-view computation, allowing our method to be directly integrated into pretrained VGGT as a plug-and-play module without parameter updates. Its advantages become increasingly pronounced with sequence length: at 2,000 frames, BlazeVGGT achieves approximately 13$\times$ faster inference than VGGT while reducing the Chamfer Distance from 0.41 to 0.32. Extensive experiments demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off in point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation, compatibility with existing VGGT accelerators such as FastVGGT and LiteVGGT, and transferability to VGGT-based models including StreamVGGT and PAGE-4D. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/MagiciannnY/BlazeVGGT.git.

papers.title: Omnilingual-MsASR: Benchmarking Multimodal, Multilingual, Long-Form Multi-Speaker ASR of Omni Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Omni-modal large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in audio and video understanding. However, existing models struggle with long-form, multi-speaker videos, especially in understanding the entire video and recognizing who says what and when. To characterize the capability limit of current omni LLMs and guide future model development, we introduce Omnilingual-MsASR, a multilingual, multimodal benchmark for long-form Multi-speaker Automatic Speech Recognition (MsASR) covering six languages, recordings up to 30 minutes, and scenarios with up to 20 speakers. Omnilingual-MsASR provides parallel audio and video inputs to evaluate models' cross-modal consistency and their ability to exploit complementary cues across modalities. Extensive evaluations of leading omni-modal LLMs reveal substantial performance bottlenecks, while their tcpWERs frequently exceed 100%. These findings highlight fine-grained temporal localization, speaker disambiguation, and cross-modal synergy as key challenges for future omni-modal foundation models. Our work is available at https://github.com/QwenLM/Omnilingua-Bench/tree/main/Omnilingua-MSpeaker.

papers.title: RegoMender: A Multi-agent Framework for Automated Rego Policy Repair
papers.abstract: Policy-as-Code (PaC) has emerged as a foundational paradigm in cloud-native systems. However, repairing Rego policies remains challenging due to their strict syntax, declarative semantics, and specific verification requirements. Existing automated program repair (APR) methods are mainly designed for mainstream languages and struggle to accommodate the unique policy logic and repair workflows of Rego. Thus, Rego policy repair remains a manual process driven by trial and error. To address this, we introduce RegoBench, the first automated Rego policy benchmark comprising 1,159 real-world defects, and propose RegoMender, a feedback-guided multi-agent framework. Collaborating via a shared blackboard and an atomic toolkit, RegoMender dynamically executes patching, rewriting, or rolling back, to resolve complex repair scenarios. Evaluated on RegoBench, RegoMender achieves syntactic and test-based semantic success rates of 82.9\% and 77.9\%, respectively, outperforming the strongest baseline by 13.4\%. Unlike other approaches whose performance drops in complex scenarios, RegoMender maintains effectiveness across single-step and chained repair tasks. Furthermore, it generalizes strongly across HCL and SQL and achieves an 86.4\% repair rate on 132 real-world CVE vulnerabilities, proving its robustness and practical utility for security.

papers.title: Short qudit triorthogonal codes from doubling
papers.abstract: We construct short triorthogonal codes for qudits of odd prime dimension by generalizing doubling, which combines a triorthogonal code with a code admitting a transversal phase gate, and raises the distance by up to two. This gives codes with parameters $[[28,1,4]]_3$, $[[37,1,5]]_3$, $[[72,1,6]]_3$, $[[118,1,8]]_3$, $[[33,1,5]]_5$ and $[[20,1,4]]_7$, each shorter than the cyclic, concatenated and Reed-Muller codes of the same distance, and a doubling construction of the $[[15,1,3]]_3$ code. When the columns of a generator matrix are regarded as charged points, triorthogonality becomes the vanishing of multipole moments up to octupole order, and doubling becomes a double layer of opposite charges; this picture explains why inputs with nontrivial coefficients can give shorter codes. We also show by exhaustive search that the shortest codes of distance three have length $11$ for $p=5$ and length $7$ for $p=7$. Combined with high-rate distance-two codes, the new codes reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in regimes with high input noise.

papers.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. While recent efforts have explored harness diversification to reduce specialization to particular execution settings, how to systematically construct and organize harness diversity for cross-harness generalization remains insufficiently understood. This work studies Harness Scaling as a distinct scaling dimension for agentic RL, focusing on structured variation in how policies execute and interact with the same underlying task and environment. Concretely, we construct a factorized harness space, select a compact training subset with balanced factorial coverage, and organize cross-harness training through locality-aware task assignment. Across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and RL algorithms, Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen harness combinations. Moreover, policies trained through structured white-box harness variation transfer effectively to unseen external black-box harnesses, outperforming policies trained through a single complex black-box harness. These results establish harness diversity as a meaningful scaling dimension for agentic RL and highlight the importance of how this diversity is organized for cross-harness generalization.

papers.title: Radio and high-energy variable emission from a multi-wavelength follow-up of the infant planet-hosting star V1298 Tau
papers.abstract: V1298 Tau is a very young and magnetically active K1V star which hosts a benchmark multi-planetary system to study planet formation and evolutionary history at the earliest stages. Between 2025 and 2026, we conducted a campaign to monitor the variability of V1298 Tau in radio (band C), X-ray, and NUV bands, with the support of publicly available contemporary optical light curve, and to investigate multi-band correlations to link the emission with stellar activity. Radio observations were carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) in band C (4.5--6.5 GHz). X-ray and NUV observations were carried out with the Swift satellite over 20 days, ending one month before the begin of the radio campaign. We analysed the temporal variability of peak (integrated) fluxes in the C-band and of X-ray (NUV) luminosities on various timescales, comparing it with the variability observed in the high-cadence optical light curve collected by the ASAS-SN survey. We observed both radio and high-energy time variable emission. JVLA detected emission in 90\% of the visits, switching between high ($\geq$0.1 mJy/beam) and low flux states in matter of days or hours. The fluxes show moderate correlation with the optical light curve, suggesting modulation with the stellar rotation period. Except for one visit, dynamic spectral analysis does not reveal short-term (minutes) variability, nor is there any evidence of circularly polarised emissions. Overall, the radio observations can be explained as gyrosynchrotron and/or cyclotron emission from the corona, and linked to stellar magnetic activity. At high-energy, we detected significant variability in X-ray luminosity (within the range ~1.2--2.5x10$^{+30}$ erg/s), the decay phase of a stellar flare, and evidence of correlation with the optical flux. Our data confirm that V1298\,Tau follows the near-linear Güdel-Benz relation.

papers.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
papers.abstract: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves $1.45\times$ the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.

papers.title: Spin-Adapted Spin-Flip Tamm-Dancoff Approximation (XSF-TDA) for Singlet-Triplet Gaps in MR-TADF and INVEST Emitters
papers.abstract: In this work, we assess the recently introduced spin-adapted TDA for spin-flip-down excitations (XSF-TDA) [Mol. Phys. e2631735 (2026)] as a practical approach to this problem. Starting from a high-spin restricted open-shell Kohn--Sham reference, XSF-TDA generates spin-adapted low-spin roots arising from open--open (OO), core--open (CO), open--virtual (OV), and core--virtual (CV) types of spin-flip-down excitations. Across four application sets comprising 243 benchmark cases, XSF-TDA substantially reduces the systematic positive bias observed for TDA and unrestricted spin-flip TDA (USF-TDA). With the B3LYP functional, XSF-TDA reduces the equal-set-weighted macro-MAE relative to USF-TDA from 0.252 eV (0.158 eV) to 0.102~eV (0.056~eV) with the ALDA0 (multicollinear) kernel. Its accuracy is competitive with state-specific $Δ$DFT and quasiparticle-energy DFT (QE-DFT), while being able to provide deeper mechanistic insight through the response vector. In particular, spin-adapted CV configurations provide selected higher-excitation character that strengthens the OO--CV dynamical-spin-polarization channel, which preferentially stabilizes the singlet states. We also identify an INVEST emitter with appreciable OO--OV mixing, suggesting a possible additional contribution to singlet stabilization when the CV contribution is small. The XSF-TDA method therefore provides practical singlet--triplet gap predictions together with interpretable state analysis for the screening and mechanistic understanding of MR-TADF and INVEST emitters.

papers.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
papers.abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. Yet its twisting is concentrated in a short buffer segment, imposing most of the workload on the two twist joints in the middle, which can often overburden the motors and limit its locomotion. With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%. Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

papers.title: Local well-posedness, blow-up phenomenon and ill-posedness for a model system of the radiating gas
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem for a model system of radiating gas in multi-dimensional space. Firstly, we prove that the model is locally well-posed in Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $s>1+\frac{d}{p}$ (resp., $s=1+\frac{d}{p}$, $r=1$), including the endpoint space $B^1_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Secondly, we show that the data-to-solution map is not uniformly continuous on bounded subsets of these Besov spaces. Moreover, we construct a blow-up scenario and derive two sufficient blow-up conditions, which improve the previous blow-up condition obtained in \cite{MR3016436}. Finally, we prove that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the critical space $B^{1+\frac{d}{p}}_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $r>1$ in the sense of norm inflation.

papers.title: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
papers.abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. The resulting AMR ratio reaches -33% at 8 K and 10 T and exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence qualitatively captured by a minimal spin-disorder model. These results show that engineering the local environment of dilute magnetic ions provides a route to large paramagnetic AMR without long-range magnetic order, extending the materials design space for AMR beyond magnetically ordered systems.

papers.title: Directional Posterior Feedback Fusion for Query Reformulation in Dense Retrieval
papers.abstract: Dense retrieval has become a fundamental paradigm for modern information retrieval, supporting efficient semantic search across a wide range of applications. Its effectiveness, however, relies critically on query embeddings that adequately capture users' information needs, which can be difficult for short, ambiguous, or underspecified queries. Feedback-based query reformulation approaches like pseudo-relevance feedback (PRF) alleviate this by incorporating additional evidence from retrieved or generated content. However, existing embedding-space approaches commonly aggregate or interpolate feedback vectors, implicitly treating them as complete target representations. Such pointwise fusion can unnecessarily suppress query corrections along directions not expressed by individual feedback items, even when these directions are supported by complementary evidence. To address this limitation, we propose Directional Posterior Feedback Fusion (DIFF), a query reformulation framework that models feedback as directional evidence rather than target points. DIFF represents feedback as confidence-weighted directional evidence in the tangent space of the original query and jointly infers a controlled query update through prior-regularized posterior fusion, without retraining the underlying dense retriever. Experiments across multiple dense retrievers and different feedback sources show that DIFF achieves the best overall retrieval performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of explicitly modeling how feedback should constrain query updates.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Computation with Power Amplifier Nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) enables efficient wireless data aggregation by exploiting the superposition of signals transmitted by multiple source nodes, but its performance is sensitive to hardware impairments such as power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity. In this paper, we develop an analytical framework for coherent AirComp with PA nonlinearities and derive a closed-form expression for the receiver mean-squared error (MSE) under a memoryless polynomial PA model. Our numerical results show that power control optimized under the conventional linear-PA assumption can exhibit rapidly increasing MSE as the transmit power budget increases, whereas incorporating PA nonlinearity into the power control design prevents this degradation and maintains low MSE over the considered power range.

papers.title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. Specifically, we propose using a non-uniform sampling distribution constructed from the leverage scores of the two matrices, and characterize the associated approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm; which is well-known to better characterize the downstream error when the matrix product operator is applied to an input vector. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.

papers.title: PreCoMem: Predictive Cognitive Memory for Self-Evolving Long-Term Dialogue Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon dialogue agents need to keep user memories stable enough for personalization while adapting when the user genuinely changes. Existing memory systems often append every observation or overwrite old entries by heuristic rules, which makes transient noise hard to distinguish from real belief drift. We introduce PreCoMem, a memory consolidation framework inspired by predictive coding that represents memory as confidence-weighted beliefs about the user's state. Its core signal, Effective Surprisal, combines semantic deviation and contradiction evidence, then downweights this signal when retrieval is diffuse and unreliable. According to effective surprisal, a two-threshold gate maps each turn to one of three deterministic updates: MAINTAIN reinforces supported beliefs, PROFILE stores ambiguous cues as low-confidence hypotheses, and CORRECT softly decays reliably contradicted facts. The PROFILE stage acts as an explicit waiting room, preventing premature commitment to noisy evidence. Experiments on LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, and PersonaMem-v2 show consistent state-of-the-art accuracy; our new DiMoBench confirms that PreCoMem adapts to non-stationary belief drift without over-reacting to noise. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhongWishing/PreCoMem.

papers.title: General function bases moment models for suspended sediment with vertical profile of concentration
papers.abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. The formulation is constructed over arbitrary vertical functional bases that are numerically orthogonalised via the Gram-Schmidt algorithm. This approach allows the approximation spaces for the vertical profile to be adapted to the specific structure of each physical variable, where also the velocity and sediment concentration can be projected onto different functional spaces. To overcome the limitations due to the inherent oscillatory nature of global Legendre polynomials, we explore a specific continuous piecewise linear $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite-element basis. Furthermore, non-uniform vertical partitions are considered, enabling an enhanced representation of the vertical profiles in specific regions. Numerical experiments involving boundary layers and suspended sediment transport demonstrate that the proposed framework is accurate to reproduce the expected vertical profiles. The improvement is particularly significant for sediment concentration profiles with sharp vertical variations, where polynomial reconstructions exhibit pronounced oscillations leading to physically meaningless profiles, whereas the $\mathbb{P}_1$ bases produce a qualitatively accurate representation of the vertical profiles observed in the sedimentation processes.

papers.title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
papers.abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{á}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$. In this paper, we extend their result by showing that for every positive integer $k$, the $k$-apex of any tree or any forest with average degree at least one is common. Our proof involves an application of the entropy method.

papers.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of numbers of type $n = 2m^2$ below $X$ which cannot be written as a sum of two primes has cardinality at most $X^{19/24 + o(1)}$.

papers.title: Enhanced Langlands Parameters of Regular Principal Series
papers.abstract: We describe the enhanced Langlands parameters of the irreducible constituents of a regular principal series of a quasi-split reductive group over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Starting from the chamber parametrization by Rodier and Luo, we determine the monodromy of each constituent and show that its enhancement is trivial. In particular, we obtain the corresponding parameter of the unique irreducible subrepresentation.

papers.title: OmniSimulator: Aligning Small Language Models for Authentic Heterogeneous Behavior Modeling
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential as general-purpose user simulators for interactive systems. Prior studies have demonstrated that training on high-quality data can substantially improve model reasoning and downstream task performance. However, the upper bound of user simulation is still constrained by the model's reasoning paradigm: native chain-of-thought often degenerates into shallow pattern matching and fails to adequately model the behavioral factors underlying real user decisions. In this paper, we propose OmniSimulator, a novel training framework designed to improve the predictive ability of small LLMs for realistic user simulation on short-video platform environments. Specifically, OmniSimulator organizes behavior-oriented reasoning through a structured schema with five dimensions, carefully selects data from real user-behavior scenarios, and introduces a teacher model to generate high-quality reasoning traces under the proposed schema, helping small models learn behavior-relevant reasoning patterns rather than relying on superficial behavioral correlations. Based on this process, we construct 9,881 high-quality training instances from three months of historical interaction trajectories of 200 real users, averaging about 50 distilled examples per user. Experimental results show that OmniSimulator improves the average score of Qwen3-8B by 34.33%, achieves performance competitive with Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and supports smaller-scale, self-hosted deployment. These results suggest that learning structured behavior-oriented reasoning patterns is a promising direction towards scalable and high-fidelity LLM-based user simulation.

papers.title: Asymmetry Tunneling Beyond Adaptive Equivariance Relaxation
papers.abstract: Equivariant neural networks encode prescribed symmetries as powerful inductive biases, yet real-world data may exhibit symmetry-breaking structure that these priors cannot fully capture. Prior work has largely addressed this challenge through model-side equivariance relaxation, seeking an appropriate level of equivariance for the data. This raises a complementary question: must equivariance relaxation be adaptively controlled? To investigate this question, we introduce a residual path alongside a strictly equivariant model and deliberately restrict their interface to examine the transmission of task-relevant structure. Across five benchmarks, we observe both residual collapse and survival despite these restrictions; we call the latter phenomenon asymmetry tunneling. We further characterize this phenomenon through four complementary diagnostics. Our results suggest that adaptive control of equivariance relaxation is not a prerequisite for capturing potential symmetry-breaking structure.

papers.title: Extending Affordance Segmentation for Wearable Robots to Multi-Object Images
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a refinement to existing vision-based portable pipelines for the recognition of graspable object parts. Such pipelines can effectively support automatic grasp selection and preshaping in upper-limb prosthetic devices. However, realistic scenarios in which multiple objects are present still represent a challenge. The proposed method exploits a minor modification to the conventional hardware setup and a custom training approach to extend the applicability of vision-based pipelines. A laser pointer is introduced in the setup as an effective mechanism for object disambiguation. Accordingly, a suitable retraining of the deep convolutional neural networks supporting recognition of graspable parts is implemented. A mixed reality strategy allows the reuse of available high-quality segmentation masks to generate realistic images procedurally, extending the range of scenarios supported by the final device. Experimental results confirm that the proposed pipeline improves target disambiguation accuracy by up to 9% compared with existing solutions, while preserving the computational cost.

papers.title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows
papers.abstract: Low-NFE generative ODE sampling is constrained not only by solver order, but also by how a fixed budget of network evaluations is distributed along the flow. We develop a density-level backward-error framework that identifies the component of a solver's modified-equation defect that changes the evolving marginal, while excluding solenoidal trajectory distortion that is invisible in Wasserstein tangent geometry. The resulting residual induces a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and, through gauge freedom, an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity representatives of the same density path. This separates our approach from schedule search driven by trajectory or endpoint surrogates and from higher-order solver design. Exact Gaussian and mixture models establish the mechanism, including cases where curvature-based allocation fails and continuum-optimal transport is not discretization-optimal. On a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM probability-flow ODE, density-aware allocation consistently improves fixed-update Euler sampling in the low-NFE regime. Matched-seed convergence to a dense Euler reference confirms that the method accelerates approximation of the same high-NFE flow rather than changing the asymptotic sampler.

papers.title: Generative Modeling via Nonlinear Schrödinger Bridges and Branching Diffusions
papers.abstract: We propose a new generative modeling framework grounded in forward-backward partial differential equations (PDEs). These equations arise naturally in mean-field game (MFG) theory, and are closely related to nonlinear Schrödinger systems. Our main contribution is to reinterpret this connection within the setting of generative modeling and to develop an efficient numerical methodology for its practical implementation. Specifically, we derive and characterize a nonlinear extension of the classical Schrödinger bridge problem through a coupled system of PDEs, yielding a model we call SBNL (Schrödinger Bridge NonLinear). To compute its solution, we design a simulation algorithm based on branching diffusions and the probabilistic representation of semilinear PDEs. The resulting method is embarrassingly parallel, scalable to high dimensions, and applicable to a broad class of nonlinear interaction functionals. We validate the approach through numerical experiments, including recovery of the classical Schrödinger bridge, nonlinear extensions with convex penalties (Gross-Pitaevskii) as well as potential interaction terms, and high-dimensional generative tasks such as image synthesis on the MNIST and FFHQ human face dataset. Furthermore, the same framework embeds score-based generative modeling, diffusion models, and tractable gaussian Schrödinger bridges.

papers.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
papers.abstract: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge agreed with the adjudicated label at Gwet's AC1 of at least 0.894 on 1,860 elements. We evaluated fourteen model and reasoning-mode combinations on whether they produce the conflicting text, decline or warn. Eleven of the fourteen produce conflicting content on most such requests, mostly without a warning, and nearly three warnings in four accompany conflicting content. The models that conform more do so by declining while still serving the legitimate twin, and enabling reasoning halved the refusals of two models. We hope the dataset and pipeline will help evaluate how language models observe professional norms and let diagnostic datasets be built for particular professions and organisations.

papers.title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments
papers.abstract: Snake robots can traverse complex environments with limbless locomotion, but maneuvering in low-clearance environments remains challenging because a gait must maintain a small swept height while also providing planar steering. Existing rolling gaits preserve a low swept height body configuration but generally provide limited steering, whereas steering gaits often introduce vertical undulation and require additional clearance. With that in mind, this paper develops S-rolling, a steerable rolling gait that combines low swept height locomotion with planar maneuverability for twistable snake robots. S-rolling is designed using an S-shaped planar backbone curve, whose head and tail segments roll with independently controlled angular velocities, producing different motion modes. We derive its joint space gait equation, in which a central twist joint realizes the relative rotation between the two segments. We also develop a quasi-static kinematic model relating the segment rolling speeds to the linear and angular velocities of the robot.
