Monitor outputs are combined in a coordination layer and mapped by a communication layer to a traffic-light display. In this work, COMET consists of three monitoring layers: signal integrity, physics consistency, and the AI system's competence envelope. The framework is evaluated on an open dataset of compressed-air leaks, where an AI system detects leaks from acoustic emissions, with held-out conditions simulating covariate shift, semantic shift, and sensor faults, events expected during runtime but unknown in their exact appearance. All monitors are frozen after development and tested zero-shot, and the framework is compared against no-monitoring and single-monitor setups. The bare AI system fails silently and confidently under all three shift types, whereas COMET reduces the trusted-wrong-answer rate to zero on covariate-shifted no-leak data and on three of four sensor faults, at a nominal false-alarm rate of $\approx 1\%$. Single monitors come close in detection but cannot attribute the fault mode. COMET converts their anonymous detection flags into diagnoses. Residual silent misses under semantic shift define the boundary of passive monitoring. Runtime monitoring frameworks for AI-enabled safety systems must therefore combine quantitative fault detection and isolation with qualitative, human-oriented feedback.

papers.title: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing
papers.abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) models can estimate item parameters through an item response decoder trained solely for next-response prediction, yet predictive accuracy does not guarantee parameter recovery. We study 2PL, GPCM, and NRM decoders paired with LSTM, Transformer, and DKVMN encoders. Response-model derivatives show why discrimination and option slope updates depend directly on the scale and spread of estimated ability. Affine logit identities show how item-dependent shifts and rescaling in estimated ability are absorbed into item parameters without changing response probabilities. In simulations, difficulty, mean threshold, and correct-option intercept recovery remain high under shuffled order across representation widths, whereas discrimination and keyed option slope contrast recovery require wider item representations and degrade further under fixed item order. Separating the sequence item representation (width $d_S$) from the item parameter key (width $d_M$), and pairing a wide key with a thin sequence representation ($\mathrm{SK}(64,8)$), reduces fixed-order ability distortions and improves recovery and cross-order consistency without sacrificing test accuracy or increasing model size relative to a shared width-64 baseline ($\mathrm{SH}(64)$). On TIMSS and EdNet, widening $d_M$ consistently improves agreement with an offline IRT reference, while the trade-off from narrowing $d_S$ depends on the encoder's reliance on sequence width for prediction. These findings show why item parameters, especially discrimination and option slopes, must be evaluated separately from response prediction.

papers.title: Pfaffian Recognition is in $\mathsf{coRP}$
papers.abstract: An orientation of a graph is called Pfaffian if all perfect matchings occur with the same sign in its Pfaffian expansion. A graph is Pfaffian if it admits such an orientation. Given a Pfaffian orientation, the number of perfect matchings can be computed in polynomial time. In 1963, Kasteleyn showed that every planar graph is Pfaffian. In 1989, Vazirani and Yannakakis showed that deciding whether a graph is Pfaffian is polynomial time equivalent to testing whether a given orientation is Pfaffian. For bipartite graphs, polynomial time recognition algorithms were obtained by Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas in 1999, and independently by McCuaig in 2004. Whether a deterministic polynomial time algorithm exists for general graphs remains open. In this paper, we first construct a polynomial that is identically zero if and only if a given orientation is Pfaffian, and show that this polynomial can be evaluated in polynomial time. Combined with the reduction of Vazirani and Yannakakis, this gives a randomized polynomial time algorithm for deciding whether a general graph is Pfaffian, placing the problem in $\mathsf{coRP}$. We also prove that an orientation of a matching covered graph is non-Pfaffian if and only if reversing the edges of some cut makes it strongly connected. Although deciding whether such a cut exists is NP-complete for general digraphs, our characterization yields a randomized polynomial time algorithm for matching covered graphs and deterministic polynomial time algorithms for bipartite and planar matching covered graphs.

papers.title: A Super-Convergent Quasi-Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Advection-Diffusion Problems
papers.abstract: The aim of the present study is to develop discontinuous Galerkin and nonconforming finite-element methods for solving the 2D advection-diffusion equation. The discrete formulations are stabilized by means of a family of numerical fluxes and the dispersion relations are constructed via a Fourier/stability analysis. The linear discontinuous P1DG and non conforming P1NC Galerkin discretizations are studied. A long time stability result is proven for the P1NC and P1DG schemes and fluxes examined here by inspecting the discrete frequencies, solutions of the dispersion relations. A super-convergent result is also demonstrated for the P1NC discrete frequency (O(h 4 ) accuracy) compared to the P1DG one (O(h 2 ) accuracy). These results are in line with those obtained in a previous paper for the shallow-water system.

papers.title: Study of $Λ$ $CP$ Asymmetry Parameter and Electric Dipole Moment at the Super Tau-Charm Facility
papers.abstract: Searching for new mechanisms of $CP$ violation beyond the Standard Model is essential to explain the observed matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe. By analyzing the full angular distribution of the quantum-entangled $Λ\barΛ$ pairs from $J/ψ$ decays, the preliminary sensitivity of $CP$ asymmetry parameter $A_{CP}$ and Electric Dipole Moment of $Λ$ is studied at the future Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF). Based on $3.4 \times 10^{12}$ $J/ψ$ events at STCF, the projected sensitivity for $A_{CP}^Λ$ reaches the $10^{-4}$ level, while the $Λ$ EDM can be probed at $10^{-20}$ $e$ cm. These results highly indicate that STCF will provide an unprecedented opportunity to search for new mechanisms of $CP$ violation with an expected world-leading precision.

papers.title: A Consolidated Deployment Edition of a Microservice Core-Banking Platform: Composing Services by Reference into Three Hosts
papers.abstract: Microservices give teams independent deployment and scaling, but each deployed service also reserves compute and adds operational work. This paper examines a second deployment edition of a multi-tenant .NET core-banking platform. The existing edition runs as nine AWS ECS Fargate tasks; the alternative composes the five API services by project reference into one API host, alongside a consumer host and a background host. The service code remains in its original repositories, and both editions continue to be built from the same commits. We describe the composition mechanism, module manifest, start-up checks, request handling and configuration precedence, then compare the editions in an emulation of the AWS deployment. The composed edition exposes all 844 declared operations. Across 47 financial workload cases, both editions produced the same observed outcomes and matching ledgers. In read probes across five principal types, 230 of 231 endpoint results matched; the remaining difference was associated with the emulated load balancer. Eleven cross-tenant and write-authorisation cases also produced the expected outcomes in both editions. In the emulation, the composed edition delivered 2.3 times the read throughput and used less than half the memory. Estimated service-task compute at list prices was 11-24% lower, excluding the shared gateway, load balancer, data stores and other operating costs. The consolidation also enlarges the failure domain: one API-host crash takes all five modules offline. Of 16 injected faults, the edition's checks detected 10, behavioural tests detected five additional faults, and one fault escaped both. These findings concern one platform and an emulated deployment that mirrors its topology, task sizes and configuration; they are not production-AWS measurements.

papers.title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Long-context inference in large language models (LLMs) imposes substantial memory requirements for the key-value (KV) cache. Token-selective sparse attention reduces attention computation and memory traffic, but KV entries must still be retained for future queries. KV storage capacity therefore remains a constraint on decoding concurrency. Combining GPU and CPU memory expands this capacity but requires efficient access across heterogeneous memory pools. We present UlaCache, a KV cache management system that provides unified logical addressing across GPU and CPU memory. Its logical-slot interface enables the inference engine to allocate, write, access, and release KV entries using stable identifiers across attention parallelism modes. UlaCache manages physical placement, residency, and transfers, updating address mappings after KV transfers. Parallel Bucketed LRU (PB-LRU) reduces the overhead of KV replacement by parallelizing recency updates and eviction-candidate selection within a GPU memory pool shared across requests. We evaluate UlaCache against state-of-the-art baselines. Under tensor-parallel attention (TP), UlaCache provides up to $11.4\times$ the usable KV cache capacity of HiSparse. For GLM-5.3 on eight H200 GPUs, UlaCache achieves peak decoding throughput of $1.10\times$ and $1.59\times$ that of HiSparse under data-parallel attention (DPA) and TP, respectively. For HY4 Preview on eight B300 GPUs, the corresponding throughput ratios are $1.27\times$ and $1.93\times$.

papers.title: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.

papers.title: UserSWE: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Conversations with Dynamic Users
papers.abstract: As coding agents become more capable, developers increasingly use them to fix bugs through multi-turn interactions. Existing benchmarks do not adequately cover this scenario. Most present a complete issue report in a single turn without interaction. Their evaluation can produce both false positives and false negatives, accepting incorrect patches or rejecting correct ones. We introduce UserSWE for evaluating coding agents' ability to fix repository-level bugs through multi-turn interactions with dynamic users and execution-grounded verdicts at every turn. Its construction pipeline turns repository history and existing single-turn benchmarks into multi-turn tasks. At each turn, information pools constrain what the simulated user can reveal, while a persona chain sampled from a transition model calibrated on 20,859 development sessions governs how it speaks. Tests run after every turn, and a pair of agents from different model families writes and gates each verdict, using test results as primary evidence and model judgment only for aspects the tests cannot resolve. We evaluate eleven agents on 72 tasks from 42 repositories and find that agent rankings change with the interaction budget. Claude Fable 5.1 resolves the most tasks in one turn, GPT-6-Astra resolves the most by the eighth turn, and Claude Opus 5 leads at most intermediate budgets. These results indicate that single-turn performance is insufficient to characterize interactive coding ability.

papers.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. This is a short empirical study, with one conversation and one run per cell. Agent memory is a costly patch for a weak model: Mem0 beats full context only with GPT-4o-mini, and its build alone costs more than a whole full-context rollout. Agent memory also has a ceiling, set by the model that writes it: a stronger reader does not recover what a weaker writer left out. With Claude Opus 5.5, Pi tops the cost-accuracy frontier, scoring 99% for less than half the cost of full context; its one miss is a wrong answer key. Part of that lead comes from photo captions that only the agents could read: on the 88 questions whose evidence has no photo, Pi and full context differ by one answer.

papers.title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
papers.abstract: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(Π,τ)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(Π,τ)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.

papers.title: GuidedSAM-Plume: An Expert-Guided Segmentation Framework for Volcanic Plumes
papers.abstract: Quantitative analysis of environmental phenomena increasingly relies on image-based measurements. In volcanology, the geometric characterization of volcanic plumes and clouds from RGB images remains hindered by the scarcity of dedicated segmentation solutions and partially handcrafted annotations remain widely prevalent. We present GuidedSAM-Plume, an open-source expert-guided framework tailored for the interactive segmentation of volcanic plumes and clouds. It leverages the zero-shot, spatial prompt-based capabilities of SAM2. The framework was thoroughly validated on a challenging dataset through dedicated segmentation metrics and field-relevant volcanological descriptors. From minimal user inputs, it is able to significantly increase performance compared to fully automatic dedicated solutions while preserving the reliability of derived volcanological parameters. The absence of retraining requirements lowers adoption barriers within the volcanological community, and the framework's demonstrated suitability for complex, diffuse plume-shaped phenomena extends its applicability to broader environmental science domains. The re-annotated dataset, produced under the guidance of expert volcanologists within the proposed framework, ultimately yields a more standardized release. The framework and accompanying dataset are made available at https://github.com/tad-damo/GuidedSAM-Plume.

papers.title: Numerical Information of Hilbert Space Operators
papers.abstract: For a Hilbert space operator $A\in B(H)$, the numerical range map of $A$, denoted $φ_A$ is the map sending unit vectors $x$ in $H$ to $\langle Ax,x\rangle$. From this map we define the Numerical Information of $A$, denoted $Σ_A$, which is the sigma algebra induced on the unit sphere by the numerical range map. One of the main results of the paper are that if $A,B\in B(H)$, and $φ_B=f\circ φ_A$, then $f$ is affine. Our other main result is showing that $Σ_B\subsetΣ_A$ if and only if $B=αRe(A)+βIm(A)+γI$ for some complex numbers $α,β,γ$.

papers.title: Kinematic and Dynamic Parameters of Anisotropic Models with Inflaton, Without A Priori Relation Between the Scale Factors and with A Posteriori Isotropization
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a detailed review of the calculations concerning homogeneous and anisotropic cosmological models, with particular emphasis on the Kantowski-Sachs cosmological model. As an innovative contribution, we derive an exact solution for the field equations, expressed in terms of a general form for the material content of the universe. We obtain the expressions for the energy density in this general case, as well as investigate the specific scenario involving the presence of a scalar field. We examine the evolutionary dynamics of the model that encompasses Hubble, density, and deceleration parameters. Additionally, we calculate the kinematic parameters associated with the model, namely: the scalar expansion Θ, the shear scalar σ, the rotation parameter ω, and the parameter Rα\b{eta}UαU\b{eta}, also known as the Raychaudhuri scalar or convergence condition, all of these parameters expressed within the framework of the Raychaudhuri equation. Instead of employing a preestablished relation between the scale factors of the model, we allow them to evolve freely, without a priori conditions. Thus, we can verify that the isotropic nature of the studied scenario manifests itself rapidly, leading to the traditional isotropic model.

papers.title: Early versus Late RGB-Infrared Fusion for Counter-UAV Detection: A Comparative Study
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel strategy for UAV detection through visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) fusion, in order to improve accuracy and precision in harsh environments and weather conditions. In this research, two opposite approaches have been studied and implemented: the first concerns image-level (early) fusion, which merges two different spectra into a single image to which one detector is applied. On the other hand, the second approach, called decision-level (late) fusion, focuses on blending together the output bounding boxes of two different detection pipelines, aiming to create a common result that can be applied to both spectra simultaneously. Both strategies have been extensively tested in a dedicated environment, which included alternating low and high brightness scenes, different backgrounds (sky and ground), distances (5, 25 and 60 m), altitudes and zoom levels (1X, 2X and 4X). These tests allowed for the assessment of actual detection capabilities and system reliability in real-world applications. Furthermore, the two fusion strategies were evaluated and compared over a set of aligned images in order to highlight the better approach of the two. The results indicate that early fusion achieves better raw performance, since it incorporates the thermal information from the beginning of the training process. However, late fusion presents an innovative and useful detection workflow that can be applied in cases of sensor or frame misalignment. Both positive and negative aspects have also been pointed out and discussed, in order to give a more comprehensive overview. Finally, the paper outlines implementation considerations and practical recommendations based on operational priorities. Overall, the findings contribute to the research in RGB-IR fusion modalities, with the goal of enhancing UAV detection capabilities.

papers.title: Robot Generalization Beyond Volume: The Diversity Path via Zero-Shot Capabilities
papers.abstract: General-purpose robots must handle tasks, objects and environments they were never trained on, yet zero-shot generalization remains one of the least solved problems in physical AI. In digital AI, zero-shot capability grew with the volume and, above all, the diversity of training data, much of it sourced from the crowd. Robotics instead relies on paid collection by a few well-funded teams, which yields volume without diversity. We formulate zero-shot generalization in physical AI as coverage of the deployment distribution, and show that more samples from the same collectors shrink the unseen region only slowly, while each new contributor can extend it. Building on this and on zero-shot learning, we propose a shared latent space for robot actions that combines multi-modal alignment, generative augmentation, and noisy-label learning. As a scalable source of diverse data, we propose a community of developers building applications on one standard, approachable robot, Origami. We close with a testable hypothesis and an evaluation protocol relating real-robot zero-shot success to the diversity of contributed data.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Failure Modes in Chest X-ray Classification via Spectral Domain Analysis
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for chest X-ray anomaly detection remain vulnerable to subtle distributional shifts (e.g., acquisition technique, patient-related factors, and preprocessing). Traditional error analysis often relies on semantic metadata or model embeddings, which can mask low-level signal variations that degrade performance. In this work, we propose a data-centric framework for automated failure mode discovery using spectral analysis. We project images into the frequency domain and extract a compact profile summarizing the distribution of signal energy across frequency bands. By performing unsupervised clustering on these spectral profiles, we demonstrate that model failures are not randomly distributed, but are strongly concentrated within specific spectral clusters. This method effectively isolates "blind spots", enabling the prediction of model reliability and the discovery of performance-degrading data slices without requiring ground-truth failure annotations.

papers.title: The Diophantine Problem with constraints in some free-by-cyclic groups
papers.abstract: In this paper we explore the Diophantine Problem, that is, the solvability of equations, in one-relator and free-by-cyclic groups, showing that this is decidable in some cases and undecidable otherwise, depending on their abelianisation and centre. In particular, we focus on a version of the Diophantine Problem which asks about the existence of solutions satisfying abelianisation constraints, and prove a number of results concerning the decidability of this problem for free-by-cyclic groups with centre, tree-GBS groups, cyclically pinched groups and the first hydra group.

papers.title: S-EDL: Eliciting Self-Evidence from Sequence Likelihoods for Semantic Calibration of LLMs
papers.abstract: Calibrating large language models (LLMs) in open-ended generation is uniquely challenging because many distinct token sequences can express the same underlying meaning. Prior calibration techniques target either fixed-set classification confidence or the binary correctness of individual strings, making them inherently ill-suited for the dynamic, multi-string nature of open-ended semantic outcomes. To bridge this gap, we introduce S-EDL, a novel evidential method that natively optimizes LLMs for semantic calibration. By eliciting evidence from the sequence likelihoods of the model itself, S-EDL constructs a differentiable Dirichlet prior over prompt-specific semantic classes. Optimizing the evidential loss under this prior yields a calibration-aware training signal over variable semantic classes, completely bypassing the need for fixed multiple-choice options. Evaluations across four open-ended benchmarks and three models demonstrate that S-EDL substantially reduces semantic calibration error while improving accuracy. By aligning generative likelihoods with semantic correctness, this work establishes a framework for deploying trustworthy LLMs in complex, open-ended applications. Code is available at: https://github.com/sandylaker/s-edl.

papers.title: Neutron Star-Main-Sequence Star Collision: Formation and Long-Term Evolution of Thorne-Żytkow Objects
papers.abstract: Thorne-$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$ytkow objects (T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$Os) are stars containing a neutron-star (NS) or black-hole (BH) core embedded in a stellar envelope and powered primarily by mass accretion onto the core. Classical evolution models of T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$Os begin with an assumed equilibrium configuration and predict chemical anomalies in the stellar envelope resulting from nuclear burning in the vicinity of the NS core. Here we connect dynamical formation to long-term evolution by combining a three-dimensional simulation of a post-supernova collision between a $1.4M_\odot$ NS and a $10M_\odot$ main-sequence star with a subsequent stellar evolution calculation using MESA. The collision successfully produces a bound, quasi-spherical T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$O with the NS settled at the center of the stellar envelope. In contrast to the classical picture, the collision heats a substantial fraction of the star and leads to widespread nuclear burning during the subsequent thermal-relaxation phase. As the envelope becomes convective, material processed by the carbon-nitrogen cycle is transported to the surface, leaving a potentially observable chemical imprint of formation that persists after the star attains the standard accretion-supported T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$O structure. At the end of our simulation, the stellar luminosity greatly exceeds Eddington in the outer envelope, suggesting that significant mass ejection will occur, leaving behind an isolated NS or BH.

papers.title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
papers.abstract: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons. The same educational framework was adopted for in service teacher professional development courses. Learning outcomes were evaluated through mixed methods. Preliminary analysis indicates significant improvements in conceptual understanding, confidence in using mathematical formalism, and appreciation of the relationship between theory, experimentation, and the foundations of quantum mechanics. The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.

papers.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

papers.title: AT-Differ: Dataset for Audio-Text Difference Captioning
papers.abstract: Evaluating audio-text semantic alignment is important in various audio-language tasks. Existing methods mainly quantify audio-text semantic alignment using a single score and cannot explicitly describe how audio and text differ. In this paper, we propose audio-text difference captioning, a task that generates textual descriptions of differences between audio and text. We also construct a new dataset AT-DIFFER containing audio-text pairs with systematically simulated differences and corresponding difference captions. Using AT-DIFFER, we fine-tune an existing multimodal large language model to describe differences between audio and text. The experimental results show that the original model has limited ability to describe such differences, whereas fine-tuning on AT-DIFFER substantially improves this ability.

papers.title: Linear Self-Symmetries of Inverse-Based S-boxes: Generic Rigidity and Applications
papers.abstract: Finite-field inversion is a basic nonlinear building block in the design of S-boxes for symmetric cryptography. In inverse-based S-boxes, finite-field inversion is often combined with linear or affine layers that may preserve or destroy algebraic symmetries of the inverse function. We study how often nontrivial linear self-symmetries remain as the outer invertible linear transformation varies over \(GL_n(\mathbb F_2)\). Using the classification of two-sided linear equivalences of inversion, we reduce the problem to semilinear conjugacy and centralizer estimates. We obtain matching upper and lower bounds for the probability that a nontrivial linear self-symmetry remains, and these bounds determine its leading quadratic exponent. This exponent is governed by the smallest prime divisor of the extension degree. Thus the decay rate depends on the arithmetic of the field extension and not only on its dimension. As cryptographic applications, we provide a practical rigidity criterion, prove that the full AES S-box has no nontrivial linear self-symmetry, and illustrate the broader relevance of the framework through ARIA and Vision.

papers.title: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
papers.abstract: Double neutron star (DNS) systems emit gravitational waves (GW) as they orbit each other, with waveforms dependent on their orbital properties \cite{Poisson+2014grav.book.....P}. The number of DNS systems surviving binary star evolution in the Milky Way and the distribution of their orbital parameters are fundamental questions for GW astronomy and binary evolution studies. Here, we report the discovery of a new Galactic field DNS system, PSR J0653+0443, comprising two ~1.4 $M_\odot$ components in an extremely eccentric orbit $e=0.992387$, $P_{\rm orb}=79.084$ d. Its unique orbital dynamics include a 46-minute transit from true anomaly $θ=-90^\circ$ to $90^\circ$ and striking periastron relative motion (maximum acceleration 1.11~km~s$^{-2}$, peak speed 1.14$\times$10$^6$~m~s$^{-1}$. The pulsar undergoes an 85-second conjunction eclipse, indicating a nearly edge-on binary orbit. Short-term variations in the periastron advance induce significant pulse arrival time modulation spanning -2.91 to +2.49 ms --- at least an order of magnitude larger than that observed in any other DNS system. From this modulation, the non-relativistic periastron advance rate is constrained to $-1.5^{+0.9}_{-0.8}\times10^{-4}$ deg yr$^{-1}$. The extreme orbital eccentricity can only be attributed to a large kick velocity imparted during the iron-core collapse supernova of the progenitor of the second component. The predicted detection probability of such a PSR J0653+0443-like DNS system is $\lesssim 5 \times 10^{-3}$, implying that our discovery of this system challenges current understanding of binary evolution. This extraordinary DNS system emits periodic gravitational wave bursts, with the GW energy flux peaking at 0.357 mHz. This makes it an ideal target for the future LISAmax mission.

papers.title: Spacetime Splines for Adaptive Robot Motions
papers.abstract: Movement primitives commonly represent robot mo- tions through basis functions indexed by time or phase. Inspired by spacetime representations employed in physics, we propose a spline-based formulation in which spatial geometry and temporal progression are represented within a common set of continuous variables. The proposed method jointly estimates a shared Bezier curve, while allowing spatial and temporal model complexity to be adapted independently (e.g., demonstration-specific phase modulation). As use case, we consider an alternating optimization process that simultaneously estimates path intervals observed in partial demonstrations. Simulation experiments demonstrate accurate joint recovery, refinement through modifications in model complexity and continuity, and improved robustness to variance in the demonstration set. Finally, we demonstrate online retiming and synchronization capabilities in a patient-turning task assisted by a robot, evaluated with a physical manikin.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for vibrating plates: simpler planar proof and nonlinear extensions
papers.abstract: We give a simpler proof of Nadirashvili's theorem (Rayleigh's conjecture) that among vibrating clamped plates of prescribed area in the plane, the disk has the lowest fundamental tone. The proof uses a one-shot Talenti type comparison for sign-changing solutions of the Poisson equation with mean-zero data, established in a companion paper. The comparison considers just two rearranged sources, rather than optimizing over all admissible sources as in the traditional two-ball technique. This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|Δu\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. Equality is characterized for $q>1$, while exceptional behavior at $q=1$ is identified. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. We also establish the corresponding interval inequality in one dimension.

papers.title: Broadband Mid-Wave Infrared Imaging Enabled by All-Silicon Hyperboloid Metalens
papers.abstract: The mid-wave infrared (MWIR, 3-5 microns) is indispensable for thermal sensing, gas detection, long-range imaging, and free-space optical communications. Meta-optics offer a compact, lightweight, and potentially low-cost alternative to conventional refractive optics, making them attractive for size, weight, and power (SWaP)-constrained systems. However, their strong chromatic dispersion has largely restricted imaging to narrow spectral bands. Here, we demonstrate broadband imaging across the full 3-5 micron MWIR band using a single-layer silicon metasurface coupled with computational reconstruction. Remarkably, the reconstruction model is adapted using only four image captures, overcoming large training data requirements and enabling broadband image recovery despite the strongly wavelength-dependent optical response. In contrast to approaches that engineer complex, dispersion-optimized metalens profiles for broadband operation, our method leverages the wavelength-dependent information encoded by a simple 2cm diameter hyperboloid metalens. We show that this metasurface captures sufficient broadband intensity information for computational reconstruction across the entire MWIR band. These results establish a simple route toward broadband computational meta-optics without requiring broadband achromatic metalens designs, offering a promising platform for compact MWIR imaging systems.

papers.title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

papers.title: Every Part Has Its Role: Part-of-Speech Effects in LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Large language models are typically trained with next-token prediction (NTP), which rewards predicting specific tokens rather than explicitly accounting for the semantic similarities between different words or expressions. Prior work has addressed this limitation by augmenting training data with minimally varying sentences that replace a target word with conceptually related alternatives, e.g., "The tired coach ran home" $\rightarrow$ {"The tired trainer ran home", "The tired instructor ran home", ...}. Such concept augmentation improves performance, but it remains unclear whether its effectiveness depends on where in the sentence the concept is expressed. We reproduce and extend prior work $\textit{beyond nouns}$ to verbs and adjectives, asking whether the part of speech (POS) carrying the concept signal affects perplexity and downstream performance. We find different patterns across evaluation settings: concept augmentation improves perplexity most consistently on news, independent of the POS used, whereas verbs provide the most reliable downstream gains. Despite these behavioral differences, representational analyses using CKA and linear probing show that the conditions yielding the largest downstream gains are not necessarily those that most alter the model's internal representations. Together, these results suggest that the effectiveness of concept augmentation depends on where and how conceptual information is introduced during training.

papers.title: Explicit finite size corrections for Toeplitz determinants and rectangular domino tilings
papers.abstract: Finite Toeplitz truncation does not, in general, preserve multiplication. For products of $m$ $N\times N$ tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices with symbols $z+z^{-1}+a_h$, we make the two boundary corrections in Widom's product formula for finite sections explicit. The method of images gives two Hankel corrections when $m\le N+2$, a sharp uniform degree bound. For $N\ge m-1$, the ratio of the determinant of the matrix product to the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol reduces, whenever defined, to a determinant of order $2(m-1)$, which reversal symmetry splits into two determinants of order $m-1$. A rectangular Schur polynomial gives an exact formula for the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol, including when roots coincide. For symbols nonzero on the unit circle, classical identities for rational symbols give an exact $m\times m$ determinant formula for the ratio, with an explicit confluent form for repeated roots. With $ρ_h$ the zero of $z+z^{-1}+a_h$ in $|z|<1$, the limit is $\prod_{i<j}(1-ρ_iρ_j)^2$ as $N\to\infty$ at fixed $m,a_h$. For rectangular domino tilings, these formulas compare the classical Kasteleyn--Temperley--Fisher product with the banded Toeplitz determinant formed from the product symbol. We obtain the first exponentially small correction at fixed width and relate this comparison to the Toeplitz determinant furnished by the dual Cauchy identity.

papers.title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced. Project website: https://rangenav.github.io/.

papers.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
papers.abstract: We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.

papers.title: Memory Manipulation
papers.abstract: We study persuasion that works through memory: a manipulator alters the probabilities with which a Bayesian decision-maker recalls the signals he has received. The decision-maker corrects for the elevated or reduced probabilities of recalling different signals, and this correction disciplines what manipulation can achieve. Manipulation cannot move the average posterior. It backfires on decision-makers with few memories, whose sparse recall is evidence against the favored state, yet it is effective on those with many, who can be led to arbitrarily confident beliefs in the wrong state. It thickens the right tail of the belief distribution and, under Poisson memory, lowers its hazard rate. In a monopoly pricing application, the seller manipulates memory retrieval at high prices, and manipulation in turn raises the optimal price. In a narrative persuasion application, memory manipulation reduces information provision and creates echo chambers.

papers.title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
papers.abstract: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material. We find nearly-perfect insensitivity to defects only for wavevectors with single transport modes within specific Fermi level ranges in CoSi(001) and PtAl(001). Importantly, we also find high insensitivity for certain non-isolated modes in NbAs that emerge specifically due to spin-orbit coupling; these modes could not be identified previously as they were buried in the total transmission. These non-isolated modes have been buried in previous studies of total transmission, and can now be directly compared to other materials due to our standardization of defect-creation. This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

papers.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
papers.abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.

papers.title: Automated Discovery of Physically Interpretable Subgrid Length Scales for Detached Eddy Simulation via Agentic AI
papers.abstract: Traditional turbulence-model development relies heavily on expert knowledge and is time-consuming. This study develops an agentic AI framework, DEScover (automated Discovery of DES closures), to explore subgrid length scales for detached eddy simulation (DES). The user provides only a modeling idea: the length scale is the grid width normal to the local vortex axis. Four large language model (LLM) agents then propose, review, implement, and evaluate candidate formulations and generate scripts for CFD simulations. The Discovery Agent infers the vortex axis from various vortex-identification methods. The candidates are tested on four cases spanning canonical and engineering flows: a flat plate, a backward-facing step, a free shear layer, and an iced airfoil. For all test cases, the best candidate consistently outperforms the standard length scale based on the maximum cell size. Its accuracy is similar to, or slightly better than, that of the expert-designed shear-layer-adapted length scale. Each agentic discovery run takes about 25 minutes on average, excluding the CFD simulations. These results show that LLM-based reasoning can significantly accelerate the discovery of physically interpretable turbulence models and reduce reliance on manual expert formulation.

papers.title: Differentiated Determinant Graphs Enable Large-Scale Multideterminant Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Multideterminant trial wave functions can reduce phaseless bias in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC), but the repeated evaluation of their overlap, force bias, and local energy restricts systematic trial improvement. In this work, we organize particle--hole excitation determinants as a shared arithmetic directed acyclic graph of canonical minors. A coefficient-weighted reverse pass and batched directional passes evaluate the complete estimator without determinant-resolved cofactor tensors while preserving the sparse $α$--$β$ coefficient coupling exactly. Controlled complex-valued tests verify the complete kernel to machine precision and show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over direct determinant summation. In molecular calculations, the observed cost remains sublinear through million-configuration selected-CI trials and the same estimator remains usable at one hundred million configurations, where the eventual exact coefficient-contraction boundary becomes visible. For Cr$_2$, an orbital-optimized CAS(12e,42o) trial in a double-$ζ$ basis yields a potential-energy curve (PEC) and spectroscopic constants in close agreement with experiment. Differentiated determinant graphs therefore convert very large correlated trials from a formal accuracy hierarchy into a practical route for systematic AFQMC studies of strongly correlated molecules.

papers.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ Γ=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Spatial preferential attachment models: robustness revisited
papers.abstract: We investigate robustness under percolation in the degree-driven spatial preferential attachment model. Consider a profile that is regularly varying with exponent $-δ$, where $δ>1$, and an attachment rule with asymptotic slope $γ\in(0,1)$. Jacob and Mörters (Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)) proved robustness when $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)<1. $$ We prove the converse in the strict regime: if $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)>1, $$ then sufficiently strong Bernoulli vertex thinning destroys the giant component. In particular, the strict robustness boundary coincides with that of the age-dependent random connection model.

papers.title: How Do DiTs Denoise? An Aggregator-Predictor View of Attention and MLPs
papers.abstract: How do diffusion transformers (DiTs) represent image content and learn rules for reusing it to generalize? We develop an aggregator--predictor view of DiTs as input-adaptive local denoisers, in which context aggregation and patch prediction provide functional roles for interpreting attention and MLPs. We first establish that, for Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) priors, the global Bayes denoiser can be approximated using only a subset of context patches, with error decaying exponentially in context radius. We further show that patchwise linear denoisers, often invoked to explain diffusion generalization, recover the empirical local denoiser with sufficiently informative aggregation. Within this view, AdaLN-modulated attention naturally parameterizes an input- and noise-dependent aggregator, while the MLP admits a learned key--value representation for tokenwise patch prediction. Our experiments support this view. DiTs trained on real images exhibit noise-dependent denoising contexts resembling those in the analytic GMRF setting, while attention mass exhibits a qualitatively corresponding broadening pattern. In a controlled CelebA64 study, shared-memory patch predictors used in place of DiT MLPs achieve competitive denoising and generative performance. Finally, cross-dataset component transplantation reveals compatibility patterns consistent with the proposed roles of QK in spatial weighting, VO in feature transport, and MLPs in patch prediction. Together, these results provide a component-level account of DiT denoising and motivate architecture-specific fine-tuning and controlled intervention.

papers.title: Regularity and $v$-number of syzygies of graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
papers.abstract: Let $A=Q/(\mathbf f)$, where $Q$ is a polynomial ring over an infinite field $k$ and $\mathbf f=f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a homogeneous $Q$-regular sequence. For $1\leq j\leq c$, set $w_j=\operatorname{deg}(f_j)>0.$ Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-module of infinite projective dimension. Set $M_i=\operatorname{Syz}_i^A(M)$. We prove that, for each $l\in\{0,1\}$, the sets $\operatorname{Ass}_A(M_{2i+l})$ eventually stabilize, and that $\operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$ is eventually bounded above and below by linear polynomials. If $w_j=w$ for all $1\leq j\leq c$, then the functions $i\longmapsto \operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$, $i\longmapsto v(M_{2i+l}),$ and $i\longmapsto v_{\mathfrak p}(M_{2i+l}),\, \mathfrak p\in\mathcal A_l,$ are eventually linear with leading coefficient $w$, where $\mathcal A_l$ denotes the stable set of associated primes.

papers.title: Efficient Eccentric and Quasicircular Effective-One-Body Waveforms via Near-Identity Averaging Transformations
papers.abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, will require accurate and efficient models of long-lived, eccentric black-hole binary signals. In previous work, we reduced the cost of evolving nonspinning eccentric effective-one-body dynamics by recasting the equations of motion in terms of osculating orbital elements and applying near-identity averaging transformations to remove the fast orbital-timescale structure during the inspiral. However, the parametrization in terms of the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly becomes singular in the circular-orbit limit, excluding quasicircular binaries and the late stages of eccentric inspirals. Moreover, the cost of generating the waveform from the averaged dynamics limited the overall speed-up to a factor of $1.5-8$. In this work, we replace the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly by the Cartesian components of the eccentricity vector, in which the averaged equations are regular for all eccentricities $0 \leq e < 1$. We also decompose the waveform modes into radial harmonics whose coefficients are tabulated as functions of the averaged variables, so that the waveform is assembled directly on the output time grid at a fixed cost per sample. We validate the method against the full effective-one-body evolution across the parameter space of binaries observable by ground-based detectors, now including circular orbits. At second postadiabatic order, the waveforms reach median mismatches of $\sim 10^{-8}$ with a maximum of $1.1 \times 10^{-5}$, while achieving speed-ups of $3-100 \times$ on a single core or up to $300 \times$ on eight cores against the serial EOB waveform. Given the speed-ups demonstrated here, we plan to apply these techniques to state-of-the-art SEOBNR models in future work.

papers.title: Semiclassical effects on ultramassive spacetimes
papers.abstract: A recent work [Senovilla, Port. Math. 80 (2023)] has shown that accretion of matter by a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole can take this object beyond a critical limit where the event and cosmological horizons coalesce, transforming it into a collapsing universe resembling a Kantowski-Sachs cosmology. In these configurations, dubbed ``ultramassive spacetimes'', future asymptotic infinity and the event horizon associated with the black hole cease to exist. In this work, we take the first steps toward exploring semiclassical gravity effects on such geometries. In particular, we examine the fate of Hawking radiation in these backgrounds and analyze the behavior of the renormalized stress-energy tensor within the Polyakov approximation. We also explore the effect of semiclassical backreaction on the evolution of the horizons, focusing on cases in the vicinity of the extremal limit, and on the subsequent universal collapse.

papers.title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
papers.abstract: The iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of non-layered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, the issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition (CVD) synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe-Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ~4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation (SHG) signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centro-symmetry of the cubic phase. SQUID magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin-orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

papers.title: Time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for viscous-dispersive heat-conducting compressible fluids
papers.abstract: We establish the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, which describes the dynamics of viscous, heat-conducting, compressible fluids with internal capillarity. We prove that, for the adiabatic exponent $γ\in(1,2]$, the solution to the NSFK system converges uniformly in space, as time tends to infinity, to a composite wave consisting of a rarefaction wave, a viscous contact wave, and a viscous-dispersive shock with a time-dependent shift, provided that the initial perturbation and the strengths of the contact wave and the shock are sufficiently small. In particular, we do not impose any smallness condition on the strength of the rarefaction wave. Because of the capillarity, the shock is viscous-dispersive and its profile equation is of third order. We treat the shock by the method of $a$-contraction with shifts introduced by Kang and Vasseur. This is the first result on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous-dispersive shock, and of a generic Riemann solution, for the NSFK system.

papers.title: Charge Density Wave transient states induced by ultrashort hard X-ray pulses
papers.abstract: The interaction of quantum systems with ultrashort laser pulses may lead to transient states far from equilibrium. Among these, Charge Density Wave (CDW) systems offer very rich non-equilibrium physics when submitted to ultrashort optical excitations in the infrared regime. In this Letter, we show that CDW systems pumped by ultrashort x-ray pulses excite the system in very different way. The x-ray pump, 6000 times more energetic than a laser pulse, pumping and probing the whole bulk system simultaneously, drives CDW systems in a novel reversible out of equilibrium state. The successive CDW states observed in the NbSe$_3$ system with respect to the arrival of x-ray pulses follow a non-thermal kinetic path. It is characterized by a change in 2k$_F$ wavevector, correlation lengths and electronic gap, as well as a change of dimensionality, all of this takes place within a very long recovery time ranging from 450$ns$ to 0.01$s$. Several scenarios are proposed, including transient nucleation and recombination of charged topological objects.

papers.title: Progress on meson-glueball mixing in lattice gauge theories coupled to fermions in multiple representations
papers.abstract: We present preliminary results from our numerical lattice investigation of the low-lying flavour-singlet bound states in the ${\rm Sp}(4)$ gauge theory coupled to fermions transforming in the fundamental and two-index antisymmetric representations. We use the Wilson gauge action and Wilson fermions. We employ the generalized eigenvalue problem (GEVP) method with a basis of smeared glueball and meson interpolating operators. We analyse two high-statistics ensembles with the same lattice coupling and different fermion mass. We study both the scalar and pseudoscalar states. We observe the first evidence for meson-glueball mixing in this theory. We improve upon previous determinations of the energy eigenstates and mixing angles in the flavour-singlet pseudoscalar sector.

papers.title: Quenched disorder in polymerized membranes: from anomalous elasticity to a glassy phase
papers.abstract: Polymerized membranes are paradigmatic fluctuating systems in which geometry, elasticity, and statistical fluctuations combine to produce anomalous long-distance behavior. In the disorder-free flat phase, bending rigidity increases at long wavelengths while in-plane elastic moduli soften. Quenched random metric and curvature introduce competing thermal and disorder-induced fluctuations. We review perturbative and nonperturbative field-theoretical approaches to these systems, from pure membranes to their disordered counterparts. Early one-loop studies identified a disorder-free fixed point, $P_4$, and a zero-temperature disorder-dominated fixed point, $P_5$. A subsequent nonperturbative renormalization-group analysis revealed a third fixed point, $P_c$, at finite temperature and disorder, governing a continuous wrinkling transition between the thermally dominated flat phase and a disorder-dominated glassy phase. Higher-order perturbative calculations also recover a $P_c$-like fixed point, with anomalous dimensions remarkably close to the reexpanded nonperturbative predictions. This scenario connects naturally with the wrinkling transition observed in partially polymerized lipid membranes. The three experimental scaling regimes of height fluctuations can be associated with $P_4$, $P_c$, and $P_5$, with theoretical exponents showing good quantitative agreement with measurements, particularly at criticality. Finally, we discuss the status of the glassy scenario, the unresolved discrepancy between perturbative and nonperturbative fixed-point stability predictions, and possible extensions to defective graphene and related two-dimensional crystalline materials.

papers.title: A Broadband Room-Temperature Design for the Einstein Telescope
papers.abstract: The unique underground location of the Einstein Telescope (ET) is expected to substantially suppress seismic and gravity-gradient noise, providing a favorable environment for gravitational-wave detection at low frequencies compared with surface-based observatories. The baseline ET design aims to achieve broadband sensitivity through a xylophone configuration, in which separate cryogenic and room-temperature interferometers are optimised for low- and high-frequency gravitational-wave detection. However, achieving the target low-frequency sensitivity introduces substantial technical complexity caused by vertical suspension thermal noise, vibrations of the cryocooler, and detuned optical configuration. In this paper, we demonstrate an alternative, entirely room-temperature, fully resonant, single-interferometer architecture that addresses these challenges and achieves broadband sensitivity superior to that of the conventional ET xylophone configuration. Using mature fused-silica suspension technology, recent advances in optical coatings, and novel inertial isolation, we show that 4-m-long fused-silica fibres can meet the required suspension thermal-noise performance. We further demonstrate that vibrations, optical rigidity, and quantum back-action noise can be controlled through appropriate design of the interferometer, test mass suspensions, optical seismometers, and quantum states.

papers.title: Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective
papers.abstract: We study gradient flow in a two-layer linear network in the high-dimensional regime where the input, inner and output dimensions diverge proportionally. Under whitened inputs and isotropic imbalance, we combine a closed-form solution of the dynamics with prior random matrix theory results to derive a high-dimensional limit for the dynamics. Our method yields exact asymptotic spectral distributions for the weight matrices at all times and characterizes the evolution of the learned subspace. In the small-initialization limit, we identify a silent alignment phenomenon: the singular directions of the network align on an order-one timescale, while the singular values and empirical loss remain at their initial values. Visible learning occurs later, on a logarithmic timescale, as singular values progressively escape zero and the loss decreases. This phase is characterized by a saddle-to-saddle dynamics, which becomes a continuous process of spectral learning in the high-dimensional limit.

papers.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
papers.abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: From Traveling Waves to Synthetic Gauge Fields: A Field-Free Route to Superconducting Diode Effect
papers.abstract: The superconducting diode effect requires the forward and reverse bias currents to differ, a scenario achieved via inversion and time-reversal symmetries broken together. The latter, and the more crucial one, is inevitably achieved by a magnetic field. Here, we show that a spatio-temporally driven chemical potential of the form, $μ_j(t)=μ+V\cos(ωt+\kd j)$, achieves both at once. Applied to a helical Shiba chain, the drive transmutes a traveling Peierls phase via generating an odd-in-momentum term, equivalent to an imaginary next-nearest-neighbour Haldane-like hopping in real space. Remarkably, the protocol is spin-blind, which renders the time-reversal breaking via a synthetic gauge flux rather than an effective Zeeman field. The rectification is odd in the drive wavevector, with exact zeros at $\kd=nπ$ and an analytical optimum at $\kd=2π/3$. It is however, even in the exchange coupling, $J$ and persists even at $J=0$. Furthermore, the rectification scales inversely with the pair-breaking gap, yielding approximately $50\%$ rectification in the topological phase and $10\%$ in the trivial phase. Symmetry breaking is thus drive-controlled, allowing it to be switched on, tuned, and reversed without an external magnetic field.

papers.title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.

papers.title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
papers.abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.

papers.title: Evaluating Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection for Identifying Unusual Galaxy Morphologies in CEERS and NGDEEP
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology out to $z\sim 6$ provides insight into galaxy formation and evolution, but identifying rare or structurally complex systems is difficult due to observational limits and the scale of modern imaging surveys. Here, we apply AdaCLIP, a Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection (ZSAD) model built upon the Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) model and adapted using non-astronomical anomaly-detection datasets, to identify structurally unusual galaxies without galaxy-specific anomaly-detection training or morphological labels. We extract anomaly scores and 768-dimensional feature embeddings from 38,853 galaxies in the Cosmic Evolution Early Release Science (CEERS) and Next Generation Deep Extragalactic Exploratory Public (NGDEEP) surveys, and compare the resulting anomaly scores with parametric GALFIT and nonparametric statmorph measurements. The feature embeddings reveal structure associated with galaxy morphology and observational properties, while anomaly scores show modest trends with structural measures, including asymmetry, concentration, $M_{20}$, and size, but weaker or less consistent trends with Sérsic index, axis ratio, smoothness, and Gini coefficient. These results highlight the potential of ZSAD as a scalable tool for identifying unusual galaxy morphologies in large astronomical imaging surveys, including those anticipated from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

papers.title: Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents that run long enough must compact their context, summarizing the conversation, discarding the original, and carrying the summary forward as memory. We show that in popular open-source coding agents this step is an exploitable trust boundary. Harnesses that flatten the typed conversation into a single plain string, marking each message with a text label such as [User]:, destroy message provenance in code, before the summarizer runs. An attacker who controls anything the agent reads can forge a user turn that survives compaction as a genuine instruction. Across five flattening harnesses (pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands) the forged approval launders into the agent's memory 87-100% of the time, up to a ~908,000-token context window; across four role-typed harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue) the identical attack succeeds 0% of the time. We follow the attack to executed consequences. A laundered standing approval drives real tool-running agents to execute attacker-controlled curl | sh in a sandbox, and end to end in the live pi TUI at ~50% against a 0% paired clean arm. The same channel reliably steers an agent's plan away from a file an attacker designates off-limits, which can blind a code review to a planted backdoor. Because the provenance is destroyed deterministically in harness code, no prompt-level defense can restore it; we measure a code-level provenance check that catches 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate summary content. The defect also has a straightforward fix at the serializer, escaping the role labels before flattening; the role-typed harnesses avoid it entirely by keeping messages role-typed.

papers.title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
papers.abstract: Coding agents can invest substantial effort in repository exploration and testing yet still produce unsuccessful patches. Existing online steering methods review trajectories periodically or invoke an advisor when a monitor detects behavioral problems; frequent reviews are costly, and the absence of anomalous behavior does not mean that an agent is on the right track. We propose PAUSE, a framework for steering coding agents with a single planning intervention. Agents reach their first source-code edit at a median of 60% of trajectory progress, after exploration, bug reproduction, and testing. PAUSE intercepts this edit request before it executes, which requires no learned monitor, no search over checkpoints, and no extra model call (search-free). A separate Planner reads the task and the pre-edit transcript and writes one repair plan; the same agent, the Executor, resumes with this plan, keeping its context and workspace. PAUSE applies online, during a live run, and offline, from a recorded trajectory prefix. We evaluate PAUSE on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual with two Executors and three agent harnesses. With Qwen3-coder as Executor and GPT-5.6 Sol as Planner, online steering improves resolution by 16.8% on Verified in OpenHands and by 14.7% on Multilingual in SWE-agent. In SWE-agent, PAUSE outperforms LivePlan, a rule-triggered advisor, by 3.2% on Verified and 3.7% on Multilingual at similar Planner cost, and is comparable to SICA's periodic overseer at about 11-15% of its Planner cost. Offline, PAUSE recovers 35.4% of eligible failed Verified tasks, and resuming from the recorded prefix uses 33-41% fewer Executor tokens than restarting.

papers.title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs.
