The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.

papers.title: Recovering Plausible Transmission Outage Scenarios
papers.abstract: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower level problem, replace it with its sensitivity matrix, and use gradient descent to update the upper level. We treat the relaxed branch states as probabilities and perform randomized rounding to restore integrality. On three test systems with synthetic outages, the recovered sets reduce the load shed error to $0.02-4.5\%$. On the California Test System with storm data from December 2025, the error falls to $23\%$. These scenarios give expansion planning a reliable source of outage data tied to observed hazards.

papers.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.

papers.title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
papers.abstract: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{à} di Bruno formula. We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

papers.title: Stochastic Nonlinearities Improve Uncertainty Estimation
papers.abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important across visual recognition tasks, providing information about the confidence and reliability of model predictions. Many uncertainty estimation methods obtain predictive diversity through mechanisms that can suppress intermediate features, perturb the input, or require substantial additional computation. Stochastic activation functions, where network units randomly select between multiple nonlinearities during a forward pass, have previously been used to improve optimization behavior, mitigate limitations of fixed ReLU activations, and increase output diversity. In this work, we reframe stochastic activation switching as a lightweight mechanism for uncertainty estimation. The proposed method samples between nonlinear activation functions, inducing predictive diversity while keeping intermediate feature pathways active. This enables uncertainty estimation from a single trained model without the training cost of ensembles, task-specific uncertainty heads, or architectural redesign. We evaluate the proposed approach across classification, semantic segmentation, and out-of-distribution detection using convolutional and transformer-based architectures on diverse datasets. Across these settings, stochastic activation switching improves uncertainty quality while preserving competitive primary-task performance, showing that stochastic nonlinearities provide an effective and information-preserving source of predictive variation for visual recognition.

papers.title: Integral trace forms of cyclic number fields without tameness
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbf{Q}$ be a cyclic number field and let $T_K=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_K,(x,y)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbf{Q}}(xy)\bigr)$ be its integral trace lattice. We prove that two cyclic number fields have isometric integral trace lattices if and only if they have the same degree, signature, and signed discriminant. More generally, an isomorphism between the Dirichlet character groups of two finite abelian extensions that preserves the conductor and parity of every character yields an isometry of their integral trace lattices, equivariant for the dual identification of Galois groups. For cyclic fields, the degree, signature, and discriminant determine the character group together with these two functions. This proves Bolaños's conjecture for wildly ramified cyclic fields and gives the corresponding extension of the tame classification: in general, the signature must be retained as an additional invariant.

papers.title: Sharp Moser-Onofri inequality on the CR sphere under zero-moment constraints and its application to the stability of the CR Moser-Onofri inequality
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. By combining a decomposition into low and high spherical harmonics with the known CR localization estimates, we first prove the existence of extremals of the subcritical Moser--Onofri inequality under zero-moment constraints. We then derive their Euler--Lagrange equation, establish their smoothness, and eliminate the moment multiplier by means of the infinitesimal CR conformal action. Using the summation identity (4.9) on the Hardy space $H^2(B^n)$, we show that the extremals of subcritical Moser-Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints are constants. By a limiting argument, we deduce the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. As an application, we establish the stability of Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere with the best stability constant.

papers.title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((ρ|ρ^\vee)+\|ρ\|\,\|ρ^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.

papers.title: Roe algebras and coarse index maps for spaces with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids. II
papers.abstract: Building on the Roe algebra framework developed in the first paper of this series, we construct equivariant coarse index maps for locally compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids, with coefficients in any separable groupoid C* -algebra. The construction uses the coarse structures determined by the groupoid action and requires no choice of metric. By identifying Roe algebras of canonical modules with reduced crossed products, we prove that the Baum-Connes assembly map with coefficients factors through the coarse index map.

papers.title: On the notion of reasonable functions in Cohen--Lenstra type heuristics
papers.abstract: We elucidate the notion of "reasonable functions" in the context of Cohen--Lenstra heuristics. For a sequence $(x_i)_i$ of independent random variables valued in an infinite discrete probability space $(X,p)$, we investigate for what sets $S$ of functions on $X$ it is true that almost surely, for all $f\in S$, the average of $f$ on the sequence is equal to its expected value. We show that if $p$ decays sufficiently quickly, as e.g. the Cohen--Lenstra distribution does, then $\bigcup_{q>1}L^q(X)$ is such a set; while if $p$ decays sufficiently slowly, then not even $\bigcap_{q<\infty}L^q(X)$ has this property.

papers.title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
papers.abstract: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

papers.title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
papers.abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.

papers.title: Pilot Decontamination via Data-aided Channel Tracking in Cell-free Massive MIMO
papers.abstract: As cell-free massive MIMO emerges as a promising technology for future wireless networks, robust channel estimation becomes increasingly important. Channel estimation relies on pilot transmissions, and with increasing number of users, pilot reuse inevitably introduces contamination that degrades channel estimation and symbol detection. This limitation is compounded by rapidly evolving channels, which render the estimates obsolete over time. To address both the problems, viz. pilot contamination and channel aging without additional pilot overhead, we propose a Kalman filter-based data-aided channel tracking strategy. By leveraging the symbol estimates as virtual pilots, the proposed approach successively refines the channel estimates over time. Unlike the conventional Kalman filter model, here, the observation model depends on symbol estimates, introducing symbol uncertainty that gets coupled with channel uncertainty. This requires a careful calculation of the innovation covariance matrices. Additionally, we discuss a stochastic-gradient-descent based tracking approach with low computational complexity. Extensive simulations are used to demonstrate that successive refinement progressively decontaminates the channel estimate, achieving lower channel estimation error and improved spectral efficiency.

papers.title: Phenotype-structured nonlocal aggregation models I: signal production and response
papers.abstract: Individuals within a cellular or ecological population can exhibit substantial variation in their traits or phenotype. Such heterogeneity can fundamentally alter population-level behaviour, including the ability to aggregate and form spatial patterns. We investigate these effects by extending nonlocal aggregation models, widely used to model cell--cell adhesion and collective animal movement, to incorporate phenotype structure. We characterise how heterogeneity and switching between phenotypes affect whether patterns form, how phenotypes are distributed within them, and whether they are stationary or exhibit spatio-temporal oscillations. We show that pattern formation is promoted when phenotypes that produce stronger interaction signals also respond more strongly to them, whereas specialisation towards either signal production or response inhibits pattern formation. Increasing rates of switching between phenotypes dampen these effects. Heterogeneity can also enable weakly interacting, and even repulsive, individuals to pattern as part of the collective. Furthermore, movement in phenotype and physical space can interact to restructure patterns and generate spatio-temporal oscillations. A further key message of this study is the value of considering both discrete $N$-phenotype and continuous phenotype formulations. We develop both in parallel, demonstrating formal correspondences, but also advantages to each framework in terms of mathematical analyses and interpretability.

papers.title: Cosmological Gravitational Wave Collider Physics
papers.abstract: Primordial tensor non-Gaussianity can probe massive particles present during inflation. We investigate this possibility in an effective field theory where the massless graviton mixes with the helicity-two mode of an additional massive spin-two field $σ_{ij}$ with cubic self-interactions. For constant sound speed, we compute the leading tensor power-spectrum correction and the tree-level bispectrum, finding novel analytical expressions for these quantities. In the $m_σ>3H/2$ regime, we find a nonanalytic squeezed contribution that exhibits logarithmic oscillations with characteristic dependence $(k_L/k_S)^{3/2\pm iμ}$, where $μ=\sqrt{m_σ^2/H^2-9/4}$. The oscillation frequency is set by the mass $m_σ$, while the polarisation contractions determine the relative amplitudes of the different graviton helicity configurations. The same mixing generates corrections to the power spectrum and the bispectrum. We derive the associated quadrupolar modulation of short-scale tensor power spectrum and relate its amplitude to the model parameters. Finally, we explore how a slowly varying sound speed modifies the squeezed signal.~These results connect the two-point, three-point, and quadrupolar tensor signatures of massive spin-two fields in the cosmological gravitational wave collider.

papers.title: Characterizing and Defending Utility-Hijacking in Instruction-Tuning Data Selection
papers.abstract: Instruction-data selectors choose which instruction-following records are used for fine-tuning, improving alignment quality, raising training efficiency, and filtering out harmful records. A selector's choices thus directly affect the fine-tuned model's safety, yet despite their widespread use, the security of these selectors remains under-studied. We conduct the first systematic study of adaptive supplier-side attacks against utility-oriented instruction-data selectors and introduce utility-hijacking. Utility-hijacking shapes harmful records to remain compatible with a selector while preserving their malicious payload, causing top-k selection to concentrate rather than filter the poison. Achieving both is non-trivial, because optimizing a record for score tends to wash out its payload, while bluntly preserving the payload makes the record look low-value. Our generate-and-rerank procedure generates, per instruction, many payload-bearing candidates and submits only the highest-scoring survivor. Evaluated across three payloads (over-refusal, false-fact injection, and insecure code), six selectors, and victim models from Qwen2.5-7B to Qwen3-32B, utility-hijacking drives refusal from 0% to 94% and insecure code up to 56/90, while false-fact enrichment intensifies with scoring-model scale from 2.84x to 7.04x. To defend against this attack, we propose CONCERT, a targeted defense needing no content detector or poison labels. It flags suppliers selected far more often than chance allows, then re-selects under the same budget, keeping only records that two dissimilar selectors both rank highly. On a Qwen3-32B victim, CONCERT reverses the poison concentration from 6.67x to 0x (code) and 3.59x to 0.67x (facts), and reduces downstream harm by 100% and 75% respectively, at unchanged capability.

papers.title: A Little Red Dot emerging from a nitrogen-rich UV-luminous galaxy with Very Massive Stars
papers.abstract: JWST is revealing abundant populations of high-$z$ galaxies with unforeseen properties: UV-luminous galaxies with high nitrogen enrichment, populations of very massive stars (VMSs; $>100\ M_\odot$), and early forms of massive black hole growth such as the Little Red Dots (LRDs). Here we present all these phenomena appearing simultaneously in COLA1, a luminous ($M_{\rm UV}=-21.3$) galaxy at $z=6.6$. New NIRSpec medium-resolution data reveal a blue UV continuum ($β_{\rm UV}=-2.5$) with strong emission lines including NIV] $\lambda1486$, stellar P Cygni profiles, and broad HeII $\lambda1640$. We fit the UV with stellar population models, and find that the models including VMSs (limited to $300\ M_\odot$) are statistically preferred. The best-fit stellar population has $M_*\approx10^8\ M_\odot$, and a young age of $2.4\pm0.8$ Myr. The rest-optical shows a redder continuum ($β_{\rm opt}=-1.1$) and broad Balmer lines with Balmer absorption akin to LRD spectra. By evolving the best-fit stellar population we find that the UV could dim by 1-2 mag in $\sim5$ Myr, and hence this system would be observed as a typical V-shaped LRD. We measure a supersolar $\rm log_{10}(N/O)=-0.07\pm0.05$ and subsolar $\rm log_{10}(C/O)=-0.64\pm0.11$; therefore $\rm log_{10}(N/C)=+0.58\pm0.12$. The independent density-sensitive NIV] $λ\lambda1483,1486$ and CIII] $λ\lambda1906/1909$ ratios require two zones with $n_e\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ and $n_e\lesssim10^{3.5}$ cm$^{-3}$, respectively. We estimate $\rm log_{10}(N/C)>1.3$ (2$σ$) for the dense zone, requiring extreme N/C enrichment mechanisms such as highly rotating $>100\ M_\odot$ VMSs, tidal disruption events, or supermassive stars. We speculate that runaway collisions of massive stars in a dense stellar cluster may have lead to the seeding of an intermediate-mass black hole resulting in the formation of an LRD.

papers.title: Competitive Lotka-Volterra systems with random catastrophes: invasion fitnesses and reversal of the competitive hierarchy
papers.abstract: We study a two-type individual-based population with logistic competition subject to random catastrophes: at the epochs of a Poisson process, each individual survives independently with a random, type-dependent probability. In the large-population limit, the process converges to a competitive Lotka-Volterra system perturbed by multiplicative jumps. We show that the long-time behaviour of this system -exclusion of one type or the other, or coexistence -is governed by two averaged invasion fitnesses, obtained from the classical ones by replacing each growth rate a i with its average {ā}i = a i + rE[ln $Θ$ (i) ], where r is the catastrophe rate and $Θ$ (i) is the survival probability of an individual of type i when a catastrophe occurs. A consequence is that catastrophes can reverse the competitive hierarchy: a type doomed to exclusion in the deterministic system may persist or even exclude its competitor, when catastrophes are frequent enough, even if each catastrophe is individually more harmful to it. In the finite population setting, we also study the invasion of a mutant on the time scale ln K, where K is a scaling parameter, through a coupling with branching processes in the varying random environment generated by the resident population.

papers.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
papers.abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].

papers.title: DynaCI: Generating GitHub Actions Workflows via Dynamic Analysis
papers.abstract: Continuous Integration (CI) is an essential practice that automatically validates code changes through builds and tests. However, configuring CI workflows remains challenging, as modern software often features complex architectures, numerous dependencies, and support for diverse execution environments. Most CI platforms also require workflows to be written in their particular domain-specific languages. As a result, CI workflows are often error-prone and hard to maintain, especially for those unfamiliar with CI semantics. Prior work on automated CI workflow generation require developers to create specifications that describe their intended workflows using natural language, partial workflows, etc. However, in practice, developers may struggle to articulate requirements and may be unaware of available CI features. To address these limitations, we propose DynaCI, a novel approach that uses runtime information from developers' local environments to generate CI workflows. DynaCI (i) traces the developers' local environment to collect runtime information, (ii) constructs an initial workflow by applying runtime-informed heuristics, and (iii) iteratively refines the workflow via LLM-based Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). We evaluate DynaCI on 50 popular Python projects that use GitHub Actions, a popular CI platform, and compare it against the state-of-the-art CI workflow generation approaches: GH-WCOM and LLM4GW. DynaCI outperforms these existing approaches by more than 21.13% in BLEU score and 20.96% in F1 score on average. It also generates workflows without missing functionality in 56% of cases, while requiring fewer manual modifications to repair such exceptions. These results demonstrate that leveraging runtime information substantially improves LLM-based CI workflow generation, and offer a promising direction for broader DevOps configuration automation.

papers.title: On complete Ricci--flat Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat Kähler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no Kähler compactification.

papers.title: Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. We show that the observed sublinear growth is to be attributed in large part to the enhanced reflection and reduced penetration depth of the pump field at high fluences. When taking into account these findings, we confirm the original interpretation of a light-induced superconducting state both qualitatively and quantitatively.

papers.title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
papers.abstract: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

papers.title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
papers.abstract: The random hypergraph process starts with an empty hypergraph on $n$ vertices and adds a uniformly chosen missing edge at each step. For even $n$, we prove that, with high probability, a $3$-uniform loose Hamilton cycle appears when the last isolated vertex disappears. The approach developed here adapts arguments from Kahn's work on perfect matchings. It can also be extended to obtain the corresponding hitting-time theorems for $r=2$ and every fixed $r\ge4$ satisfying $(r-1)\mid n$. Furthermore, it can be used to estimate the numbers of loose Hamilton cycles at these hitting times for every fixed $r\ge2$, up to a factor of $\exp\{o(n)\}$.

papers.title: Conformer diversity over quantity in COSMO-RS-based LLE predictions
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of phase equilibria is essential for chemical process design, particularly in systems characterized by complex intermolecular interactions. This work investigates the influence of conformer selection and sigma-profile characteristics on COSMO-RS predictions of liquid-liquid equilibria (LLE), using the tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA)-methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK)-water system as a case study. Calculations were performed at the TZVP and TZVPD-FINE levels of theory. While TZVP failed to capture the experimentally observed phase behavior, TZVPD-FINE provided substantially improved predictions. The differences are attributed to the relative importance assigned to less-polar conformers and more-polar conformers capable of hydrogen bonding. Although the TZVPD-FINE calculations reproduced the main experimental trends, the predicted organic-phase composition showed a mean percentage deviation of 5.27%, slightly exceeding the adopted 5% agreement threshold. Investigations using individual conformers demonstrated that predictions can be strongly influenced by conformer selection and that representative conformer ensembles are necessary for reliable results. Further analysis showed that diversity in sigma profiles is more important for predictive accuracy than the total number of conformers. These findings emphasize the importance of carefully selecting conformers when applying COSMO-RS to liquid-liquid equilibria involving phases of contrasting polarity.

papers.title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing machine learning (ML) methods for extracting materials data and, where possible, materials knowledge directly from the scientific literature. This review traces the evolution of these methods from heuristic, rule-based pipelines through natural language processing (NLP) models and transformer-based encoders to, lastly, large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems capable of extracting materials information across multiple modalities, including text, tables, and figures. Beside construction of large, queryable materials databases and knowledge graphs that support downstream materials discovery, we discuss how these advances have enabled new capabilities, such as, generic question answering across materials science, AI co-scientists and chatbots for research assistance, and closed-loop optimization and discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories. We critically assess the datasets generated using these approaches, their extraction accuracy and computational costs, and the respective strengths and limitations of different methodologies, and even provide practical guidelines for developing more reliable and scalable materials data extraction pipelines. Finally, we identify key open challenges, including the extraction of full materials structure-property-processing-performance tetrahedron at the sample level, the scarcity of reliable benchmark datasets for systematic evaluation, and the resolution of non-standard materials terminology across different document modalities.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of Learner Errors on Social Bias in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Existing social bias benchmarks evaluate large language models mostly on fluent, well-formed English, reflecting native speaker usage and leaving non-native writers unrepresented. To address this gap, we investigate how grammatical errors by non-native writers affect social bias. We develop a controlled framework that injects common learner errors into prompts and apply it to three bias benchmarks covering stereotype alignment and demographic preference across gender, race, and religion. We find that grammatical errors increase bias, and the effect grows with the error rate. Among the four common error types we consider, preposition errors produce the largest and most consistent increase in stereotype alignment. Our analysis suggests that errors increase bias when they are more likely to interfere with comprehension. Finally, fine-tuning on erroneous texts reduces the bias increase caused by grammatical errors. Our findings show that bias evaluations based exclusively on well-formed prompts may underestimate the bias experienced by users whose English contains grammatical errors.

papers.title: Observability Inequality for a Multi-Dimensional Degenerate Schrödinger Equation with an Interior Degeneracy Point
papers.abstract: We study the observability inequality for a multi-dimensional degenerate Schrödinger equation possessing an interior degeneracy point, where the principal coefficient vanishes at the origin inside the domain and breaks ellipticity. Within a weighted Sobolev space, we establish the spectral properties, well-posedness, and regularity estimates for the degenerate operator. To tackle the failure of classical controllability tools, we develop a regularization approximation scheme. We construct a sequence of non-degenerate approximating problems. We then establish uniform a-priori estimates and solution convergence. Furthermore, we derive an observability inequality for the regularized problems and pass to the limit. This yields a non-standard observability inequality for the original degenerate equation for sufficiently large observation time, which quantifies the influence of the degeneracy strength on the observation time. Crucially, we establish the precise parameter restriction $3α+ N > 4$ to ensure that every test function in $C_0^\infty(Ω)$ belongs to $D(\mathcal A^{\frac 32})$.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.abstract: Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/δ)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$. For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/δ)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.

papers.title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
papers.abstract: This experimental study demonstrates MHz-order acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a compact through-hole lithium niobate thickness-mode transducer integrated at the nozzle exit and driven near its 6.7 MHz resonance. Jet dynamics were measured by high-speed shadowgraphy at 50,000 fps, and breakup lengths were obtained from instantaneous jet-length records using an autocorrelation-based method that identifies statistically separated breakup events. Acoustic actuation produced visible interfacial corrugations and reduced the normalized breakup length, $L_b/d$, for both water and glycerol--water jets. In water, the response was threshold-like at low Weber number and weakened as the jet velocity increased to We ~ 50. A reduced-order threshold correlation, fit to the water amplitude and velocity sweeps, captured this abrupt shortening and the subsequent loss of actuation efficacy. More viscous glycerol--water mixtures shortened immediately at low forcing, indicating a distinct acoustic-coupling regime rather than a universal collapse of the water response. A wetting-control experiment showed that liquid spreading at the nozzle base can also shorten the jet, so the measured response reflects coupled radiation-pressure forcing, capillary-wave feedback, and wetting-mediated disturbance injection. Resolved droplet tracking further showed that MHz excitation changes the visible gate-crossing droplet population, although sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured. These results establish through-hole MHz actuation as a compact route for modifying free-surface jet breakup and provide a repeatable image-analysis protocol for experimental-fluid-mechanics measurements.

papers.title: In search of the third dimension in Compton X-ray polarimeters
papers.abstract: Compton polarimeters are typically designed to be sensitive only to the azimuthal angle of the scattered photon, ignoring the scattering angle. Such a 2-dimensional reconstruction of the event is pursued for both simplicity and because the polarization of the incident photon influences only the azimuthal response of the instrument. While this is true for on-axis sources, when the source starts to be off-axis of several degrees the azimuthal response of the instrument is effectively a convolution of the azimuthal and polar scattering angles: measuring the latter would provide a better sensitivity and smaller systematic effects. In this contribution, we will present a design which allows to estimate the scattering angle in a Compton polarimeter through the read-out of the light signal at the two ends of scintillator bars. Such a design is being tested with a representative set-up and first results on the performance are presented.

papers.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
papers.abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

papers.title: Morphological instability and negative geometric friction from contact with active and driven particles
papers.abstract: Overdamped particles on a deformable substrate induce a geometric friction through their response to metric perturbations. Nonequilibrium dynamics couples such a perturbation to kinetic effects, which can flip that friction negative, softening the substrate's rigidity and favoring invaginations and evaginations. A breathing circle, with local curvature radius as dynamical variable, is the main example. At equilibrium the friction reduces to an ordinary potential response and stays positive. Geometric response emerges as a new route by which active and driven matter reshape their environment.

papers.title: Relaxation and $Γ$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $Γ$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.

papers.title: HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking
papers.abstract: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.

papers.title: Kelly's conjectures on Condorcet winner probabilities for odd electorates
papers.abstract: Let $C(m,n)$ denote the probability that, among $n$ independent uniformly random permutations of $m$ labels, there exists a label that precedes every other label in a strict majority of the permutations. We prove that $C(m,n)>C(m,n+2)$ for $m \ge 3$ and odd $n \ge 1$, and that $C(m,n)>C(m+1,n)$ for $m \ge 2$ and odd $n \ge 3$. These results establish Kelly's two monotonicity conjectures for odd electorates. The proofs use integral representations involving probabilities associated with sums of independent Bernoulli random variables.

papers.title: ViBMR: A Large-Scale Multi-Sequence Brain MRI Dataset and Comprehensive Evaluation for Vietnamese Radiology Report Generation
papers.abstract: Automated radiology report generation for multi-sequence brain MRI holds strong promise for alleviating radiologists' workload, yet it remains a demanding problem: brain MRI studies are inherently volumetric, each pulse sequence carries complementary diagnostic information, and annotated data are critically scarce for low-resource clinical languages. Existing brain MRI-report resources are still dominated by English reports, translated clinical text, or datasets adapted from task-specific imaging benchmarks, leaving routine low-resource clinical reporting and heterogeneous multi-sequence MRI protocols insufficiently represented. To bridge this gap, we introduce ViBMR, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale multi-sequence brain MRI dataset paired with routine Vietnamese clinical reports, comprising 3,649 patients and 11,875 MRI series across T1, T2, FLAIR, and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences. Building on ViBMR, we establish a comprehensive evaluation setup for brain MRI report generation, covering representative medical vision-language models, multi-sequence inputs, and feature aggregation strategies. The results provide key insights into dataset characteristics and model behavior, while demonstrating the necessity of native low-resource clinical datasets for reliable Vietnamese-origin brain MRI report generation. Our dataset and baseline models will be released for non-commercial research.

papers.title: AI Mindmeld: A Latent Interconnect Protocol
papers.abstract: LLMs can act as scientific agents using tools to consult specialists and run experiments. Yet specialist information must enter their context, generally as text, images, audio or video: a bottleneck between models with rich, high-dimensional representations. We advocate direct representation exchange: a mindmeld conveying many properties, including information an LLM would not think to request. It should be extensible to new specialists, flexible across questions and tasks, and compositional across independently connected specialists without joint training. The Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP) learns connectors mapping specialist representations into LLM internal states. Training only connectors keeps this practical as LLMs grow and evolve. We connect three protein and three small molecule specialists to Gemma 3 (4B and 12B parameters) and Kimi K2.6 (1T total, 32B active), freezing all pretrained models. Independently trained connectors provide useful information without changing the LLM or existing connectors, supporting familiar and new question types about unseen objects. We demonstrate zero-shot transfer to cross-domain tasks without joint training. Task performance and compositionality generally improve with LLM capability, with especially strong gains in zero-shot task transfer. Limitations remain: current LLMs were not trained for specialist representations as native inputs; access does not ensure reliable interpretation, integration or use in reasoning. We call on specialist developers to provide consistent representation interfaces and, especially, on LLM developers to train models to receive, combine and reason with these inputs. These efforts could expand scientific agents' information while preserving conventional tools' flexibility. Data, pretrained connectors, and code for training, evaluation and interactive inference: https://github.com/PolymathicAI/AI-Mindmeld

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
papers.abstract: We propose a reinforcement learning framework for solving control problems on dynamic networks, where control decisions consist of a combination of graph-level (global) and node-level (local) actions. To exploit the underlying network structure in a policy-gradient algorithm, we introduce a message-passing neural network architecture with separate global and local policy heads. The architecture ensures that the resulting policies satisfy natural permutation symmetries and transparency constraints. Our main theoretical contribution is an analysis of the robustness and regularity properties of the proposed architecture. We derive explicit Lipschitz bounds with respect to both parameter and input perturbations and use these estimates to establish convergence guarantees for a projected policy-gradient algorithm. The resulting constants reveal how architectural choices and graph characteristics influence sensitivity to input perturbations and the convergence behavior of gradient-based optimization methods. As an application, we study the management of systemic risk in financial networks, where a regulator allocates capital interventions across interconnected institutions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed reinforcement learning architecture outperforms standard architectures based on feedforward neural networks while the learned policies fulfill desirable symmetry and transparency constraints. The algorithm scales to large networks and effectively combines global budget decisions with local allocation policies by exploiting the underlying graph structure.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Detecting Satirical Code-Mixed Sentences
papers.abstract: Code-switching is a natural linguistic phenomenon, yet its impact on high-level reasoning tasks remains largely unexplored in under-resourced languages like Romanian. Natural language processing tasks, such as satire detection, rely heavily on nuanced cultural and syntactic cues that large language models struggle to capture. In this paper, we investigate four methods (i.e., random replacement, phrase translation, dependency parsing, and large language models) for generating synthetic code-mixed Romanian sentences with English, German, French, and Italian. We start with an existing dataset for satire detection, compiled from Romanian news articles and annotated at the sentence level by humans, and augment it with over 600k samples, namely CS-SeLeRoSa. We provide an in-depth analysis of the dataset generation process. Then, we evaluate several multilingual large language models across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and fine-tuning regimes on both the synthetic corpus and a human-adjudicated gold benchmark, namely CS-SeLeRoSa-Gold. While older open models suffer substantial degradation (dropping to 37%-55% macro-F1), newer models like Gemma 4 31B achieve 68.1% zero-shot, rivaling frontier models like GPT-5 mini (69.5%). Furthermore, fine-tuning significantly reduces formatting errors and improves the results, increasing Gemma 4 31B to 77.5% on CS-SeLeRoSa and 72.6% on the gold standard, outperforming frontier zero-shot baselines.

papers.title: Testing Dynamical Dark-Energy Model with Standard Sirens
papers.abstract: Bright standard sirens from the Einstein Telescope (ET) provide an independent probe of cosmic expansion. In this article, we test whether future ET observations can constrain a dynamical dark-energy scenario inspired by DESI DR2. Using the best-fitting 29-bin dark-energy equation of state as the fiducial cosmology, we generate mock catalogs of 100, 500, 1000, and 3000 binary-neutron-star standard sirens with known host redshifts, and reconstruct the equation of state using both GW-only data and combined analyses with DESI DR2 BAO, BBN, and a compressed CMB constraint. The effective numbers of constrained modes are $N_{\mathrm{eff}}\sim 4-5$ (GW-only) and $5-6$ (combined), with information concentrated in a few correlated modes. The GW3000 catalog yields a departure from $Λ$CDM exceeding $5σ$, and combined analyses reach similar significance for $O(10^3)$ events. Comparing flat $Λ$CDM with its Chevallier-Polarski-Linder extension using GW data alone gives significances of $3.3σ$ and $6.3σ$ for 1000 and 3000 events, rising to $7.7σ$ and $11.0σ$ with external data. These results indicate that a few thousand ET bright standard sirens could provide a sensitive test of departures from $Λ$CDM.

papers.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schrödinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.

papers.title: Worst-Case Finite-Horizon Analysis of Perturbed LQR via Performance Estimation Problem
papers.abstract: We propose a framework to assess the robustness of a given state-feedback controller by evaluating its worst-case finite-horizon cost over a class of norm-bounded perturbations. To compute this cost, we show how to apply the Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) framework, originally developed to analyze optimization algorithms, and reformulate the worst-case search as a rank-constrained Semidefinite Program (SDP). Our results suggest that the perturbations that induce the highest finite-horizon costs can differ substantially from those identified using standard asymptotic metrics. Intuitively, worst-case perturbations are obtained by aligning slowly decaying modes with specific initial conditions to drive transient growth, causing a bifurcation in the worst-case behavior as the horizon length changes. These findings open new possibilities to certify finite-horizon performance of broader system classes, including data-driven models or nonlinear components.

papers.title: Lean-QuantumAlg: A Framework for AI Agents to Produce Quantum Algorithms that Humans Can Trust
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly capable of constructing quantum algorithms and proofs, yet machine-checked proofs alone cannot guarantee that the intended problem is solved or that resource claims match the verified computation. Here we introduce Lean-QuantumAlg, a Lean 4 framework for trustworthy AI-assisted development of quantum algorithms. Its Algorithm-Solves-Problem contract binds correctness, success probability, borrowed-state restoration and quantum and classical resource bounds to a single execution, while separating the guarantees that Lean checks from the problem specifications and execution models that humans review. We demonstrate the framework on nine AI-formalized quantum algorithms, from Grover search to quantum attacks on RSA-2048 and P-256, with less than 1% of each algorithm's imported source code requiring statement-level human review once the shared framework has been audited. By integrating reusable mathematical foundations, certified algorithmic primitives and execution-grounded verification, Lean-QuantumAlg provides a basis for AI agents to construct and certify quantum algorithms, opening a path toward scalable AI-driven discovery of quantum algorithms.

papers.title: Squarefree values of random polynomials are Gaussian mixtures
papers.abstract: Fix $d\ge1$ and choose a polynomial $P$ uniformly at random from the set of integer polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients have absolute value at most $H$. We study $E_{P}$, the error in the count of squarefree values $P(n)$ for $n\leq x$. In the range $x=H^{o\left(1\right)}$, we prove that $E_{P}\left(x\right)/x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ converges to a Gaussian mixture that is not itself Gaussian, $\sqrt{C\left(G\right)}Z$, where $G$ is the weak limit, as $H\rightarrow\infty$, of the prime-indexed vector $\left(P\bmod p^{2}\right)_{p}$, $C$ is a nonnegative function and $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian. This answers a question of Sofos. Finally, in the appendix, we establish that $\log \mathbb{E}[C(G)^m]\asymp_d m^2/(\log m)^2$ as $m\to\infty$.

papers.title: Derived categories of threefolds near the Noether line
papers.abstract: We show that derived categories of canonical stacks associated to general threefolds in the principal component of the moduli space of canonical threefolds on the refined Noether line are semiorthogonally indecomposable. First we generalize a criterion of Kawatani-Okawa for the indecomposability of derived categories of surfaces of general type to higher-dimensional varieties and stacks. And then we generalize a construction of Kobayashi and Hu-Zhang and a classification result of Coughlan-Pignatelli to the second and third Noether lines to show that our criterion applies to these canonical stacks.

papers.title: Asking a Multimodal LLM Whether Someone Fell: Zero-Shot Screening of Low-Resolution Thermal Video in a Laboratory and an Occupied Home
papers.abstract: Thermal cameras can watch over older people living alone without capturing faces, and multimodal large language models (LLMs) can judge a short video without task-specific training. We evaluate a production multimodal LLM, Gemini 3.8 Flash at temperature 0, as the decision stage of an event-triggered fall screener, used exactly as a deployed prototype uses it: one request per short thermal clip, with its sound track when there is one, and its predecessor Gemini 3.7 Flash on the same requests. On 438 staged falls and 563 non-fall windows that we located by hand in a public 32x24 thermal dataset, the deployed request called 69% of the held-out subjects' falls (67% over all subjects; bed falls excluded) and none of 499 non-fall windows, including people lying on the floor and getting up. Over 76 h of ordinary life in an occupied room, recorded at 160x120 with sound, it called none of 395 clips a fall (95% upper bound 1.2 false alarms per day) and caught 4 of the 9 staged falls the camera could see. One cautionary sentence in the prompt ("a person who goes out of view ... is not a fall") accounted for many of the misses: removing it raised sensitivity on the held-out subjects from 69% to 83% on 3.8 Flash and from 80% to 92% on Gemini 3.7 Flash, and in the home from 4 to 9 of the 9 visible falls, with no false call in ordinary living but at the price of calling deliberate lie-downs a fall. Sensitivity collapsed at 8x6 pixels (34%); identical requests disagreed on 4% of windows; and when the model called a fall, its explanation placed it within a second of the annotated landing 99% of the time. Two conventional detectors trained on the laboratory data caught nearly every held-out laboratory fall but raised 14.2 and 23.9 false alarms per day in the home. We release the frame-level fall annotations of the public dataset and every model answer on it.

papers.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.

papers.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.

papers.title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

papers.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.

papers.title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization
papers.abstract: Consider a contextual linear optimization problem, where a predict-then-optimize (PTO) system returns optimal decisions without revealing the cost vectors used in its downstream linear program. Our focus is on how to prevent attackers, who can submit context queries, from extracting the underlying prediction model. Although the cost-to-decision map is many-to-one, observations across contexts can reveal the underlying prediction model. For linear models, we provide sufficient conditions where the attacker can learn the model up to positive scaling by only observing the decision. These conditions motivate an adaptive attack that alternates inverse optimization with boundary sampling, i.e., using context queries leading to decision boundaries of the current attacker model. To prevent extraction, we propose a mechanism that perturbs decisions only when the predicted cost vector is near a decision boundary. We establish a regret bound in terms of the perturbation radius. For the attackers that fit the defended responses as optimal decisions under the evaluation distribution, we also prove a lower bound on expected extraction error. Experiments on synthetic instances and real data quantify the security-performance trade-off of the defense mechanism and illustrate that our defense can increase the extraction error.

papers.title: Resource Analysis of Quantum Optimization Algorithms via Variational Methods
papers.abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are promising approaches for solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices. However, the role played by quantum resources such as entanglement and coherence during the optimization process remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the evolution of these resources in two VQAs--the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON)--applied to the Minimum Vertex Cover problem. We employ a variational resource-quantification framework based on the Bures metric and Uhlmann's theorem, in which an auxiliary quantum circuit is optimized to identify the closest resource-free states. This approach allows us to quantify Bures entanglement and Bures coherence of the algorithmic states without requiring full quantum state tomography. For the considered problem instance, QAOA exhibits a pronounced accumulation of entanglement in its initial layers, followed by a progressive reduction as the algorithm converges toward the optimal solution. Its coherence likewise decreases overall with increasing circuit depth, although a finite residual value persists due to the degeneracy of the optimal-solution subspace. In contrast, FALQON exhibits a substantially lower entanglement peak, reached at larger circuit depth, followed by a decay as convergence proceeds. Its coherence decreases smoothly and monotonically together with the optimization error. These results reveal distinct quantum-resource trajectories associated with the two optimization strategies and illustrate how entanglement and coherence evolve as variational quantum states approach solutions of a classical combinatorial optimization problem.

papers.title: In-orbit anomaly and recovery of IXPE detector 2
papers.abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) is a joint NASA-ASI mission launched in December 2021 to measure the linear polarization of celestial X-ray sources in the 2-8 keV energy range. The payload comprises three identical telescopes, each combining grazing-incidence X-ray optics with a focal-plane photoelectric polarimeter based on the Gas Pixel Detector technology. On 14 April 2025, the second detector experienced an anomaly that significantly altered the electrical behavior of the ASIC responsible for reading out the photoelectron track images. In this contribution, we describe the effect of the anomaly on the instrumental response and the actions taken to mitigate its effects and recover the scientific observations of the instrument.

papers.title: Exact nonsymmetric vacuum magnetic field with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform
papers.abstract: We show that an exact vacuum magnetic field without continuous Euclidean symmetry can fill a bounded solid torus with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform. We construct such a field in closed form and show that it is nowhere vanishing. Every off-axis field line closes after one toroidal transit and one poloidal turn, with rotational transform $ι=-1$ on every flux surface. The solution provides an exact benchmark for three-dimensional equilibrium codes.

papers.title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs
papers.abstract: As LLMs are increasingly deployed in value-sensitive contexts, aligning them with human values has emerged as a post-training objective in NLP, aimed at instilling additional values and guiding model behaviour. However, current evaluations remain narrow. Because values are interconnected, it is unclear how fine-tuning for specific values alters unrelated capabilities and behaviours. In this work, we adapt four instruction-tuned LLMs across individual Hofstede's value dimensions and evaluate them on both cross-value transfer and broader behaviours. We find that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits. Consequently, we suggest that value alignment after post-training should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations, and we highlight the need to investigate where additional value training might best fit into the pipeline.

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Observations using Coincident Scintillator and Radio Signals with the Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON)
papers.abstract: At energies above 100 PeV, coherent radio frequency (RF) emission across the 10 -- 1000 MHz band from cosmic particle-induced atmospheric showers becomes increasingly dominant, making radio detection a powerful probe at ultrahigh energies. The Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON) considers mountaintop phased radio arrays to monitor large areas at the horizon for upward-going geomagnetic emission in the 30 -- 80 MHz band produced as a consequence of Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. As part of ongoing efforts to measure the sensitivity of BEACON to such signals, the BEACON prototype identifies cosmic rays through the same emission mechanism. Prior to 2023, BEACON operated a four-antenna prototype, which successfully demonstrated identification of coherent and impulsive sources using a beamforming RF trigger. In 2023, we upgraded the instrument to six newly designed antennas and added an independent scintillator array to cross-validate radio-detectable cosmic rays. This work details the observation of 22 candidate cosmic-ray events in a scintillator-coincidence-triggered dataset using selection cuts based on expected radio characteristics. A simulation of the hybrid-instrument performance verifies this observation rate to within an order of magnitude. We estimate a background of 0.11 events by applying the selection cuts to synthetic datasets of uncorrelated radio-scintillator pairs that are randomly formed using fixed-rate software-triggered data. The reconstructed signal polarization angles are consistent with pure geomagnetic emission compared to various background classes.

papers.title: Geospatial Dynamics of Online Attention to Nuclear Power in Japan Before and After Fukushima
papers.abstract: Nuclear power is increasingly seen as necessary for sustainable development, but this role depends on informed public engagement and support. Building this support requires understanding what citizens want to know, as reflected in their spontaneous online searches. To map this demand, we present the first long-term (2004-2024), prefecture-level analysis of Google Trends data on nuclear power in Japan. The results indicate that in routine periods, search interest followed a host-locality pattern, being significantly higher in prefectures hosting nuclear plants, with little spillover to their neighbors. Immediately after the Fukushima Daiichi accident in March 2011, this pattern changed, and interest instead declined with distance from Fukushima, before the host-locality pattern returned from 2012. During March 2011, searches leaned heavily toward general and live information rather than guidance on what to do. Their framing also varied with proximity, as those near Fukushima prioritized live updates and formal countermeasures, while others leaned toward background information and personal-scale questions. These patterns and the shift between them provide a behavioral evidence base for designing communication strategies in Japan and countries weighing the use of nuclear power. More broadly, the finding that searches vary with proximity can inform public communication in other geographically anchored crises.

papers.title: Privacy in Context Is Being Overlooked in the Age of General-Purpose LLMs
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) continue to grow in scope and capability, privacy concerns are on the rise. Since users increasingly interact with a single general-purpose system across many distinct contexts, there is a natural tendency to pursue a one-size-fits-all solution to privacy. Unfortunately, this overlooks a crucial insight from decades of privacy research: privacy is inherently contextual. In this paper, we argue that existing work in prompt privacy is drifting towards attempts to design a unified framework, which is highly misleading and can foster a false sense of security. Furthermore, we argue that even future work in this direction needs to wrestle with fundamental tensions across various desirable properties of prompt privacy. Thus, such continued attempts towards a unified framework need to be reconsidered. We recommend three critical paths forward: application-specific deployment of LLMs, context-specific evaluation of privacy frameworks, and better privacy literacy.

papers.title: Task-Preserving Multilingual Instruction Tuning for Open-Ended QA in WMT 2026 MIST
papers.abstract: This paper describes our submission to the WMT 2026 Multilingual Instruction Shared Task. We adapt Qwen3-8B with LoRA using organiser-provided data, EuroAlpaca, a multilingual instruction dataset created through task-preserving localisation, and CrossEuroAlpaca, a cross-lingual augmentation that assigns different source and target languages to instructions, contexts and responses. Our system targets open-ended question answering (QA-OEG) in ten shared-task languages represented in the auxiliary data. Under matched decoding, adaptation improves the mean Gemma-4 judge score on target-language QA-OEG by 7.8% relative to the base model. On an additional evaluation using the Aya Evaluation Suite across all shared-task languages, it yields relative gains of 41.5% in macro-averaged ROUGE-L and 2.9% in BERTScore-F1, with larger improvements in target languages. However, these gains are task- and language-specific. Gemma-4 scores improve for QA-OEG and summarisation in the target languages but decline for context-grounded QA there and across all three tasks in the non-target languages.

papers.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
papers.abstract: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful localized training progress. We propose two diagnostic metrics that capture these two failure modes and provide rigorous theoretical guarantees. Empirically, we analyze 25 popular benchmarks spanning 7 domains using carefully estimated item difficulties. Our results show that many benchmarks implicitly overweight certain difficulty regions, so their leaderboard conclusions should be interpreted with caution; others leave substantial portions of the difficulty axis uncovered, limiting their ability to monitor the model improvement process. Finally, we turn diagnosis into action by introducing BenchFill, a simple difficulty-targeted item rewriting algorithm that effectively reduces local coverage gaps.

papers.title: The medium is the message: How neurometabolic entanglement generates conscious experience
