papers.abstract: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. Five paired conditions assess perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, and intent understanding for navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks. Our evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult. Frequent collisions and falls further motivate evaluating execution safety alongside task success, even with a shared action interface and decision budget.

papers.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.

papers.title: Which Differences Matter? Controlled Tests of Rule Transfer, Joint Reliability, and Information Use in Decision Models
papers.abstract: Decision models map stated rules and observed states to discrete answers. Aggregate accuracy leaves unresolved which rule and information changes guide those answers. We connect controlled input changes to transfer, joint reliability, and directed information use through executable arithmetic rules. Semantic rule separation and crossed rule and state tests make transfer and joint success separately measurable. We compare equivalent wordings, calibrate joint correctness through marginal-preserving reassociation, and alter tables to define alternative answer targets. Adaptation gains increase with nearest-source answer agreement; fully conflicting quartets yield small pooled gains and different gain signs across source splits. Equivalent rewrites have opposing task-level effects, linking transfer gains to rule presentation. Joint-score departures depend on which rule and state associations the reference preserves. A decision service changes answers more across equivalent wordings than across identical-text repeats and usually follows the answer targets implied by altered table values or mappings.

papers.title: Relative geometry of nuclear mean fields through differential forms
papers.abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. A pair invariant measures the angle between two density gradients, weighted by their magnitudes, and the coarea formula resolves its contribution over level surfaces. A triple invariant factorizes exactly into a weighted pair term and a directional term that measures the variation of a third field along the level-surface intersections. We test these quantities in 98 magnetized Wigner-Seitz solutions, five static Hartree-Fock configurations, an illustrative $^{16}$O + $^{34}$Mg collision, and periodic nuclear pasta (a slab and a connected network). The pair invariant distinguishes cell solutions with comparable proton quadrupole moments and is 253 times larger in $^{34}$Mg than in $^{24}$Mg; refinement to 0.6 fm changes it by at most 1.3% in the four configurations recomputed. The directional factor separates the sampled triaxial configurations from the prolate ones. In the collision, it accounts for the 7.3-fold rise of the triple before the first recorded low-density connection, while the weighted pair term changes by at most 3%. In nuclear pasta, slab and network configurations have similar integrated proton-neutron misalignment but different distributions over density levels; their triple invariants differ by a factor of about 370 on the finer grid, mainly due to the variation of the Coulomb potential along joint density levels. These comparisons require no preferred origin or axis. A resolved nonzero triple excludes a common symmetry axis, but zero does not establish one. The pasta results require further convergence studies.

papers.title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
papers.abstract: Coding agents are typically evaluated using one-shot, well-formulated prompts. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench use existing GitHub issues as input for a coding agent and evaluate whether the agent successfully solves the task. However, in real-world use cases, prompts are often not as well-formulated or structured as existing GitHub issues. Additionally, a coding agent session is not limited to a single prompt; it typically involves a multi-turn interaction in which the user iteratively adds new tasks and requirements that the agent must fulfill. To benchmark these abilities, we developed SWE-DIVE, a dynamic, interactive validation and evaluation framework for benchmarking coding agents in a multi-turn environment. To achieve this, we introduce a user simulator that can simulate different behavioral patterns and communicate with the coding agent. We also introduce a conversation validator that evaluates the user simulator's outputs to determine whether they fulfill the initial requirements and guide the agent toward successfully solving the task. The entire framework is embedded in a Harbor environment, which orchestrates the coding agent, user simulator, and conversation validator, and executes the test environment to determine whether the agent successfully solves the task. Our results and source code are available in our GitHub repository (https://github.com/lorenzbrehme/swe-dive_usersim).

papers.title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-$1/2$: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
papers.abstract: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-$1/2$ models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-$1$ or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin $S$. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(1)$, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$; the latter has no spin-$1/2$ counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric $\mathrm{U}(1)$ state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of $2S+1$. We apply the formalism to the spin-$1$ diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped $\mathrm{U}(1)$ states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.

papers.title: Exceptional points and hysteresis in Kerr-Newman quasi-normal modes
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) and eigenstate hysteresis, previously found in Kerr only with an auxiliary scalar field, arise intrinsically in the quasinormal-mode spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. Using a hyperboloidal formulation of the coupled gravito-electromagnetic Teukolsky equations and a Chebyshev pseudospectral method, we compute the $\ell=m=2$ spectrum and locate four EPs at up to $99.974\%$ of extremality, one from a new repulsion. The gaps close as a square root branch point, and quasistatic loops around one or more EPs exchange the coalescing modes, confirming hysteresis.

papers.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
papers.abstract: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.

papers.title: How Prompt Style Affects AI Accuracy and Speed in Competitive Programming
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in competitive programming, and their outputs are sensitive to how a prompt is phrased. Prior work has compared prompt strategies for accuracy on competitive programming, but not for runtime speed, and has not situated the results against human performance. In an exploratory study of one prompt in each of nine styles on GPT-5.5 across three accuracy tasks from the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) and two NP-hard speed tasks, we found that no single prompt was best: the strongest prompt depended on the task type and on whether results were summarized by the mean or the median, suggesting that, at least for these tasks, prompt style should be matched to the objective rather than treated as universal. Many differences in mean scores came from a few outlier runs, showing that evaluating prompting by a single metric can obscure how much its effectiveness varies. Compared descriptively with human IOI contestants, who worked under different conditions, the AI was neither strictly better nor strictly worse, exceeding the average contestant on one task but falling short on the other two. By extending prompt comparison from accuracy to runtime speed and grounding it against human performance, this study gives a broader picture of how prompt style affects competitive programming performance.

papers.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
papers.abstract: Recent advances in frontier AI models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, planning, and tool use, raising the possibility of using general-purpose AI models for robot manipulation without task-specific training. However, their manipulation capabilities have not been systematically evaluated on standardized robotics benchmarks. In this report, we present a unified closed-loop manipulation framework for evaluating frontier AI models on the LIBERO-10 benchmark. Our framework enables models to control a robot directly through visual observations, robot proprioception, and structured tool calls, primarily by specifying target end-effector poses and gripper commands, without task-specific fine-tuning or pretrained manipulation skills. We evaluate six frontier AI models, including GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini-4 Argon, across three reasoning effort levels, resulting in 18 configurations and 1,800 evaluation episodes. Our results show that GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest success rate of 44%, followed by Gemini-4 Argon at 43%. Increasing reasoning effort generally improves manipulation performance, but the benefits vary across models and come at additional inference cost. We also observe substantial differences across tasks, with models performing relatively well on object placement tasks but struggling with precise spatial arrangements and complex multi-step interactions. These findings demonstrate both the potential and limitations of frontier AI models for robot manipulation, highlighting the challenges of translating reasoning capabilities into reliable physical actions. We release our evaluation framework and experimental results to support reproducible benchmarking and future research on reasoning-based robot manipulation.

papers.title: Tight Bounds on the Randomized Communication Complexity of Vector-in-Subspace
papers.abstract: We prove that the randomized communication complexity of Vector-in-Subspace in $\mathbb R^n$ with error at most $1/3$ is $Θ(\sqrt n)$. Alice holds a unit vector $u$ and Bob holds an $n/2$-dimensional subspace $H$; they must distinguish $u\in H$ from $u\in H^\perp$. An exact one-way quantum protocol uses $O(\log n)$ qubits, making the problem a geometric example of an exponential quantum advantage over interactive classical communication. Our lower bound matches Raz's $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound, improves the $Ω(n^{1/3})$ lower bound of Klartag and Regev, and removes the total-rank restriction in Grupel's $Ω(\sqrt n)$ result. The proof establishes a Gaussian moment bound over complete rectangle partitions. A complex Gaussian representation yields a vanishing even moment whose cancellation is preserved when averaging over the partition. We control the signed conditional moments around a real center by decomposing conditional Gaussian measures into fixed coordinates and sub-Gaussian components. Combining this estimate with spherical harmonic analysis gives the communication lower bound.

papers.title: NLOS-Aware TDOA-Based UAV Localization: Cramér-Rao Bounds, Measurement Modeling, and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract: Passive time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) localization is well suited for tracking non-cooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that do not report their positions. However, its accuracy degrades under the mixed line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation that is typical of low-altitude flight. In this paper, we develop NLOS-aware Cramér--Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) and an empirically calibrated measurement model for TDOA-based UAV localization, and we evaluate both with measurements from five UAV flights on the Aerial Experimentation and Research Platform for Advanced Wireless (AERPAW). The analysis yields an identifiability condition that relates the number of sensors to the number of NLOS links, together with a bias-induced error floor that a wider bandwidth cannot remove. The model parameters are estimated by matching simulated and measured error distributions. Experimental results show that the error depends most strongly on the number of sensors in LOS, while a higher altitude and a wider bandwidth lower the median error. Relocating a sensor that is always in NLOS into the open flight area can lower the median horizontal bound by two orders of magnitude if the relocated sensor is in LOS. The fitted model reproduces the median errors of the 2.5 MHz and 5 MHz flights but underestimates the heaviest error tails. Finally, rejecting outlier fixes lowers the error far more than Kalman or particle filtering, because the remaining error is dominated by bias.

papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $ω_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $ω_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $ω_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $ω_\mathbb{F}$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.

papers.title: A Real-time tax compliance architecture for VAT split payments with Making Tax Smart and Open Banking
papers.abstract: This paper presents Making Tax Smart with Open Banking (MTS-OB), a novel DLT-based architecture designed to integrate real-time VAT compliance into the existing payment system through split payments and Open Banking. Motivated by the substantial VAT gap, the research investigates how leveraging the informational value embedded within payment transactions can reduce the tax administration burden. MTS-OB, a proof-of-concept application built on R3 Corda, facilitates automated, real-time VAT split payments (VSP) without disrupting current payment infrastructure. MTS-OB integrates with existing banking systems via Open Banking APIs, enabling secure information management for VAT collection, reporting, analytics, and automated compliance enforcement. The system uses traditional bank deposit money as a real-time information sensor thereby extending its functionality to include "money as a medium of real-time taxation". Scalability testing demonstrates the system's ability to maintain operational stability under increasing transaction loads, illustrating its potential for real-world deployment. The key finding is the necessity of redefining money to include its informational value for real-time tax compliance, requiring a redesign of the money system while adhering to existing regulations and standards. This research demonstrates the feasibility of integrating tax functionality directly into payments, offering a path towards "hard to get tax wrong" compliance and a potential reduction in the VAT gap without compromising financial stability.

papers.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

papers.title: Differential powers of monomial ideals in affine semigroup rings
papers.abstract: This article gives explicit descriptions for differential powers of monomial ideals in certain (possibly non-normal) affine semigroup rings. We use these descriptions to show that the topologies defined by the ordinary, symbolic, and differential powers of any monomial ideal are all linearly equivalent. We then prove the existence of differential signature in our settings, relating it to the volume of some convex polytope. Finally, we apply our results to pinched Veronese rings.

papers.title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
papers.abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.

papers.title: Validating Autoformalized Specifications via Contrapuntal Languages
papers.abstract: Formal specifications can make AI-generated code mechanically checkable. Because user intent is typically expressed in natural language rather than formal logic, specifications must first be derived from it, e.g., via LLM-based autoformalization. Yet autoformalized specifications are themselves untrusted, so a key challenge is validating whether they capture user intent without relying on a costly oracle such as human review. In this oracle-free setting, a natural strategy is to vote among model outputs, but because model errors are often correlated, agreement among outputs may reflect shared mistakes rather than correctness. Our key insight is that these errors can be decorrelated through representational diversity. We achieve this diversity with contrapuntal languages: pairs of task-specific formal languages, each designed to express the intended specification, yet admitting no structure-preserving translation between them. An LLM formalizes the intent independently in each language, and we accept a specification only if a solver proves the two formalizations equivalent. To construct such languages, we present a synthesis algorithm that reuses fragments of sampled seed specifications as syntactic sugar over a base specification language. We implement the approach for first-order logic specifications and evaluate it on HumanEval+ and LiveCodeBench using GPT-5.4 mini and Qwen3.6-Flash with and without thinking. Over the strongest baseline, our method increases the proportion of accepted specifications that are correct, i.e., complete and sound, by 12.0% on HumanEval+ and 42.9% on LiveCodeBench. The accepted specifications judged complete reject 98.6% of buggy program variants on HumanEval+ and 96.2% on LiveCodeBench, compared with 92.8% and 78.3% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
papers.abstract: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

papers.title: Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery
papers.abstract: Humanoid fall recovery requires selecting a motion that suits both the surrounding scene and the task. The same fallen pose can admit several ways to stand, with different routes, support transitions, and final headings. Yet reliable recovery alone does not provide control over which of these alternatives the robot executes. Steering this choice requires anticipating the physical consequences of a requested movement. We present RISE, an approach to perceptive humanoid recovery that lets task objectives steer how the robot returns to standing at inference time. It builds on two insights: diverse recoveries can be composed from shared movements, and anticipating how these movements unfold allows recovery to be steered toward a task objective. We learn a recovery vocabulary that connects intended movements to motor actions through sensory feedback. A visual diffusion planner learns from executions of this vocabulary to predict motion intent as future body states. Task costs guide this prediction toward a desired heading, rise speed, or path. The planner then generates motion latents conditioned on the steered intent, allowing the requested movement to shape its execution. Simulation experiments demonstrate diverse recoveries, terrain adaptation, and test-time steering without retraining, complemented by real-world demonstrations on a Unitree G1. Project page: https://osheraz.github.io/RISE/

papers.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
papers.abstract: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

papers.title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
papers.abstract: In this short note, we give an exposition of the recent proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture provided by OpenAI.

papers.title: Post-adiabatic effective-one-body waveforms for coalescing compact binaries
papers.abstract: I apply and extend the formalism of osculating orbits of Damour et al. (2004) and Lynch et al. (2026) to eccentric effective one body (EOB) models, in order to obtain an efficient yet accurate description of the inspiral-to-plunge dynamics of tidal, spinning compact binaries, including precessing ones by twisting the otherwise planar motion. The method is recast in terms of equinoctial orbital elements, to circumvent singularities associated with the zero-eccentricity limit. While the formalism is general and can be applied to any EOB model, I focus here on the TEOBResumS-Dalí family and demonstrate how this technique speeds up waveform generation without significantly compromising the accuracy of the model. Over $10^4$ binary neutron stars (BNSs) and as many binary black holes (BBHs) with initial eccentricities up to $0.6$ at $20$ Hz, the median speedup against an optimized version of the model is $\sim 2.6$ for BNSs and $\sim 1.5$ for BBHs, with mismatches against the full numerical solution always below $5 \times 10^{-7}$. The largest speedups, up to $\sim 7$ for individual systems, are obtained for light BBHs ($M \lesssim 8 M_\odot$) with low eccentricities $(e_0 \lesssim 0.1)$. In absolute terms, the median time needed to generate a BNS waveform is $\sim 0.5$ s, with $99.7\%$ of the systems below one second, and for long signals the model is up to $\sim 26$ times faster than a previous version. Applied to the calculation of initial conditions in the $e \rightarrow 0$ limit, the inclusion of radiation-reaction effects allows the model's input eccentricity to agree with the gauge-invariant waveform eccentricity down to initial values of $\sim 7 \times 10^{-8}$. Beyond time-domain applications, the same construction also gives frequency-domain EOB waveforms for eccentric compact binaries via a multi-harmonic stationary phase approximation.

papers.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.

papers.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance. Recently, selective looping, which recursively applies a few early Transformer layers within each denoising step, has been shown to improve training efficiency in MDLMs under an iso-FLOP budget. We investigate looping in UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged. We find that looping significantly improves training efficiency: looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu. We also find that, at a matched NFE budget, looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity than the non-looped UDLM, with most gains achieved at moderate loop counts. Finally, we study different loop-count distributions and find that sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training improves inference efficiency: on downstream tasks, this strategy uses 12% fewer loops than uniform loop-count sampling without degrading accuracy.

papers.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: Vietnamese pre-trained encoders have improved rapidly, but the strongest ones are large, multilingual-vocabulary models or depend on external word segmentation, which makes them costly to deploy. We present GoiBERT, a family of two compact Vietnamese encoders with 26M and 49M parameters that operate directly on raw text. GoiBERT learns from two complementary teachers. A same-tokenizer Vietnamese encoder first teaches general-purpose representations. A much larger teacher then provides task-level guidance through soft labels that are generated without ever labeling its own training data. Across eight benchmarks covering text classification, aspect-based sentiment analysis, natural language inference, and named entity recognition, GoiBERT-large achieves the highest average score among non-teacher models. It does so with fewer than half the parameters of the strongest compact baseline and twice its throughput. GoiBERT-base retains 99% of that baseline's performance at a quarter of its size. Our analysis shows that compression is nearly lossless for sentiment and classification tasks but remains costly for inference and entity recognition, which points to clear directions for future work. Our code and models are available at: https://github.com/Nhantran65/GoiBERT.git

papers.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
papers.abstract: Recent Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) use Self-Conditioning (SC), or Loopholing, to improve their performance. While SC is traditionally seen as an auxiliary heuristic, its empirical success raises the question: can a continuous generative model be based purely on Self-Conditioning? We answer affirmatively with LAW (``Loopholing All the Way''), which propagates the Expected Embedding under the denoiser's prediction across steps, decoding the tokens once, at the end. On Sudoku, LAW outperforms previous Discrete and Continuous Diffusion Models, including Loopholing Discrete Diffusion. On Maze, LAW is the most accurate from 2 to 64 NFE. After training on TinyGSM and sampling at temperature 1 with 1024 NFE, LAW solves 42.2% of GSM8K problems against 34.5% for uniform Loopholing Discrete Diffusion. Additionally, fine-tuning a pre-trained Uniform Diffusion Model (Duo) with LAW increases its accuracy from 17.2% to 48.1%. Finally, on OpenWebText, LAW pushes the Pareto frontier and approaches Autoregressive Models (ARMs) with 64 NFE. Find our code at https://github.com/ilievanadezhda/law.

papers.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
papers.abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

papers.title: A random sampling method to test the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
papers.abstract: We introduce a random sampling method for testing the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (wETH) that is particularly useful for large, sparse Hamiltonians. We test the method on a well-studied Rydberg atom system that exhibits both two- and three-body dipole-dipole interactions. Our results show that our method allows for the study of system sizes significantly beyond the limits of exact diagonalization. We find that the fluctuations in eigenstate expectation values decay as the Hilbert space dimension $D^{-1/2}$, consistent with wETH and in agreement with previous numerical results.

papers.title: Inaccessibility of the Cosmological Singularity to Quantum Probes
papers.abstract: We propose an operational resolution of the FLRW big bang singularity using quantum probes satisfying a curvature coupled Klein-Gordon equation. Applying the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of a Klein-Gordon field on a classical near-singularity FLRW background, we show that the induced conformal geometry renders curvature invariants finite and makes past directed causal geodesics complete. The classical big bang surface is therefore inaccessible to this class of quantum probes in finite effective proper time, while the underlying FLRW spacetime remains singular.

papers.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. We first build \probe{}, a suite of 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions, and find a persistent gap between what agents can read and what they choose to use. Agents score as well from self-generated charts as from numeric output, yet plotting access alone does not translate into consistent use. Task slices show that charts lead on temporal, pattern, and anomaly reasoning, while text leads on precise reading and conditional verification. We then propose \method{}, which distils two families of experience from conditioned trajectory rollouts. One family records how to select and verify analytical operations, and the other records when to invoke text, charts, or both. A trajectory judge scores outcomes and labels intermediate steps, and a validation gate admits only experience that improves held-out performance. On three held-out benchmarks with four LLM backbones, \method{} raises analytical accuracy and visual evidence quality over matched baselines, and backbones that never drew charts begin using them, all without touching model parameters.

papers.title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster
papers.abstract: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration. For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.

papers.title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
papers.abstract: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/χ_f(G)$ fraction of the total verified local improvement, where $χ_f(G)$ is the graph's fractional chromatic number. This guarantee is tight among mergers that select a subset of the same proposals. Under conditional local-improvement guarantees and a block error-bound condition, repeated collaboration converges geometrically in the objective gap. The rate separates task structure, agent allocation, and computation cost, yielding a linear program for agent assignment and an explicit time-cost trade-off. Code-repair experiments show that verified merging resolves conflicts between individually useful edits that cause naive merging to fail. On larger conflict-free tasks, parallel agents reduce modeled completion time at higher input-token-equivalent cost. On three public road networks, fractional integration retains 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs. For route-search agents sharing exclusive access to vehicle routes, fractional scheduling reduces measured wall time by a median of 15% across twelve paired runs, with route-cost changes varying across runs.

papers.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
papers.abstract: Personalized federated learning must decide which clients should share representations. We introduce HDC-FL (Head-Derived Clustering for Personalized Federated Learning), which reads that decision off a signal shared-encoder training already produces: the client-specific classifi- er heads. At periodic refresh rounds the server projects the cached heads into a normalized low-rank descriptor space, groups the descriptors, builds one encoder prototype per group from the cached client encoders, and returns to each client a soft mixture of those prototypes paired with its own unchanged head. Client-specific heads are never averaged or distributed to oth- er clients; the shared-encoder trajectory is left intact; and no second optimization trajectory, additional local objective, or post-training fine-tuning stage is required. Across 11 CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 configurations covering label-subset, Dirichlet and rotation heterogeneity with ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2 encoders, HDC-FL is competitive with the strongest personalized and clustered baselines in macro-averaged mean accuracy and attains the numerically highest macro-averaged worst-client and bottom-20% accuracy among the evaluated methods. The tail results distinguish methods that look similar when only their means are compared. A controlled donor-swap diagnostic further finds positive donor-ranking associations between head similarity and encoder compatibility in all three settings tested, most clearly under covariate shift.

papers.title: Circuits of LLM Classifiers
papers.abstract: Language models make it easy to build classifiers by simply prompting a model with the sample to classify. However, their predictions are neither deterministic nor uniformly reliable across samples. How can we combine predictions from different models to improve reliability? We view LLM classifiers as noisy measurement instruments of an underlying target label. Our goal is to maximize average classification accuracy at a given average query cost. To this end, we introduce circuits that organize LLM classifiers into an adaptive sequence of queries and decisions. We then characterize the optimal circuit, obtain the fundamental limits of achievable accuracy, and provide practical insights on realizing the optimal circuit. Across seven classification tasks spanning safety, health, political science, human preference, agent evaluation, decision-making and reasoning, our method improves the cost-accuracy frontier over routing and cascading baselines.

papers.title: A linear, second-order, unconditionally energy-stable scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme for the CHQ viscoelastic phase-separation model
papers.abstract: The CHQ model describes viscoelastic phase separation in a polymer--solvent mixture: a Cahn--Hilliard equation for the polymer volume fraction $φ$ is two-way coupled, through a phase-dependent cross-diffusion flux, to a damped relaxation equation for a scalar bulk elastic stress $q$. We propose a scalar-auxiliary-variable (SAV) time discretisation of this system, combining the SAV reformulation of the double-well potential with a second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) and a second-order extrapolation of all phase-dependent mobilities: a linear, computationally cheaper complement to the reference scheme's fully nonlinear Newton solve. The resulting method is (i) linear at every time step, with a coupling structure we prove has exactly one solution at every step, for every choice of time-step size; (ii) mass conserving, exactly, as an algebraic identity of the discrete equations themselves (the only drift ever seen numerically traces to the finite tolerance of the iterative linear solver, not a failure of the conservation property); and (iii) unconditionally stable for a modified discrete energy, via an exact one-step energy--dissipation identity. We show the energy identity extends to this filtered variant as well, with two explicit extra non-negative terms. Hence, the scheme actually producing the physics results is itself provably stable for the same energy. A Fourier--Galerkin implementation verifies that the energy identity holds at every time step to within floating-point round-off. It also confirms second-order temporal accuracy, including in the steep-interface regime, and agreement with an independently implemented nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver. Compared with that independent nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver, at equal grid resolution, the SAV method uses $2.5$--$3.0\times$ fewer linear-solver iterations and $1.7$--$2.0\times$ less wall-clock time.

papers.title: The Dynamics of RMSProp Beyond the Stability Threshold
papers.abstract: We study what happens to RMSProp when the learning rate is too large for convergence to the minimizer. For positive-definite quadratic loss functions, we show that the minimizer is Lyapunov un- stable above an explicit critical learning rate. Nevertheless, every trajectory eventually enters a compact trapping region. We obtain explicit bounds proportional to h in the spatial variables and to h2 in the memory variables, where h is the learning rate. We also prove that nontrivial period-two orbits exist precisely above the critical learning rate, and under additional spectral assumptions, an attracting branch of these orbits emerges from the minimizer. For sufficiently large learning rates, we construct branches near admissible corners of a cube. We then explore the dynamics inside the trapping region using the parameterization method and numerical continuation, exploring invariant circles and tori, coexistence of attracting sets, circle-doubling sequences, and chaotic motions. We examine how the dynamics depend on the loss Hessian, memory decay, and dimension. Finally, we test a learning-rate reduction schedule and continue selected invariant circles into an autonomous variant of the Adam optimizer.

papers.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
papers.abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI): an effective saturable absorber built from cascaded second-order nonlinearity in periodically poled lithium niobate nanophotonics, with a measured sub-20 fs response time. Through hybrid integration with an electrically pumped semiconductor gain element, we demonstrate a self-starting quadratic-soliton mode-locked laser with femtojoule pulse energies, operating in single- and multiple-soliton states. Quadratic solitons arise through the QNLI's dissipative and dispersive nonlinear response, which we confirm with a modified complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in agreement with measurements. By combining soliton formation with intracavity electro-optic modulation, we generate 750 fs pulses with flat-top spectra. Our engineerable, ultra-energy-efficient, electrically powered laser provides the critical source for fully integrated ultrafast photonic circuits in lithium niobate nanophotonics that natively offers electro-optic control, quadratic wavelength conversion, pulse compression, and spectral broadening.

papers.title: Wormhole geometries and energy conditions in linear and non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity
papers.abstract: This study explores static and spherically symmetric wormhole configurations in an extended formulation of symmetric teleparallel gravity governed by $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m $ and $f(Q,L_m)= -Q+L_m^α $ (where $Q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $L_m$ is the matter Lagrangian, and $α, β$ are constants). By varying the action with respect to the metric, we obtain the corresponding field equations. We conclude that the linear $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m$ framework successfully supports physically realistic wormholes without requiring extreme energy condition violations. It has been demonstrated that spacetime solutions violating both the radial and lateral null energy conditions in general relativity can nevertheless satisfy the NEC in $f(Q, L_m)$ gravity. Within non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity, non-exotic asymptotically flat wormhole solutions are derived using linear and asymptotically linear equations of state. Our results open new avenues to link modified gravity models with the observable astrophysical traits of exotic spacetimes.

papers.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots could aid lunar operations, but how to train their locomotion controllers for lunar gravity, terrain, and soil is unclear. We compare 12 strategies for a simulated Unitree G1 across gravity, terrain, and rigid or granular 3D resistive force theory (3D RFT) contact. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground in 10 s episodes, but falls continue, so longer episodes would see lower survival. Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies, in contrast, fall in every Earth episode, nearly all within 2 s. Rough-terrain training helps on uneven rigid ground only at training gravity. 3D RFT soil training helps on Earth sand but little on lunar soil. On three held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies lose no detectable progress at lunar gravity. Among tested strategies, only gravity-randomized rough 3D RFT training keeps mean survival above 0.83 at Earth and 0.95 at the Moon on all key tests up to 20 deg. Its ablation without soil training differs consistently only on soil at Earth gravity, falling in most sand episodes. These predictions depend on the contact model and soil stiffness, so lunar soil claims require agreement across soil models.

papers.title: AnyonWiki.org
papers.abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.

papers.title: When Standardization Spreads Factor Variation Across the Spectrum
papers.abstract: Standardizing variables by their sample standard deviations is routine in multivariate analysis and removes marginal scale differences before dependence is assessed. The resulting correlation matrix captures both dominant common components and dependence beyond them. A central inferential difficulty arises because the same random sample variances normalize the entire spectrum. In spiked covariance models, the sampling errors of leading and residual eigenvalues can become asymptotically independent. Sample standardization fundamentally changes this behavior and can preserve their dependence, allowing strong factors to remain a major source of uncertainty even after the leading eigenvalues are excluded. To obtain valid inference for both residual and full spectrum statistics, we establish their joint sampling law for sample correlation matrices with diverging spikes. The theory reveals exact trace compensation and statistic dependent transitions between asymptotic independence and dependence as the spikes grow. It leads to tests of an identity correlation matrix under strong factors and a feasible two sample comparison of residual spectral concentration. A sex balanced HapMap analysis illustrates the substantial effect of factor variation on residual spectrum inference.

papers.title: Joint Uniform Continuity of Reduced Free Products for strong convergence
papers.abstract: We investigate a generalization of Skoufranis' theorem on joint continuity of free products of laws in the strong topology. Namely, we show that this operation is moreover \emph{uniformly continuous}. Our methods follows those of Piser and go through the estimates of Ricard-Xu.

papers.title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
papers.abstract: When a multi-parameter model is fitted to measured data, only a few parameter combinations are often identifiable, as Fisher Information Matrix eigenvalues span several orders of magnitude. Sensitivity-based tools, including the Fisher Information Matrix and MBAM, reveal this structure analytically, while manifold learning can recover it from sampled trajectories. For an infinite-bus synchronous generator, both approaches show that inertia H and damping D are among the least identifiable parameters on a late post-disturbance window, t in [3,5] s, where six of the eleven parameters suffice to describe the response. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores H or D in the late window, whereas the early window [0, 2]s makes H the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter scenario pairs.

papers.title: Heavy-Quark Dynamics from $D^{0}$-Meson Anisotropy-Response Scaling Violations
papers.abstract: A species-resolved anisotropy-response scaling framework is used to investigate heavy-quark dynamics through the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) azimuthal anisotropies of $D^0$ mesons. The independently constrained light-flavor response provides a direct null test: the transformed $D^0$ harmonics exhibit approximate inter-harmonic closure but remain systematically displaced from the kaon-anchored scaling function, revealing a charm scaling violation. The common response is recovered through a charm-specific attenuation rescaling, $k_c$, together with a small low-$p_T$ hadronic-rescattering correction, $ζ_{\rm hs}\simeq0.06$, while retaining the established light-flavor prescription. In Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV, $k_c$ decreases from approximately $2.0$ in central and mid-central collisions to $1.27$ in the 30--50\% interval. For $D^0$ $v_2$, ultra-central p+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=8.16$~TeV require $k_c\simeq1.5$, whereas Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$~GeV are consistent with $k_c\simeq1$. The transition momentum exhibits a distinct system dependence: $D^0$ and light mesons show comparable $p_{T,\rm tr}\simeq4.5$--$5.0$~GeV/$c$ in Pb+Pb, consistent with the common large-system prescription also used in Au+Au, whereas p+Pb $D^0$ measurements are consistent with the lower light-meson scale of approximately $1.6$~GeV/$c$. These complementary constraints on attenuation strength and transition momentum provide a differential benchmark for heavy-quark transport and medium evolution.

papers.title: Orbitol: Crystal Generation on Wyckoff Orbits
papers.abstract: Generative models propose crystalline materials by learning composition and geometry, but unconditional sampling gives no direct control over the space group, which constrains whether responses such as piezoelectricity are symmetry-allowed. We present Orbitol, a crystal generator built on the Crystalite diffusion Transformer that replaces atom tokens with Wyckoff-orbit tokens. Given a space group and a collection of occupied Wyckoff positions, Orbitol generates the atom type and free coordinates of each orbit together with a compatible lattice, so every valid structure is invariant under the operations of the requested group. It generates structures two to three orders of magnitude faster than the symmetry-aware baselines at the evaluated settings. On MP-20, 13.8% of Orbitol's attempts yielded stable or metastable, unique and novel structures that retained the requested space group after relaxation, compared with 10.8% for SGFM, the next best model. We also introduce SPARC, a score that combines retention of the raw detected space group with agreement between the retained-group and training distributions. Finally, we used Orbitol to generate candidates in piezoelectric crystal classes. Of the structures selected by internal screening, 89% passed our density functional theory checks, and 79% also matched no Materials Project or Alexandria entry with the same space group. Their median figure of merit was nine times that of the piezoelectric materials computed in the Materials Project, and 24% of the new candidates ranked in that set's top 10%.

papers.title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum architecture that achieves addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant logical in high-rate codes. The codes are obtained from the flexible concatenation of small-distance high-rate self-dual CSS codes. Addressable and parallel universal logic on the resulting $K$ logical qubits is injected by fault-tolerantly preparing and then consuming diverse logical $K$-qubit CSS stabilizer states and logical $\lvert H \rangle^{\otimes K}$ global magic states. Flag-at-origin is used to prepare the stabilizer resource states while a concatenated cultivation protocol prepares the global magic states. These resource states are consumed by Steane-QEC or Knill-QEC teleportation gadgets, which simultaneously perform quantum error correction. Any quantum algorithm with $T$-depth $D_T$ can be executed by consuming $12D_T$ or fewer resource states. We benchmark the fault-tolerant preparation of the resource states for several two-level concatenations of the $[[k+4,k,2]]$ H codes and the Hamming $[[15,7,3]]$ code. In particular, we find that the concatenated cultivation offers at least one order of magnitude spacetime reduction compared to cultivation in the surface code.

papers.title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems
papers.abstract: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. Furthermore, many existing works focus on specific crop diseases, limiting their broader applicability. This paper presents a lightweight Group Equivariance Attention Network (GANet) designed for the prediction and monitoring of 38 types of plant diseases. GANet introduces a novel Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block, making it both sparse and efficient. With only 0.001M parameters, the model achieves an impressive 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset. Additionally, GANet is optimized for deployment on edge devices such as the Raspberry Pi 4b and Jetson Nano, where it reaches 5 FPS and 11 FPS, respectively, demonstrating its potential for real-time plant disease monitoring on low-power devices.

papers.title: The strengthened quantum Hamming bound of Yu, Lai, and Oh
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Yu, Lai, and Oh: their strengthened quantum Hamming bounds, a family that interpolates between Hamming-type bounds and the Singleton bound, hold for all quantum codes of dimension $K>1$, including impure and nonadditive codes. The result covers every integer local dimension $p\ge2$, not necessarily a prime power, every integer $t\ge1$, both distances $2t+1$ and $2t+2$, and every interpolation parameter $e\in\{0,\ldots,t\}$. The case $e=0$ implies the ordinary quantum Hamming bound for general codes, recently proved by Zhang and Chen. Yu, Lai, and Oh proved their bounds for pure codes and for general codes of distance three or four. More generally, for every integer $p\ge2$ and every quantum code of length $n$, dimension $K>1$ and distance $d\ge3$, we prove $Kf(0)\le p^n\mathbb{E} f(X)$, where $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-p^{-2})$, for every real polynomial $f$ of degree less than $d$ that is nonnegative on $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and positive at zero. For pure codes this inequality is implicit in the argument of Yu, Lai, and Oh. The proof uses the linear-programming method with quantum weight enumerators.

papers.title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. Doing so on the user's behalf requires identifying what matters, understanding the scene in real time, and initiating memory maintenance in the background while the user stays focused on their activities. We introduce ProactEgoMem, a benchmark that evaluates proactive memory in streaming egocentric video. Three tasks ground the evaluation in ambient environmental needs: Information Capture (IC) preserves transient yet dense visual information, State Tracking (ST) follows changing object states, and Location Tracking (LT) records object movements. The benchmark defines its protocol at two levels of proactiveness: the Notification Level asks for a single timely notification that satisfies the user's intent, while the deeper Intervention Level asks the agent to maintain memory on the user's behalf through an active start-to-stop tool lifecycle. Parallel ProactEgoMem-Daily and ProactEgoMem-Sci tracks contain 300/100 clips covering daily and scientific use cases, paired with 1000/500 questions in ProactEgoMem-QA, which measures the quality of the proactively acquired memory. Across proprietary, open-source, video-language, and streaming baselines, even the strongest models fail to capture memory both timely and accurately. ProactEgoMem provides a rigorous evaluation foundation for proactive multimodal assistance and for video agents that co-exist with their users.

papers.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage
papers.abstract: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and unparseable. We present VX-One, a small multi-head network (100K--10M parameters) with calibrated typed outputs: a binary gate, a closed-set choice with an explicit unknown option where the benchmark supports it (and abstention elsewhere), and an ordinal score. Heads are temperature-calibrated, with 0.7--1.7 ms single-event CPU p50 latency. We evaluate UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, and EMBER2024 against calibrated XGBoost, Random Forest, MLP, and Kitsune baselines, and measure a Suricata-to-VX-One cascade over five days of CIC-IDS2017. Results are deliberately double-sided: on UNSW the gate ties the best baseline (0.9837+/-0.0002 versus MLP 0.9835+/-0.0013 across three seeds), while VX-One wins temporal CIC detection (0.734+/-0.022 versus 0.639+/-0.027) but loses multi-class attribution to XGBoost. Under leave-one-family-out, the gate detects all nine UNSW families but drops below chance on CIC recon; CIC trees transfer better. Suricata resolves only about 0.1% of attacks on flow reconstructions and 0.2--2.2% on payload-bearing PCAPs; the strictly by-day Phase 2 recovers only the in-scope DoS/DDoS share on the wave day (recall 0.34, precision 0.97). Calibration collapses under temporal drift (ECE 0.04->0.40) for every method while ranking partly survives. We contribute a measured account of where typed calibrated decisions help perimeter triage, and where they fail.

papers.title: PhishGen: Understanding LLM Capabilities in Automated Phishing Website Generation
papers.abstract: Phishing relies on visual deception, traditionally requiring web-development skills or pre-built kits. LLMs erode this barrier by generating functional websites from natural-language prompts, yet prior work does not answer how far LLM-driven generation actually reaches: functionality is assessed by inspection rather than execution; visual fidelity is scored by automated metrics or a few internal coders rather than the humans such pages aim to deceive; evaluation is confined to commercial models; and no study benchmarks generated pages against phishing kits deployed in the wild. We present PhishGen, a framework that evaluates the appearance fidelity and end-to-end functionality of LLM-generated phishing pages. PhishGen constructs prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generates pages using 14 LLMs spanning commercial, open-source, and uncensored categories, and assesses each via automated similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user study, and execution-based functionality testing, benchmarking all results against 64 real-world phishing kits. Although 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs render, their perceived fidelity is modest (2.02/5), and only 38.7% complete the full credential-harvesting pipeline, with the Unsaved error as the largest failure mode. Contrary to the belief that uncensored models pose the greatest threat, GPT 4.1 reaches 86.3 to 94.1% functional success while uncensored models rarely exceed 45.4%. Phishing kits remain more complete per sample, yet three strong LLMs surpass the kit-level rate (70.9 to 89.7%), showing that LLMs trade average completeness for scalable, low-barrier generation of working phishing pages. We further identify generator-level fingerprints that current similarity-based defenses miss, and distill recommendations for hybrid detectors.

papers.title: An Implicit Conservative Finite Volume Scheme with Poisson Brackets for the Steady-State Transport of Galactic Cosmic Rays
papers.abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) pose a persistent radiation hazard to astronauts and spacecraft in the heliosphere. Modeling their transport is essential for understanding how the solar wind and heliospheric magnetic field shape their spatial distributions and energy spectra. Timely predictions require solving for the particle distribution function much faster than real time, but explicit numerical schemes are restricted by the stability limit on the time step. In this Letter, we present an implicit conservative finite-volume scheme for kinetic equations formulated with Poisson brackets. This scheme conserves particle number, maintains the total-variation-diminishing property, achieves second-order spatial accuracy, and remains stable for time steps far beyond the explicit limit, while reaching quasi-steady states in less than ~1/100 of the computational time required for the explicit scheme, as demonstrated by numerical tests. We apply this scheme to the Parker transport equation along magnetic field lines in the background solar wind during Carrington rotation 2211, where it reaches steady-state GCR distributions within 10 iterations, about 1000 times faster than the explicit scheme. The GCR proton spectrum averaged over 27 days agrees with AMS-02 measurements to within 10%. The simulation also yields a realistic radial intensity gradient and captures the Forbush decrease features associated with three stream interaction regions observed at Earth.

papers.title: Spatial Control of Compressible Active Fluids
papers.abstract: We study the response of compressible microtubule-based active fluids to sinusoidally varying activity patterns, using experiments and theory. Microtubules accumulate in low-activity regions and are depleted from high activity ones, with the density difference controlled by the wavelength of the activity pattern. To explain these observations the continuum model needs to account for both active stresses that are proportional to nematic order tensor and the isotropic active pressure. At short wavelengths, active vortices spanning adjacent high and low activity regions suppress density modulation. At larger wavelengths, vortical flows confined to the low or high activity region allow for the emergence of the density contrast. Our work shows that a minimal theoretical model of active compressible fluids accurately reproduces experiments, while elucidating the fundamental constraints on control protocols that seek to tame their chaotic dynamics.

papers.title: Extended vs. thin screen approximation in astrophysical settings
papers.abstract: Context: In the context of radio wave propagation through plasma concentrations and for gravitational lensing, the thin screen approximation often provides a suitable approximation for scattering and deflections caused by three-dimensional spatial structures. For scattering of electromagnetic waves from an extended medium, stochastic theories provide analytical bounds on ensemble averaged quantities, such as the scintillation index. If neither the conditions for a stochastic treatment nor the thin screen approximation are fulfilled, fully numerical methods are required. Aims: For an extended structure, the applicability of the thin screen approximation needs to be verified by comparing it with the fully three-dimensional scattering solution. We discuss various exact solutions to simple lensing geometries and provide numerical results for the propagation in the branched-flow regime, which is also of relevance in astrophysical applications. Methods: We transfer several analytical results obtained in quantum mechanical scattering theory to astrophysical settings and complement them with different numerical methods to quantify the deviations of thin screen theories from an extended medium results. Results: We provide the analytical results for spherical waves scattered by a point source and show the emergence of branchef flow in the intermediate regime between thin screen physics and stochastic media results.

papers.title: Stockmayer Fluid with a Shifted Dipole. III. Ion Solvation
papers.abstract: Though ion solvation is well understood for the standard Stockmayer fluid, the effect of displacing the point dipole of a Stockmayer particle, a simple geometric modification, on ion-solvent structuring and solvation thermodynamics remains less understood. We use molecular dynamics simulations to describe how a dipole shift affects radial and orientational solvent structure around centered ions, how strongly the solvent distinguishes cations and anions, and how the solvent mediates ion-ion pairing. We show that, with a centered dipole, cations and anions have equal preferences for the local solvent environment. Shifting the dipole breaks the fore-aft symmetry of the local electrostatic field, leading to a stronger preference for a Stockmayer particle's dipole to orient towards an anion and a weaker preference to orient away from a cation. These structural asymmetries propagate to the solvation free energies: increasing dipole displacement makes anion solvation more favorable, while cation solvation becomes less favorable overall across dipole strengths. The same asymmetry also manifests in the effective ion-ion interaction-increasing the dipole shift reorganizes the local solvation environment, enhancing solvent shielding of short-range cation-anion contact while weakening screening at longer range. As a result, solvent-separated configurations become comparatively more favorable, whereas increasing dipole strength produces the opposite trend. Such effects cannot be explained by bulk dielectric screening alone, indicating that molecular charge geometry plays an important role in both single-ion solvation and solvent-mediated ion-ion interactions. This work demonstrates that dipole location, not only magnitude, provides a geometric control on ion-specific solvation and ion pairing in general polar fluids.

papers.title: DBDSVDMR3: An MRRR-Based Bidiagonal SVD Solver Built from DSTEGR
papers.abstract: The optimal algorithm for the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem is Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR or MR$^3$), which is capable of computing $k$ eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs in only $O(kn)$ floating-point operations. While MRRR is nearly 30 years old, it has never successfully been adapted to the bidiagonal SVD. This is not for lack of trying; two previous attempts produced implementations that were considered for LAPACK but eventually abandoned, a result of the fact that neither was reliable enough when run on test problems. The question therefore remained: is there a problem with the theory of MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD or were there simply bugs in the previous implementations that went undetected? This paper resolves this question by presenting DBDSVDMR3 -- a new implementation of the MRRR-based algorithm for the bidiagonal SVD originally proposed by Willems and Lang [ETNA 2012], which, for the first time, performs well on a variety of test problems while achieving significant speedups over both LAPACK's bisection-based solver and, in certain cases, divide-and-conquer for the bidiagonal SVD (thereby indicating that the theory is sound). DBDSVDMR3 will be available in the next release of LAPACK. In this paper, we discuss the design of our implementation, which was obtained with the help of Claude Code, and exhibit its performance on a diverse set of test problems.

papers.title: Modeling MAD Sgr A* flares and their dependence on spin
papers.abstract: Aims: This study aims to place constraints on the spin of Sgr A* from recent flare observations. It models the flare kinematics in the vicinity of a supermassive black hole, evaluates their dependence on black hole spin, and assesses the correlation between the spin of the black hole and the astrometric observations in the Galactic center. Methods: Our study extends the work of Antonopoulou et al. 2025 to a range of black hole spins. A prominent flux eruption is identified in the simulation, and the evolution of the active region on the equatorial plane is tracked during the event. The flare model consists of a spherical hot spot ejected along the flux tube with a relativistic velocity. Results: In MAD simulations, the flux tube wraps around the jet funnel in the opposite direction to the black hole's spin. This dependence is imprinted on the flare trajectory and provides a strong correlation between the spin of the black and the flare kinematics.
