The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

papers.title: Cographs in chordal graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.

papers.title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
papers.abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

papers.title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
papers.abstract: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

papers.title: Quintaverse-Phantiverse Cosmologies in $f(Q,C)$ Gravity: a Non-coincident Geometrical Origin of Cosmic Acceleration
papers.abstract: We investigate the asymptotic dark energy sectors of a quadratic form of $f(Q,C)$ Lagrangian. We reformulate the original equations of motion to obtain the equivalent dynamical system, for two non-trivial classes of affine connections allowed by symmetries of $f(Q,C)$ gravity. In these scenarios, the late-time accelerated expansion emerges as an intrinsic geometrical effect of the $f(Q,C)$ sector, without invoking an independent dark energy component. We find that an effective dark matter solution emerges for one class, whereas for the other class, the positivity of the matter density and the conservation of the momentum tensor cannot be simultaneously satisfied. This leads to the conclusion that there exists an effective dark matter solution for which the matter contribution is a combination of a pressureless matter as well as a stiff fluid. Furthermore, in both cases there always exists a universal stable accelerated expansion solution. Besides, the matter solutions are saddle points for those values of the model parameters that ensure the conservation of the energy momentum. In addition, we introduce a parameterization in which the equation of state parameter at the fixed point corresponding to accelerated expansion is characterized by a free parameter that quantifies its deviation from $-1$. We thereby inspired to invent the terms ``Quintaverse'' and ``Phantiverse'', corresponding to quintessence-like and phantom-like attractor solutions. Also, we numerically illustrate the evolution of different cosmological quantities and the phase-space diagrams. Particularly, the behavior of the Universe using two kinematic toolkits, namely, the cosmographic and statefinder variables, is discussed.

papers.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: classical coefficients across ionization and magnetization
papers.abstract: The classical transport of magnetic field and electron energy in a plasma requires the use of coefficients that depend on plasma ionization $Z$ and magnetization $χ$. This paper explains these scalings through studying the electron velocities responsible for each transport process. Both electron-electron collisions and magnetization affect higher velocity electron populations preferentially, lowering the carrier velocities; transport carried by a high energy electron population is therefore more suppressed by both electron-electron collisions and magnetization than transport carried by lower velocities. Carrier Hall parameters $ψ=χf(Z)$ are defined for each coefficient such that magnetization can be described independent of ionization. An analytic idealized coefficient with a single rigid carrier velocity reproduces many of the characteristics of the coefficients, in particular thermal conductivity, but overestimates plasma magnetization due to magnetization itself lowering the carrier velocity. A single moving carrier model improves agreement, but cannot describe the smoothness of the Righi-Leduc coefficient, which originates from being an average over a range of carrier velocities. This is the first paper in a 3-part series; the subsequent papers will extend the carrier picture to non-local heat-flux (paper 2) and non-local magnetic field evolution (paper 3).

papers.title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
papers.abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

papers.title: Dealing with low-weight errors that lead BP OSD to fail
papers.abstract: Belief Propagation combined with Ordered Statistics Decoding (BP OSD) is an open-source decoding tool used widely within the community due to its versatility and ease of application to Quantum Low Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes. However, the degeneracy of quantum codes has been observed to degrade the performance of BP OSD, particularly leading to error floors for low physical error rates. Here, we investigate the low-weight error configurations responsible for such failures in Bivariate Bicycle codes. We show that, at code capacity, BP OSD fails on errors whose weight is significantly smaller than d/2, arising from global symmetries of the decoding graph that prevent the convergence of parallel BP. Furthermore, our analysis reveals new pitfalls that can arise when analysing the performance of BP OSD in the rare events regime, such as loss of ergodicity in splitting methods and numerical instabilities in the decoder. We show how to mitigate these failure mechanisms by modifying the BP update rules and the decoder implementation, leading to substantial improvement in logical error rate.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.

papers.title: The Customer Is the Builder: How AI Coding Agents Are Rewriting the Economics of Software
papers.abstract: AI coding agents could change whether organizations buy software or build the functionality they need. We focus on organizations and professional buyers whose domain knowledge can help them specify and evaluate tools for their work. We define the software substitution frontier as the functions customers could build and maintain at an acceptable standard for less than buying them. Using public data, we compare growing capacity to build with indicators of market change. Since 2023, the length of benchmark tasks that leading agents can complete at 50 percent success, measured in human working time, has doubled about every 129 days. A broad search identified 575 potential open-source alternatives to selected commercial products, although some functional matches still require independent validation. The Craft suite produced 12 application repositories over 12.0 days of public development, but these remain early versions with unverified completeness and reliability. Market evidence is mixed: purchased software gained US investment share and tracked commercial installations grew. Yet 32 percent of respondents to an organizational survey reported forgoing at least one software purchase because their organization could build the functionality with coding agents. These self-reports do not establish the spending displaced or the reliability of the resulting tools. The gap motivates a warning: customers' capacity to build could affect individual buying decisions before a broad purchasing shift becomes visible. We examine this possibility using benchmark projections and observable market tests. The projections are an extrapolation, not a forecast of customer switching.

papers.title: Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs
papers.abstract: I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.

papers.title: The PAU Survey: Active galactic nucleus galaxies in galaxy pairs
papers.abstract: Aims. Leveraging the high-precision photometric redshifts of the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS), we aim to investigate the connection between active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and galaxy pairs up to redshifts of $\sim1.0$. Methods. We identified 16,824 galaxy pairs with projected separations of $r_p < 100$ kpc and radial-velocity differences of $ΔV < 3500$ km s$^{-1}$. AGNs were selected by cross-matching PAUS galaxies with multi-wavelength AGN catalogues, yielding 270 AGNs in pairs out of a parent sample of 8,880 AGNs in PAUS. We constructed control samples of isolated AGNs; non-AGNs in pairs; and isolated non-AGNs matched in redshift, absolute magnitude, and environment. Results. Active galactic nuclei in pairs show progressively redder rest-frame colours with increasing redshift, particularly at redshifts of $z\gtrsim 0.5$, whereas isolated AGNs and non-AGNs in pairs show no significant colour evolution and remain at $\mathrm{M_g-M_r}\sim0.65$. Pairs hosting AGNs are also preferentially morphologically disturbed interacting systems found at smaller projected separations and velocity offsets, consistent with more dynamically advanced interactions. Conclusions. These results provide evidence of a redshift-dependent link between galaxy interactions and AGN activity, suggesting that interactions play an increasingly important role in triggering nuclear activity at intermediate redshifts. This study highlights the unique capability of PAUS to probe AGN-galaxy interaction connections beyond the local Universe with unprecedented statistical power.

papers.title: Space curves in Hahn calculus: rotation structure, a fundamental theorem, and $q$-deformed invariants at the fixed point
papers.abstract: We develop the differential geometry of space curves in Hahn's quantum calculus, where the derivative is the difference quotient along the contraction $σ(t)=qt+ω$ with fixed point $ω_0=ω/(1-q)$. The Hahn Frenet frame is transported along every orbit of $σ$ by rotations through turning and torsion angles, which identifies it with the discrete Frenet frame of the inscribed orbit polygon. An embedded regular Hahn curve is determined, up to linear reparametrization about $ω_0$, by its trace and the induced contraction. We prove a sharp planarity criterion and a fundamental theorem via an infinite product of rotations and the Jackson--Nörlund integral. For smooth curves, expansions uniform in $q$ show that at $ω_0$ the Hahn curvature and torsion carry the factors $[2]_q/2$ and $[3]_q/3$. These factors, a sampling effect of geometrically decaying steps, disappear under edge-length normalization, but their quotient persists in the limiting ratio of torsion and turning angles of every polygon inscribed in a smooth curve with monotonically converging vertices and edge lengths decaying with ratio~$q$. In uniformly sampled relaxation towards a stable node, the factors can become measurable biases. We characterize generalized Hahn helices by a two-step relation between turning and torsion angles; their Lancret ratio at $ω_0$ is $\pm([2]_q/2)\cot\vartheta$, where $\vartheta$ is the helix angle. Unlike the classical case, a constant ratio of torsion and curvature does not characterize helices: curves with constant curvature and torsion are never generalized Hahn helices, and, near $ω_0$, unit-speed helices with a given ratio are unique up to similarities and linear reparametrization.

papers.title: OGLE-2012-BLG-0563: Relative Proper Motion Constraint from Keck Follow-up finds the correct Lens
papers.abstract: We present Keck/NIRC2 adaptive optics imaging results of planetary microlensing event OGLE-2012-BLG-0563. We find that the OGLE-2012-BLG-0563L planetary system consists of a 1.12 +/- 0.09 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting a 0.81 +/- 0.04 solar-mass host star at a distance of 5.49 +/- 0.56 kpc from the Sun. This event has a lens-source separation of 23.28 +/- 0.48 mas, which is the smallest lens-source separation measured to date with Keck AO data. We find that the incorrect solution - which identifies the Northeast (NE) star as the source star - is favored if one only considers the discovery paper, the Fukui et al. (2015) solution, or an unconstrained model. However, by performing an image-constrained light curve model fit using the relative proper motion direction constraint from the Keck follow-up data, we demonstrate that the correct solution identifies the NE star as the lens star. The discrepancy in the unconstrained models is driven by systematics in the FTS and MOA B & C data, alongside the impact of the relative proper motion direction constraints. This outcome offers two important lessons for future Roman data analysis: (1) thoroughly verify systematics across all passbands and identify the precise origin of chi-squared differences, and (2) utilize image-constrained light curve modeling incorporating relative proper motion direction constraints to identify the correct lens.

papers.title: Amplified EFT corrections near exceptional QNMs
papers.abstract: We show that the ordinary expansion of EFT corrections to individual QNM frequencies breaks down at an exceptional QNM, and that these corrections become enhanced for near-exceptional QNMs. We give a brief argument for why this should generally happen, before numerically demonstrating this behaviour by calculating the $α'^3$ corrections to QNMs of equal-spin Myers--Perry-AdS$_5$ black holes. This calculation corresponds to $λ^{-3/2}$ corrections to the poles of the retarded Green's function in the boundary CFT, where $λ$ is the 't Hooft coupling. Treating the coalescing pair together, we calculate the leading $λ^{-3/4}$ splitting at the uncorrected exceptional point and the $λ^{-3/2}$ displacement of the exceptional point in temperature and angular velocity. The background derivative expansion can remain valid while the nondegenerate expansion of individual frequencies fails. We discuss the implications for the full response and for other areas of black hole physics.

papers.title: Black Hole Shadows and Quasinormal Modes with Dark Matter at the Horizon
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the effect of a surrounding dark matter halo on two horizon-scale observables of a black hole: its shadow and quasinormal-mode spectrum. We consider a Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a Hernquist halo and construct a one-parameter family of solutions that preserve the total halo mass while varying how the halo density vanishes at the horizon. By closing the Einstein equations with an Einstein-cluster stress tensor, we show that horizon regularity requires the density to vanish at least linearly. Our results also indicate that the dominant energy condition is violated in a thin layer outside the horizon, highlighting the limitations of the Einstein-cluster description within the photon sphere. We demonstrate that, at fixed black hole mass, the halo always enlarges the shadow, with the effect becoming more pronounced for more massive and compact halos. Comparison with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr\,A$^*$ and M87$^*$ shows that only sufficiently compact halos can be constrained, with the inferred bounds depending sensitively on whether the observed mass is identified with the black hole mass or the total mass of the system. We further show that the halo lowers both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of electromagnetic and axial gravitational quasinormal modes, leading to higher quality factors. These spectral shifts are quantitatively explained by changes in the photon-sphere properties through the eikonal correspondence. Since the effects scale with the ratio of the halo mass to its size, they are observable only for dark matter concentrated within a few tens of gravitational radii of the black hole, which is the regime considered here.

papers.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
papers.abstract: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

papers.title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
papers.abstract: Pauli-based computation (PBC) is a measurement-based model of quantum computation that samples from output distributions of universal Clifford+$T$ circuits. Here, we provide a normal form (NF) that completely characterizes its adaptive and entanglement structures. These insights unify PBC with one-way quantum computing as dual or `time-reversed' counterparts. We use the NF to advance strategies for distributed computation and investigate magic-state injection rates. We also demonstrate an exponential improvement in the detection of unnecessary magic-state qubits, allowing their efficient removal. Our NF further enables ahead-of-time circuit compilation using PBC, reducing CNOT gate count and quantum memory of random quantum circuits on average by 50% and 40%, respectively, beating other state-of-the-art compilers.

papers.title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
papers.abstract: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

papers.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
papers.abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We propose Poly-Ripple, a framework in which multiple clients perform ICL using large autoregressive vision models (LAVMs) without model updates. Each client is prompted by its private demonstrations and predicts the radio map for the same scene query. To capture the causal structure of wireless propagation outward from the transmitter (Tx), we adopt ripple-ordered autoregressive modeling. We further introduce importance-aware aggregation to exploit heterogeneous contextual knowledge distributed across clients under the context length constraint. We provide theoretical analysis and conduct extensive experiments on a public indoor RME benchmark. The experimental results show that Poly-Ripple consistently outperforms representative ICL baselines, while aligning with our theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
papers.abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

papers.title: Domain walls in $R3c$-structured NaNbO$_3$
papers.abstract: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral $R3c$ phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO$_3$. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109° domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO$_3$. Finally, we find that this class of 109° walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the $R3c$ phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the $R3c \leftrightarrow Pbcm$ phase transition.

papers.title: TerraTransfer++: Demonstration-Free End-to-End Planner
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks and real-world deployments. Its standard training recipe, however, is expensive across all existing paradigms: imitation learning requires fleet-scale driving logs whose behavior distribution only thinly covers the safety-critical tail; closed-loop reinforcement learning in a photorealistic simulator, while offering diverse behaviors, is bottlenecked by sample-efficiency, per-step cost of rendering, and a forward pass through a large vision backbone. Self-play in vectorized simulators changes the economics: at millions of rollout steps per second, one can obtain a state distribution with natural diversity in collisions, near-misses, and recoveries that no driving log contains, and a highly reactive policy emerges from a basic driving-quality reward. Our approach exploits this asymmetry. We pretrain a single policy by self-play, distill its rollouts into a flow-matching trajectory teacher that also plans, and train lightweight adapters on a frozen pretrained vision backbone to reproduce the latent space of either teacher through the action KL divergence, a batch-relational low-rank structural loss, and, for the planner, a trajectory-matching loss. Every target traces back to the self-play policy, so alignment never supervises against a logged trajectory: a paired dataset of (image, scene-state) frames suffices, with no need for the curated expert demonstrations that imitation pretraining is built on. From this one self-play teacher we obtain two end-to-end students: a closed-loop policy that outperforms every published imitation-based end-to-end method on the photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting closed-loop benchmark HUGSim, and a planner that reaches 59.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM navhard, above every published method including DriveZero-Scale (57.1), and 95.5 PDMS on navtest, without human demonstrations.

papers.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 19.4% for the best competing WAM.

papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: A Sharp Distributional Lower Bound for Planar Discrepancy
papers.abstract: We prove that the unnormalized discrepancy function of every $n$-point set in the unit square has absolute value at least $c\sqrt{1+\log n}$ on a set of measure at least $η$, with absolute constants $c,η>0$. Consequently, its $L_p$-quasinorm is bounded below by $c\,η^{1/p} \sqrt{1+\log n}$ for every $p>0$.

papers.title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
papers.abstract: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.

papers.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

papers.title: Paying for Information, Not for Clicks: A Block-Level Publisher Content Marketplace for AI Answers
papers.abstract: We propose a publisher content marketplace that allocates payments for information used in AI-generated answers. The unit of attribution is a ``lego block:'' a distinct fact or piece of commentary that may appear in articles from multiple publishers. A simple news-reading model connects three payment rules: equal sharing among all publishers reporting on a block, rewarding the publisher who reported a block first, and rewarding indispensable contributions. Each can be represented within a Shapley-value framework. We evaluate the framework using answers to 1,974 search-engine queries about a heavily covered news episode. When attribution considers only the articles retrieved for an individual query, most cited blocks appear unique, and the rules produce nearly identical allocations. A global index covering the full news corpus reveals overlap across publishers, making the choice of payment rule consequential. Premium publishers, defined as established outlets with substantial newsgathering operations, receive 42% of allocated value under equal sharing, compared with 46-50% under a first-publication rule, depending on the treatment of publication timestamps. These findings highlight the importance of a shared global index that records which publishers provide each block and when they published it. Attribution restricted to the sources retrieved for an individual answer lacks the information needed to distinguish these payment policies.

papers.title: Spin correlations in the $τ$-lepton pair in polarized electron-positron annihilation
papers.abstract: Possible anomalous New Physics contributions to dipole and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton rise considerable interest in theoretical and experimental studies of the $τ$-pair production in electron-positron annihilation and in proton-proton collisions at the LHC. In the present paper we discuss and calculate the spin-correlation matrix in the $e^+ e^- \to τ^+ τ^-$, and in general $f \bar{f} \to τ^+ τ^-$ processes, including New Physics contributions to the $γττ$ and $Z ττ$ vertices and longitudinally polarized beams of initial fermions. The $τ$ decays are included as well. This work is an upgrade of our previous studies of the spin correlations in the $ττ$ system produced in the processes with unpolarized initial fermions ($e^- e^+$ and $q\bar{q}$). A corresponding numerical code is developed. Brief information on how to use and configure the MC programs with a new subroutine is also given.

papers.title: R4DGS: Referring Segmentation in 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Dynamic representations based on 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) have shown strong capabilities in reconstruction and rendering, yet current methods remain limited in supporting complex natural-language referring in dynamic scenes. Existing 4D Gaussian methods are primarily designed for rendering-oriented dynamic modeling, while current semantic extensions often rely on scene-specific semantic optimization or are evaluated on relatively simple query settings. In this paper, we study Referring 4D Gaussian Splatting (R4DGS), a task for grounding temporally varying, multi-target or reasoning-intensive, and zero-target or distractor expressions in dynamic 4D scenes. To support this task, we introduce R4D-Bench-QA, a benchmark with structured query annotations. We further present ReferGaussian, a unified framework built upon 4DGS that converts low-level dynamic Gaussians into persistent, language-addressable entities for training-free referring inference. ReferGaussian organizes mask-supported Gaussian entities in an EntityBank, uses Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to decompose complex queries into trackable object phrases and structured referring constraints, and performs constraint-aware grounding without scene-specific semantic optimization. Experiments on R4D-Bench-QA and the 4D LangSplat protocol demonstrate improved temporal target selection and competitive spatiotemporal grounding without scene-specific semantic training. Project resources are available at https://chenbangpu.github.io/R4DGS/.

papers.title: Covering lemmas associated to maximal operators of weak type
papers.abstract: Building on the work of A. Córdoba and R. Fefferman, we provide a necessary and sufficient covering condition on a basis $\mathcal{B}$ on a separable metric space $X$ with a Borel measure $μ$ so that the associated \mbox{geometric} maximal operator $M_\mathcal{B}$ satisfies for all $α> 0$ the weak type estimate $$μ\left(\left\{x \in X : M_\mathcal{B}f(x) > α\right\}\right) \leq \int_{X}Φ\left( γ_\mathcal{B} \left|\frac{f}α\right|\right)\,dμ\;,$$ where $Φ: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is an everywhere finite Young's function.

papers.title: Top quark differential distributions in the SMEFT
papers.abstract: We discuss top quark processes, in particular $tW$ production and top-antitop pair production, as probes of dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We calculate top-quark double differential distributions in transverse momentum and rapidity, and we perform SMEFT fits at LO, NLO and, by adding second-order soft-gluon corrections, at approximate NNLO.

papers.title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

papers.title: Shear-induced mechanical yielding controls cluster morphology and dynamics in aggregating non-Brownian suspensions
papers.abstract: In sheared aggregating suspensions, flow drives both the formation and breakage of particle clusters, whose dynamic evolution influences transport and rheological properties. Understanding these mechanisms remains challenging due to the complex interplay between interparticle forces, hydrodynamic interactions, and shear flow. Using parallelized Accelerated Stokesian Dynamics (PASD) simulations, we investigate cluster microstructure and rotational dynamics, and how their coupling produces suspension stress in sheared, attractive non-Brownian suspensions. When interparticle attraction dominates over separating shear forces, clusters grow until mechanical loading balances maximum interparticle bond strength. We examine how the cluster stresslet depends on cluster size, with both quantities normalized by their mechanical yielding scales. Scaled cluster stresslets collapse onto a master curve exhibiting three distinct regimes: cubic, quadratic, and linear with respect to the scaled radius of gyration $R_g$. In the cubic regime, small, compact clusters behave as rigid bodies, whose hydrodynamic stresslet scales with cluster volume $R_g^3$. As clusters grow into the quadratic regime, low-aspect-ratio clusters preferentially yield under flow, driving a proportional increase in average aspect ratio with size. High-aspect-ratio clusters follow Jeffery rotational dynamics within the flow-gradient plane, spending longer durations aligned with the flow and thereby reducing their time-averaged hydrodynamic stresslet to scale as $R_g^2$. In the linear regime, clusters approach the maximum size sustainable by the interparticle bonds. The internal tension is bounded by the maximum bond strength, limiting the stresslet to an $R_g$ dependence. These findings establish a mechanistic framework connecting microscale cluster morphology and dynamics to macroscale rheology.

papers.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
papers.abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

papers.title: Evolution of Jeans instability in nonthermal magnetized complex plasmas
papers.abstract: The classical Jeans instability framework provides a conceptual foundation for understanding self-gravitational collapse and subsequent star formation in interstellar environments. However, cosmic plasmas are inherently magnetized and frequently collisionless, exhibiting significant departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium. While linear theories predict initial instability thresholds, they fail to track the long-term nonlinear runaway dynamics. We present a fluid simulation investigating the nonlinear evolution of the Jeans instability in a magnetized tricomponent complex (dusty) plasma. The constituent nonthermal electrons and ions are governed by the $κ$-distribution law, while the heavier dust grains are treated in a fluid framework, coupled with a uniform ambient magnetic field. The numerical architecture utilizes a fourth-order finite difference method (FDM) for spatial gradients and a second-order leap-frog time-integration scheme. We systematically investigate the complex interplay among the self-gravitational attraction, nonthermal electrostatic screening, and magnetic pressure across a wide range of magnetic field strengths and degrees of nonthermality. It is found that enhanced nonthermality accelerates structural localization, while the magnetic field introduces a critical pressure barrier that suppresses the instability. In highly magnetized environments, thermal and nonthermal systems exhibit identical growth rate characteristics, indicating that magnetic pressure dominates the nonthermal thermostatistics in the strong magnetic regime. This study develops a comprehensive and numerically robust framework to understand early-stage star formation and evolution processes in nonthermal astrophysical media.

papers.title: Solar Photospheric Flows and the Origin of Active Regions
papers.abstract: The early evolutionary stages of some active regions (ARs) are analysed with the aim of resolving one of the paramount-importance problems of heliophysics: what plays a primary, active role in the formation of active regions and sunspots---magnetic fields or motion of solar plasma? In particular, the first view underlies the popular model of rising $Ω$-shaped, twisted flux-tube loop of strong magnetic field. In this study, optical images obtained by the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) of the Solar Dynamics Observatory are used along with full-vector maps of magnetic field based on HMI data. Maps of fluid-particle tracks are constructed using local correlation tracking of photospheric brightness elements. Comparisons of optical and magnetic maps for three developing active regions confirm the conclusion made by Bumba and Howard in the mid-1960s that the supergranulation pattern is not destroyed by the emerging magnetic field of the developing AR, which would be inevitable if a loop of the strong-magnetic-field flux tube rose through the subphotospheric layers. There are no signs of spreading flows on scales comparable to the size of the whole active region. Various forms of dissymmetry between the leading and trailing parts of ARs are revealed. Next, an example of a well-developed sunspot group is considered, which demonstrates that the twist of the magnetic configuration may develop much later than the group starts growing. It is concluded that plasma flows appear to be determinant with respect to magnetic fields. The considered scenarios of the origin of ARs are in sharp contradiction with the rising-tube model.

papers.title: MPBRS: Multi-Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Unified Reward Configuration in Humanoid Locomotion
papers.abstract: Designing and tuning reward functions remains one of the main challenges in building effective reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines for humanoid locomotion. While shaping rewards can accelerate learning, naively formulated terms often conflict with the desired behavior, overfit to a specific robot, or become unstable under small weight changes. Potential-Based Reward Shaping (PBRS) offers an alternative solution: shaping the reward via differences of a potential function to guide exploration without changing the optimal policy. In this paper, we study Multi-PBRS for humanoid locomotion and propose a unified reward configuration. We then evaluate the same reward structure and weights across nine humanoid robots, requiring only robot-specific metadata (joint/link mappings and default poses) rather than per-robot reward redesign. Our experiments show that, compared to standard shaping, MPBRS provides more consistent scaling behavior and reduced tuning sensitivity across robots, making it easier to tune without altering the optimal policy.

papers.title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.

papers.title: Optical-Infrared Extinction Variation in Nearby Molecular Clouds
papers.abstract: The dust extinction curve is an important probe of the properties of dust grains, particularly their size distribution. The properties of dust grains are expected to change significantly in dense molecular clouds due to shielding from interstellar radiation and increased frequency of grain-grain and grain-gas collisions. We measure the dust extinction curve shape parameter R(V) in 9 nearby, dense molecular clouds using data from the APOGEE spectroscopic survey, in combination with ten-band photometry from PS1, 2MASS, and WISE. We analyze the results to determine how the extinction curve varies in nearby molecular clouds. We find that most molecular clouds show a positive correlation between R(V) and E(B-V), but the strength of the correlation varies significantly between clouds. In addition, we find that the clouds with the strongest correlation tend to have very high dispersion in R(V) at fixed E(B-V), which tightens dramatically when clouds are subdivided into separate regions. This suggests that local environmental conditions beyond density shape the R(V)-E(B-V) relation.

papers.title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation
papers.abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Plücker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. A differentiable expectation over joint types and axis directions couples attribute reconstruction to the motion it induces. An image-conditioned flow learns the resulting functional latents, while a multi-state-adapted Gaussian model supplies appearance. At inference, recovered part assignments and joints articulate a single set of rest-pose Gaussians without regenerating the object for each state. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and ACD show stronger part-box agreement, articulated-state geometry and visual similarity than the compared baselines, while joint prediction reduces axis, origin and range errors relative to ArtiLatent. Controlled ablations support the joint-line encoding and show that motion supervision reduces anchor-motion error. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be released in the future.

papers.title: Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
papers.abstract: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2θ_{23}$, $Δm^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $δ_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

papers.title: Non-Induced Representations in Characteristic Zero
papers.abstract: This paper explores the failure of induction from all proper subgroups to generate the full representation ring, measured by a quotient group $Q_k(G)$. We extend existing results for cyclic groups to all finite abelian groups and calculate this quotient for all finite groups over fields of characteristic 0 by reducing to the abelian case. We briefly discuss extensions to positive characteristics via modular representation theory. Finally, we detail our result for certain well-known families of groups.

papers.title: Spike-Aware Gradient-Based Mixed-Precision Quantization of Spiking Neural Networks for Vision Applications
papers.abstract: In recent years, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have gained massive attention as an energy-efficient neural computing paradigm due to their event-driven and sparse computing capability. However, maintaining accuracy under low-precision constraints, necessary for practical deployment, has been largely unexplored for SNN models. In addition, existing Hessian-based approaches for quantization, such as HAWQ-V2, incur significant memory and computational overhead due to temporal unrolling across multiple SNN timesteps. We propose a spike-aware gradient-based mixed-precision quantization framework for SNNs that adaptively assigns bit-widths using first-order gradient information, avoiding costly second-order Hessian computations. We evaluate our method across various SNN-based architectures, including VGG, ResNet, and Vision Transformer models obtained from both ANN-to-SNN conversion and direct training frameworks, on CIFAR10/100, ImageNet, and DVS-CIFAR-10 datasets. Notably, on ResNet-34 evaluated on ImageNet, our method achieves 73.30% accuracy at 4.78$\times$ compression, which is comparable to that provided by HAWQ-V2, while reducing memory consumption by 2.31$\times$ and bit-allocation runtime by 100$\times$. We also present an energy analysis for mixed-precision SNNs showing that the proposed quantization strategy enables energy-efficient deployment without compromising performance.

papers.title: Foundation4D: Towards a unified perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles
papers.abstract: We introduce Foundation4D, a unified feed-forward model for geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera driving video. A shared backbone uses factorized spatiotemporal attention to efficiently combine observations across cameras and time. Our video inference pipeline uses pose graph optimization to refine camera trajectories and assembles object tracks across input windows. We also develop a data annotation pipeline and release PAI-Foundation4D, a benchmark with dense depth and semantic occupancy labels for 1,253 driving clips. With benchmark-specific fine-tuning, Foundation4D achieves the lowest depth AbsRel on Waymo and nuScenes, the highest detection mAP on nuScenes, and the highest occupancy mIoU on OpenOccupancy among the compared methods. Our task-combination study shows benefits for both detection and geometry: co-training detection with geometry and occupancy improves top-class mAP by 1.2 points over detection-only training, while co-training geometry with detection reduces camera-to-rig translation error by $13.4\%$ relative to geometry-only training. We further use the predicted geometry and trajectories as priors for lidarless NuRec, supporting reconstruction of driving scenes for simulation.

papers.title: Higgs Fluctuation Solver in Four Dimensions: Part I-A Matrix-Free Global-Scalar Bounce and Determinant-Renormalization Audit
papers.abstract: We report a matrix-free numerical pipeline for semiclassical false-vacuum decay in a four-component global-O(4) scalar theory in four Euclidean dimensions. The calculation combines continuum bounce shooting, action relaxation, channel-resolved fluctuation spectra, deflated stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ), and a continuum partial-wave determinant with Gel'fand-Yaglom radial ratios and large-angular-momentum subtraction. For the benchmark potential, the bounce action is B = 145.203947 and the tail residual is 0.281955%. On an L = 26, h = 0.8 lattice, the relaxed field achieves an RMS EOM residual of 4.43 x 10^-12; its low spectrum contains one negative radial mode, four lattice translations, and three near-zero internal modes. The 16-probe bare SLQ trace-log is -2079.9042 +/- 6.4504. Under the subtraction prescription, the scalar partial-wave calculation returns a primed trace-log of 40.9324 at mu = mF = sqrt(0.4), giving a determinant factor of 1.2931 x 10^-9. We show the leading rho^8 potential is not closed under its scalar one-loop divergence: local rho^10 and rho^12 counterterms are required, leaving finite coefficients unmatched; hence this is a prescription-level result, not a complete EFT prediction. The translation-normalized scalar expression is 5.9974 x 10^-70 in lattice energy units to the fourth power, omitting the internal-orientation Jacobian. We summarize tested SU(2) operator and pole-algebra infrastructure, identifying finite full-gauge matching and controlled limits as open work.

papers.title: Before the Ticket: Grounding HPC User Support in Documentation and Resolved Tickets with an Agentic LLM Assistant
papers.abstract: Most questions that reach an HPC help desk have already been answered in the center's user guides or in a ticket someone else filed last semester; users still file new tickets because the guides are hard to navigate and the ticket history is not theirs to search. We present an assistant that answers from both sources: an orchestrator calls two tools over the Model Context Protocol, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the live documentation and a Llama-3-8B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on 11,244 query-resolution pairs mined from historical tickets, and merges their answers. Every model runs on-premises or on the university's hosted LLM service because ticket data may not leave the institution. On 400 held-out tickets from Purdue's Rosen Center for Advanced Computing, disjoint from training and free of near-duplicates, and evaluated by two judges from model families that generated none of the answers, fine-tuning on resolutions rewritten into self-service guidance is the clear winner in agreement with RCAC's resolutions (BERTScore F1 improves from 0.06 to 0.27 over the base model) and is judged most correct on average. The end-to-end system does not improve on its tools, although they are complementary: choosing the better answer per question would exceed either tool (judged correctness 3.41 versus 3.20, an oracle bound), while the merge follows the documentation tool in 78% of answers. Returning one tool's answer instead recovers the fine-tuned tool's quality (3.19 versus 2.66), but neither a learned selector nor an LLM verifier beats that tool alone.

papers.title: A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underlineα$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underlineα$-stable Lévy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.

papers.title: A novel mechanism for spontaneous ExB shear layer formation in scrape-off-layer plasmas
papers.abstract: We present a novel mechanism for spontaneous shear-flow generation in the scrape-off layer (SOL) of magnetically confined plasmas, arising at abrupt changes in the sheath connection length $L_\parallel$. Such transitions occur naturally in the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator. Applying a critical balance treatment for interchange turbulence, we find that $L_\parallel$ sets the equilibrium pressure gradient and hence the radial electric field away from the transition, producing an $E\times B$ shear around the transition comparable to the turbulence growth rate. High-fidelity simulations are shown to be consistent with the theoretical prediction.

papers.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining
papers.abstract: Training Arabic large language models faces challenges from noisy web data, dialectal variation, and the high cost of continual pretraining (CPT). We introduce AQL-Lite (AQL: Arabic Quality Language), a time- and resource-efficient framework for adapting a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). AQL-Lite couples a quality-first curation pipeline (structural cleaning, heuristic and model-based filtering, MSA selection, and deduplication) with a partial-parameter CPT recipe that trains RS-LoRA adapters across the network together with the last eight transformer blocks and the embedding matrix, under layer-wise learning rates. At a matched 1B-token budget, CPT on AQL-curated data raises a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over CPT on raw web text, which yields no gain over the base model. In a controlled 5B-token comparison, AQL-Lite recovers 94% of the gain of full-parameter CPT (mean 73.19 vs. 73.58) in 52% of the wall-clock time and outperforms adapter-only baselines on every benchmark, and a component ablation shows that adapters, unfrozen blocks, and embedding training each contribute. Scaled to 40B MSA tokens and instruction-tuned on one million examples, the resulting 12B model scores 75.3 on the seven-benchmark Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2 (OALL v2) suite. These results suggest that partial-parameter CPT on a carefully curated corpus is a practical route to efficient MSA adaptation.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
papers.abstract: Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.

papers.title: Optical and near-infrared s-process abundance scales in the Galactic disc
papers.abstract: A discrepancy has recently emerged between optical and near-infrared (NIR) s-process abundance scales, particularly for Neodymium (Nd). We investigated this issue using a direct cross-match between the optical Gaia-ESO Survey (DR5) and NIR SDSS-V/MWM (DR19). While atmospheric parameters and Cerium (Ce) abundances exhibit robust 1:1 correlations, Nd displays a systematic X-shaped vertical stretching. Our analysis reveals that the SDSS-V pipeline expands intrinsic Nd variations by a scaling factor of 5.54 relative to the stable optical baseline. This phenomenon is driven by baseline compression in the APOGEE H-band, where the growth of the molecular forest (CN and CO) at high metallicities depresses the local continuum. This forces the chi^2 minimisation engine in the NIR abundance determination to inflate derived abundances to reach mathematical convergence. We provide an empirical calibration framework to reconcile these disparate regimes. This correction effectively eliminates the contradictory negative radial [Nd/Fe] gradient of -0.052 dex/kpc reported in recent NIR surveys, bringing them into alignment with the rising trends established by the optical high-resolution Gaia-ESO survey. These results demonstrate that the observed scale expansion is a spectroscopic artefact of line-blanketing rather than a physical Galactic trend.

papers.title: FiLM-CAM: Keyed Feature Modulation for Conditional-Access Watermarking
papers.abstract: We propose FiLM-CAM; a conditional-access image watermarking approach that enforces authorized encoding, decoding, and removal through keyed feature modulation. A secret key conditions a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism that transforms the internal representation of the watermark signal before embedding, thereby coupling the payload to the key at the feature, rather than pixel level. The same key must be presented to condition the decoder to correctly recover the payload embedded in an image. To enforce conditional access, we train the system to maximize the performance gap between authorized and unauthorized use, ensuring reliable extraction under the correct key while inducing failure under incorrect keys. In addition, we design our encoder to estimate the watermark residual invariant to the presence of pre-existing watermarks. This design enables conditional watermark removal via simple re-encoding and subtraction of the residual using iterative refinement, contingent on knowledge of the secret key. We evaluate FiLM-CAM across multiple watermarking encoder-decoder backbones, demonstrating that keyed feature modulation serves as an effective, architecture-agnostic conditional access module (CAM) for image watermarking.

papers.title: Mirage: Targeted Jailbreaks Against Post-Generation Safety Checkers in Multimodal Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Post-generation safety checkers are widely employed in diffusion-model pipelines to prevent unsafe generated content from reaching users. In this paper, we show that these safety checkers can still be bypassed by our proposed multimodal jailbreak attack, Mirage. Given an adversarial target, which can be either a reference NSFW image or a malicious text description, Mirage conceals the target within an imperceptible perturbation applied to a benign input image. Mirage exploits the shared representation space of multimodal encoders to jointly align the perturbed image with the cross-modal adversarial target while repelling its representation from commonly filtered NSFW concepts. Such semantic separation can transfer across representation spaces, enabling Mirage to evade heterogeneous safety checkers without accessing their internal details. We further employ lightweight black-box query refinement to improve evasion near the unknown safety boundary. We implemented Mirage on Stable Diffusion 1.5, Stable Diffusion XL, and Kandinsky 2.2, and evaluated it on two cross-modal NSFW datasets, covering both text-to-image and image-to-image generation scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that Mirage achieves strong targeted jailbreak performance across diverse post-generation safety checkers with limited black-box queries while preserving high semantic alignment with the adversarial targets.

papers.title: Consistency Is Not Validity: Self-Rewarded Moral Argumentation Makes Language Models Decisive but Pliable
papers.abstract: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. We aim to improve performance on such tasks by rewarding good arguments, on the premise that arguing well increases the likelihood of judging well. We train a reinforcement learning policy initialized from a state-of-the-art language model in a self-judged tournament with masked thinking: the generated arguments are judged pairwise on argument quality by the policy itself. As an empirical basis, we extract authentic dilemmas from classic novels, using a logic solver to verify that each constitutes a conflict. We show that our judge rates argument quality like human annotators, and the policy then adopts the language register that it rewards. Testing on the external benchmarks MoralChoice, ELEPHANT, and MORABLES, we find that the policy becomes more decisive and invariant to the order in which options are presented, but sycophancy and reframing remain a challenge to validity. Two ablation studies with synthetic dilemmas and unmasked thinking match the reordering gains, but show a weaker register shift and higher sycophancy. We conclude that consistency is not validity: consistency under reordering can be optimized without improving the moral judgment it is meant to signal.

papers.title: Who Patches the Lightning Network? Evidence from Release Lines in Gossip, 2023-2026
papers.abstract: Every implementation of Bitcoin's Lightning payment network disclosed security vulnerabilities in 2026, and every advisory told operators to upgrade. Whether they do has never been measured, because Lightning gossip carries no software version. Matching the feature bits a node announces against the source of every LND, Core Lightning, Eclair and LDK release, we show that gossip reveals a node's release line after all. Where Core Lightning nodes state their version, the inferred line is exact for 132 of 136 node-line pairs. Across 814 daily snapshots of the public graph from 2023 to 2026, the network patches on release and platform schedules, not on disclosures. Half of LND nodes upgrade within 88 days of a release; small nodes and those that skipped releases lag far behind. The three largest upgrade waves came about a day after the Umbrel app store shipped a new LND version. Since June 2025, 17% of LND upgrades came in the 48 hours after a platform release, windows that cover 4.4% of the time. Disclosures, a median 256 days after the fix, moved few operators: of 12 we can test, only Core Lightning's of July 2026 sped up upgrades, and only among nodes one release line behind. Its later call to restart offline was followed mostly by nodes already patched. Two months after Lightning Labs' August 2026 batch, 71% of the LND nodes exposed at disclosure still ran an affected release. For maintainers, the lever on the nodes that lag is the platforms that package their releases.

papers.title: Route-and-Generate: KL-Regularized Router Improvement for Reasoning Routing in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models often apply complex reasoning indiscriminately, leading to overthinking on simple tasks and underthinking on harder ones. We present Route-and-Generate (Rouge), a hierarchical training framework that enables LLMs to adaptively decide when and how much reasoning is required for each input. Our approach decouples reasoning effort allocation from answer generation by introducing a routing policy that allocates a fixed sampling budget across multiple reasoning formats, while the base model is optimized with GRPO using per-sample rewards. To promote efficient reasoning, we employ a rank-based reward that favors shorter correct solutions, and update the routing policy via a closed-form KL-regularized policy improvement step distilled into a neural router. This design encourages concise answers on easy problems while reserving longer reasoning for harder ones, achieving improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across multiple reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
